entries.section: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

paragraphs.text: In the beginning: that is, the beginning of the creation of the world, and not eternity as is meant in (Jn 1:1). It is not a specific time, for there was no time then, but it announces the beginning of the world, which only God knows, who alone was present at that time, and God has not revealed it to man. Before it was eternity, and no creatures existed before that, whether heavenly or earthly. Created: this means that God is the Creator of the world out of nothing, and this is against the theory of the eternity of the world that some philosophers proclaim.

God: in the Hebrew language it came as "Elohim", that is, in the plural, and it means God, the Trinity of hypostases, although the word "created" came in Hebrew in the singular. The meaning of this is that the one God, the Trinity of hypostases, is the One who created the world. Heavens: this means everything that is above man, that is, the world of spirits with all the orders of angels and all the heavens with their different degrees.
The earth: this means the visible world, and it includes the dry land, the seas and all perceptible beings.
This verse declares that God alone is the Creator of the world and of all that is in it.

entries.section: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

paragraphs.text: Without form and void: in Hebrew, desolation and confusion, and in Greek in the Septuagint, invisible and unfinished. It means that obscurity and incompleteness surrounded the earth, and it was invisible because man had not yet been created. It does not mean that some being had caused confusion in it, but rather incompleteness and the absence of life in it, because God had not yet created the world in its known form, which He made for the life of man. The deep: that is, waters covering everything, so that no land could be seen in them, nor any planets or sun.
Darkness: this means a very thick fog that prevents sight, making everything vague and obscure.
The Spirit of God: the Holy Spirit, for it is a clear declaration of the Third Hypostasis.
Moved: that is, moved, and the Syriac word means "brooded", that is, hope is hung on the Spirit of God, who is able to give life out of this ruin and emptiness.

It declares to us that God created out of nothing, as we understand from (v. 1), the beginnings of the heavens and the earth, which are this water and the thick fog that covers the earth and all the planets, and the Spirit of God was brooding over this creation in which He would give life, in this water and the earth hidden within it.

entries.section: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

paragraphs.text: How did light precede the creation of the sun, which came on the fourth day?!

The light meant here is the creation of the cosmic galaxies, each of which carries millions of stars and hundreds of millions of planets, and every planet and every star and every galaxy is in a state of rotation about itself at a very high speed. This whole cosmic entity (the galaxies) and what lies between them was called light, and it is an entity of light that preceded the appearance of the sun that we know ... The greatest proof of the existence of light apart from the sun is that scientists are now able to see and identify the galaxies, which could not be seen if they were dark. As for the sun that we know, either it existed on the first day but in a gaseous, cosmic, foggy state and completed its maturity and appearance on the fourth day, or it was taken from the luminous mass on the fourth day. This accords with science and does not contradict it, and it is the opinion supported by His Holiness Pope Shenouda III in his book "Years with People's Questions", Part One, and by His Grace Anba Paula, Bishop of Gharbia, in his book "The Bible and Science."

entries.section: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

paragraphs.text: God declares His satisfaction with the light that He created by describing it as good, that is, it fulfilled the will of God, and this is an important first step before the creation of the other things for the sake of man.

He divided the light from the darkness: that is, there came to be an illuminated region, which is the region of the nebula and the cosmic galaxies, and another region, which is the darkness from which the created light came forth. In a spiritual contemplation, St. Augustine sees that this darkness means the fall of the angels who became demons, so God divided between the light and the darkness, that is, between the angels and the demons.

entries.section: (1) The first day (the creation of light)

paragraphs.text: God gave the light the name Day, while the darkness He called Night. This day is different from the day produced by the sun, which means specific hours, as it will begin on the fourth day, but a day with God is a period of time not known, which may include millions of years by the reckoning now known.

He declared the end of the day by the presence of an evening and then a morning following it, because the darkness existed first and then God created the light, although we are accustomed to the day beginning with the morning and then the evening, but some peoples, such as the Jews, begin the day with the evening and then the morning.
The evening is meant to be the dimness, that is, weak light, and not the night that occurs after sunset, because the sun had not yet been created. For God works in the morning and the daytime.
The mention of the evening and then the morning gives a good hope that every darkness is followed by light.

The Spirit of God who dwells in you, however confused or ruined or far from God you may be because of your preoccupations and your sins, is able to work in you and create a life of light within you. So submit to Him when He guides you to every spiritual work, and your life will change and you will find the salvation of your soul.

entries.section: (2) The second day: the creation of the heaven

paragraphs.text: The firmament: the earth was in a state of boiling, as scientists say, and then it calmed and its heat decreased in its outer crust, so the vapors surrounding it became cool. This envelope of air surrounding the earth is what is called the firmament, and the birds fly in it.

On the second day God created the air surrounding the globe of the earth, and it divides between waters below it, which are the waters of the seas and rivers, and other waters above it, which are the clouds that move, then condense and fall to the earth as rain, then the water evaporates from the earth to turn into clouds.

entries.section: (2) The second day: the creation of the heaven

paragraphs.text: God called this air heaven, and it is the first heaven, that is, the heaven of the birds and not the heaven of the planets. Then He declares the end of the day, which is a period of time whose length is not known, as we mentioned, and the evening came, that is, the dimness, and it was followed by a morning, the beginning of a new day.

It is not mentioned that God saw what He had made on the second day to be good, as with the other days, because it is connected with and completed by what He did on the third day, when He made the dry land appear in the midst of the seas, and then after His creating the plants, also on the third day, He said that what He had made was good for the second time.

The creation of the heaven declares the existence of that which is lofty and high above the earth, to draw your gaze from the passing earthly things to the abiding heavenly things. This heaven is the beginning of other heavens, the last and highest of which is the Kingdom, that is, the everlasting existence with God. So let your goal be to reach heaven, and whenever you lift your eyes to heaven, your heart is drawn to contemplate God and to strive to please Him, so that you may have constant enjoyment with Him in eternity.

entries.section: (3) The third day: the creation of the earth and the plants

paragraphs.text: The waters covered the whole earth, then cracks occurred in the earth's crust, and channels for the seas were formed, connected with one another, and the dry land appeared, raised above the seas and even bearing high mountains. Thus a place appeared where man could live, which is the dry land, while the seas he uses for traveling from one place to another on the land. He called the dry land earth and the gathering together of the waters seas, and this is a completion of what He did on the second day, and He saw that it was good, that is, He was pleased with it.

entries.section: (3) The third day: the creation of the earth and the plants

paragraphs.text: Grass: what is meant is the simple marine plants, which are the algae that appeared on the sides of the sea.
Herb: these are the plants of the various crops such as wheat and beans ... which give food to man and animals.

Yielding seed: it differs from the previous grasses, which are the algae, in that it forms seeds that fall into the earth and produce new plants of the same kind as the plant that produced these seeds.

Tree: these are all kinds of trees, small and large, that give fruit for the food of man and animals and produce seeds like the herbs, which can be planted to give the same kind of trees that produced them. Thus these plants do not perish when man or animals eat them, but their existence is renewed by means of the seeds. After the appearance of the earth, God created upon it the various plants to be food for man and the animals that serve him, and gave them the ability to multiply and continue by means of the seeds that they produce, and God saw that it was good. The repetition of the word good twice on the third day shows that the first is connected with what He did on the second day, as we mentioned.

entries.section: (3) The third day: the creation of the earth and the plants

paragraphs.text: God's work on the third day ends with the coming of the evening, which is followed by the morning of the fourth day.

God's love formed for you a place on which to settle, and He set bounds for the sea so that it would not overwhelm you and destroy you, then He gave you plants of many kinds to eat from as you wish. It is a love and care that surpass man's understanding, and God awaits you to settle in Him and be satisfied with His love. All these gifts are meant to draw your heart to Him and to let you see Him in them. When you walk on the earth you feel Him carrying you, and when you eat the plants you feel His hand feeding you, so you rejoice in His love and are eager to thank Him night and day.

entries.section: (4) The fourth day: the creation of the sun, the moon and the stars

paragraphs.text: Lights: these are the stars, the most important of which is the sun.
In the firmament of the heaven: what is meant by it is the heaven of the planets, and not the heaven of the birds, which was created previously on the second day.

Day and night: as a result of the earth's rotation around the sun, the day came to be with its two parts, day and night, and thus the time now known began on the fourth day, which is the day that comprises 24 hours. Signs: divine wonders in the rotation of the earth, the sun, the planets and the various stars in set courses.
Seasons: the time now known began.
Days: the plural of day, which includes the day and the night.
Years: the year, which includes the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.

On the fourth day God created and ordered the sun, the moon and the stars together with the earth and the rest of the planets, and by this He formed time with its different periods, whether over the course of the year with its four seasons or over the course of the day with its two parts, night and day.

entries.section: (4) The fourth day: the creation of the sun, the moon and the stars

paragraphs.text: What is meant by the sun, the moon and the stars is that they give light upon the earth, so they are for its service or the service of man.

entries.section: (4) The fourth day: the creation of the sun, the moon and the stars

paragraphs.text: The greater light: the sun.
To rule the day: to order and serve the day by shining upon the earth, announcing the hours of the day and providing the sight and the heat needed for man's work.
The lesser light: the moon.
To rule the night: to order the night and its hours and the lighting in it, together with the rest of the stars.

God created the sun, the moon and the stars to order the day and the night on the earth, so that the day would be suitable for man's work and the night for his rest, so that he regains his energy for work on the following day. The sun is a type of Christ, the Sun of righteousness, and the moon of the Church, because she receives her light, like the moon, by the reflection upon her of the light of the sun, that is, Christ. As for the stars, they are types of the saints, because they are exalted above earthly things and give light to the people after them until they complete their striving and reach heaven.

entries.section: (4) The fourth day: the creation of the sun, the moon and the stars

paragraphs.text: God created all these heavenly bodies in the heaven of the planets to order the day and the night. God was pleased with what He had made and testified that it was good, and thus the work of creation on the fourth day ended, and the evening came, followed by the morning of the fifth day.

Would that you make use of the divine order of day and night, working with energy in the day, using the time faithfully for doing good and showing your faithfulness to God and your love for those around you, while at night you grow quiet with yourself to pray to God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (5) The fifth day: the creation of the sea creatures and the birds

paragraphs.text: Creeping things: this includes all kinds of fish and sea creatures that live within the sea, such as the whale, or that creep to come out onto the land at times, such as the crocodile and the seal.
Living soul: it gives them movement, vitality and instincts, but it is not the human spirit. In the open firmament of heaven: that is, in the air surrounding the earth.

On the fifth day God created all kinds of sea creatures, so the sea was filled with them, and likewise He filled the air with birds that can walk on the earth and fly in the air, whether large or small birds, some of which incline to life on the earth, such as poultry, and some of which settle on trees, mountains and high places.

entries.section: (5) The fifth day: the creation of the sea creatures and the birds

paragraphs.text: Great whales: what is meant by them is the large sea creatures such as the whale, and most of these huge sea creatures have become extinct.
God created different kinds of sea creatures and likewise of birds.

entries.section: (5) The fifth day: the creation of the sea creatures and the birds

paragraphs.text: God gave the sea creatures and the birds the ability to multiply and reproduce, to preserve their kinds and to increase until they fill the sea, the air and the earth.

entries.section: (5) The fifth day: the creation of the sea creatures and the birds

paragraphs.text: The creation of the fifth day ended, and the evening came, followed by the morning of the sixth day.

The Christian is likened to the fish that can swim against the current, that is, does not submit to the evil thoughts of the world, and is also likened to the bird that tends to rise toward heaven. Would that you imitate these creatures in looking to God and holding fast to His commandments even if those around you reject them, and incline to prayer and the love of contemplating God.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: Living creatures: the higher animals that live on the earth, which are other than the sea creatures and the birds.
After his kind: that is, each kind of animal is different from the other, and God created of it a male and a female to produce animals of their same kind and species.
Cattle: the tame animals such as the livestock used in farming.
Creeping thing: all the four-footed animals that move along on the earth.
Beast of the earth: the animals that became predatory after the Fall.
On the sixth day God created all kinds of animals that live on the earth.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: After God created the animals, He was pleased with what He had made and declared that it was good.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: Let us make: He speaks here in the plural to declare His Holy Trinity, who carried out the creation of the whole world, and He mentions it here because this is the most important work, the creation of man.
Our image: the image of God, not in the body but in the spirit, by which man is distinguished from the rest of creatures, and which includes the mind and the emotion.
After our likeness: that is, the inclination to be like God and to imitate Him.
Let them have dominion: He means man, who will multiply, and will lead, manage and tend all the animals.

After the creation of the animals on the sixth day, God created the greatest being, who is man, and this means that He brought him into being out of nothing, and that he is not one who spontaneously evolved from lower animals. He created him distinguished from the rest of creatures by the presence of a spirit in him, so that he becomes in the image and likeness of God, and He also gave him to be a leader and to have dominion over all kinds of animals.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: He declares here that He created man male and female, and this is what He will explain in detail in (ch. 2).

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: God gave man the blessing to multiply, fill the earth and have dominion over all the animals, and this is God's plan and has no relation to man's fall. He could multiply without falling, and therefore the sexual relationship has no connection with sin, but is a relationship blessed by God for bearing fruit and filling the earth. He said "blessed them" because He means in Adam and Eve the whole human race.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: God gave the plants to be food for man, and afterward, after the Fall, He gave him to eat the herb like the animals (ch. 3:18), while as for the animals, He permitted him to eat them after the Flood (ch. 9:3). It is noted that He gave him the superior plants, which are the herb and the fruits of the trees, that is, the well-known crops of the field and the fruits of the orchard.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: As for the animals, God gave them the plants also to eat and live by, but the lower plants, which are the grasses that include the algae and the various weeds and some of the plants cultivated in the field.

entries.section: (6) The sixth day: the creation of the animals and man

paragraphs.text: After the creation of man God testifies that what He had made is very good, distinguishing him from the rest of the creatures of the world, because the goal of creation is man, so that the whole world might be at his service, and with this the sixth day ends. It is noted that if man was created on the sixth day, he was also renewed and redeemed on the sixth day, that is, on Great Friday and at the sixth hour, by the crucifixion of Christ.

The goal of your creation is that you imitate God and grow toward Him, and the whole world is under your feet, to use it to reach God. So do not become preoccupied with it at the expense of your goal, but seek God in everything you see of creatures and thank Him for all His gifts, and you will feel His fellowship on earth until you reach your permanent place with Him in the Kingdom. Adam and Eve in Paradise

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the seventh day

paragraphs.text: At the end of the sixth day God completed the creation of the world in its two parts, heaven and earth, and all the host of them, that is, the creatures in them, whether the angels in heaven or man and the animals on the earth. The angels, men and all creatures are God's soldiers, belonging to Him in His army and obeying His laws.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the seventh day

paragraphs.text: The seventh day: the Sabbath day.

God rested: He rested in the rest of His creation, that is, He was pleased and rejoiced in the creatures He had made. But this does not mean that He grew weary of creating or that He rested in the sense of not working, for He still works, as He said, "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work" (Jn 5:17). God completed the works of creation in the six days and rejoiced and was pleased with what He had made, and this is His rest.

entries.section: (1) The sanctification of the seventh day

paragraphs.text: God blessed this day and sanctified it, that is, He made it an opportunity for man for spiritual rest, so that he would set it apart for the worship of God and His service and for fulfilling His will by keeping His commandments. It is noted that the seventh day did not end with an evening and a morning, because it extends until now, for God rejoices in what He has made and in the submission of His children to Him. Many years later the Ten Commandments mentioned the Sabbath day, which is to be sanctified for the worship of God, but it was known before, from the beginning of creation. The Church until now still regards the Sabbath as special, so there is no absolute fasting on it and no prostrations (metanoias) are made on it, but the glory of Sunday surpassed the glory of the Sabbath through the Resurrection of Christ on it, after He died for mankind and redeemed it.

Take care of the Lord's Day every week, which is Sunday, so that you spend longer times with God in His worship and service, and you make those around you happy, and God rejoices in you and blesses you.

Here he repeats the details of some of the events of the creation of the heavens and the earth, mentioning details of what He created on the third day and showing that there was no rain on the third day, because it arose from the effect of the sun's rays on the seas, so that the water evaporated into clouds and afterward became rain; all this happened on the fourth day. Likewise there was no man to care for the plants, because he was created on the sixth day, and the plants had not yet been created.

God brought forth a mist from the earth, which is vapor or a flow of water, and made it water the plants He had created on the third day. This mist was either a means that God made for watering the plants on the third day, or it resulted from the effect of the sun's rays on the seas, which produced the clouds and the mist, because the sun was created immediately after the plants, on the fourth day.

Here he explains how man was created: he is from the red dust, and therefore was called "Adam", that is, red, so that he would always remember his origin, that he is from the dust. So although he is the head of all creation, he is to be humble before God and with all people, and he even learns from all creation.

Man is distinguished by the breath of God in him, which made him in His image and likeness. This breath gave him not only to move, breathe and do the works of the animals, but to be distinguished from them by the rational spirit, which is not found in any other creature.
Garden: a large walled garden, or a paradise, and its diminutive is a little garden.

God prepared for Adam a garden to live in and placed in it all the animals and plants, and he explains that its place was in the east and specifies that it was in Eden. It is not the present city of Aden, and the exact place of the garden of Eden is not known, and it is thought that it was in Iraq.

God planted in the garden trees with fruit pleasant to the sight and delicious to the taste; and He also planted in the midst of the garden the tree of life, which gives strength and vigor to man by eating of its fruit, and even gives him the ability to be incorruptible, that is, immortal, as is shown by what He says about it in (ch. 3:22), that if Adam continued to eat of it he would live forever. It is a type of Christ, the Bread of life, who gives us His Body and Blood on the altar in the New Testament. It is also a type of the Cross, which gave us redemption and life.

He also caused to grow the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, from which man was forbidden to eat. It was an ordinary tree and there was no sin in it, but the sin was in disobeying God by eating of it.

He explains that there was a river that watered the garden and divided into four branches. There are many opinions about the places of these rivers that are mentioned next, but no one can determine their place exactly, even if the names are similar, because these places may have been named after the names of the rivers mentioned in the Book of Genesis.
Pison: its meaning is overflowing, or flowing violently.
Bdellium: a kind of gum-bearing or medicinal tree, and some thought it a kind of pearl. Onyx: a kind of precious stone.
He called the first branch of this river Pison, and it compasses the land called Havilah, in which there are gold mines of a good kind, and in this land there are also bdellium and onyx.
The second branch is the river Gihon, and its meaning is bursting forth, and it compasses the land called Ethiopia (Cush).
Hiddekel: that is, the Tigris, and its meaning is lightness and swiftness, while the Euphrates means the abundant or the holy.

God in His love prepared for you a perfect paradise and distinguished you from the rest of creatures by the human spirit, so thank Him at all times for His gifts, and look at all creation, and it will speak to you of Him, for it is He who made it wonderful. And when you have dominion over the whole world and many praise you, do not forget that you were created from dust, so look at the earth from which you were taken, and bear the offenses of others, and do not despise anyone.

God created Adam from the dust (v. 7), then prepared the garden for him (v. 8) and put him in it, and made him a leader and responsible for the whole world, and asked him to care for all the plants and animals, tending the growth of the plants, the trees and their fruits, and guarding them from the animals so that they would not destroy them but only eat of them. Adam worked with joy because he worked with God and for Him and felt His presence with him. This shows the importance of work in the life of the children of God, and that it is a blessing and not a burden, but the distress of work appeared after the Fall, as is made clear by His saying, "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (ch. 3:19), that is, the feeling of weariness from work began after the Fall.

Take care to have good works in every place you go, and force yourself to work even if only a little, and you will feel confidence in yourself, benefit others, close the door against the wars of the demons, and be able to practice your worship and service with energy and competence and be an example to those around you.

God gave the plants and the fruits of the trees as food for man, and when He speaks to Adam He means Adam and Eve, that is, the whole human race. But God gave man a commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, to show His concern for man's freedom and as a test of his obedience and sonship to Him. For despite God's fatherhood and His boundless love toward man, He gave him the freedom to remain with Him and enjoy every grace, or to reject His word and eat of the tree He had forbidden. And as a warning of the gravity of disobeying God and being separated from Him, He told him that if he ate of the tree he would die.

Adam had known the meaning of death from the fall of the angels, who had been created before. The commandment is not a restriction of man's freedom but a proof of his love for God and a confirmation of his enjoying freedom beyond the rest of creatures. For what would be the benefit if there were no commandment? He would be compelled to do good as a natural law for him, like the animals, that is, not liable to error.

And God in His foreknowledge knows that man will fall into sin and will need redemption, and God accepted this great condescension because of His love for him, for He was not pleased with his destruction. This confirms two things:
1- The surpassing love of God for man.
2- God's insistence on man's enjoying freedom.

Adam looked at all the animals moving around him and found them male and female, and he felt the harmony among them and also rejoiced in their company, but they did not rise to the level of understanding with him and did not satisfy his needs. He received everything from God, whose fellowship he enjoyed, but he needed God to give him someone like himself to help him in his life and be in harmony with him, each giving his love to the other. Here God shows Adam's need of a woman to share his life, so that his joy might be complete.

God showed Adam's leadership over all creatures, the first of which were the animals, and asked him to name each animal by its name. This means the intelligence and surpassing wisdom that Adam enjoyed, so that he was able to understand the natures of the animals, distinguish between them, divide them into different kinds and name each animal with the name suitable for it. This includes all the animals, large and small, that move on the earth, that fly in the heaven, and that travel in the seas and waters. It is understood implicitly that he also called all the plants by their names after dividing them into different classes, which is what is now studied in the various universities, that is, the science of the classification of plants, animals and insects.
It is also understood implicitly that he called all the things on the earth, such as the mountains, hills, valleys, rivers...

Man is the head of creation and its leader in glorifying God and praising Him, and of course it is not right for him to become attached to it and be preoccupied with its beauty rather than with God, who gave it to him, as happened in the worship of idols, or as happens now in man's attachment to material things.

In order to create a female for Adam, God did not want to create her from the dust, so that she would not be an equal rival to him but a part of him, so that each would feel sympathy toward the other; he loves her because she is part of him, and she loves him because he is her origin and she was taken from him. So God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep and took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place, or in other words, the wound was healed in its place. God took a rib so that Eve would be from his side and be like him, and not from his head, so that she would be proud toward him, or from his foot, so that he would be proud toward her.

And Christ, the Second Adam, slept on the Cross, and the Church came forth from His side when He was pierced with the spear, and His blood flowed to redeem her and give her life, so that she might begin her new life with Him.

When Adam awoke from his sleep and saw Eve, he felt that she was from him when he noticed the traces of the rib taken from him, so he said of her that she was a part of his flesh and bones, and he called her woman, that is, the female of man, because she was taken out of man. This gave them feelings of oneness in the bond and completeness between them. This first marriage declares to mankind that every marriage God wanted to be a union between man and woman, so that neither lives without the other, and no differences in character or conduct separate them, but they strive for one life in which each completes the other.

Adam prophesied about the human race that every man will leave his father and his mother, between whom he was raised, and be united to the girl he has chosen, and the two shall be one flesh, that is, be united. This is what Christianity completed when it made marriage a holy sacrament in which the Holy Spirit descends to give the couple the ability for the marital union. This verse applies to Christ, who left His Father by the Incarnation without being separated from Him, but appeared in the form of humility, and left His mother, that is, the synagogue of the Jews, and was united to His Church through His Incarnation and redemption, that is, He raised the humanity that believes in Him to the level of union with Him through the Church.

Adam and Eve were in innocence before the Fall into sin, so they were not ashamed of their nakedness, but after the Fall they felt the shame of sin and needed clothing. Here God made for them coats of skins, which He obtained from the slaughter of an animal, and they are a type of redemption by the blood of Christ, which clothes them and frees them from the shame of sin.

Do not be preoccupied with clothes and outward appearances, for they entered the world to cover the shame of sin, but now that you are clothed with the garments of righteousness in Christ, you need only clothing, merely simple garments that cover you, because righteousness has clothed you first. So do not compare yourself with those around you and seek after passing material things, for you are the son of the King of kings and grace covers you, and indeed you are the greatest of His creatures.
The fall of man

Satan entered into the serpent, so it had more intelligence and wisdom than all the animals God had created. All the animals have no mind and no ability to speak, but the serpent, by the Satan who had entered it, was able to draw man into sin by evil wisdom. It appears that man noticed this wisdom and did not reject it but may even have admired it, so he accepted to talk with the serpent, although he lived with God in spiritual fullness and did not need another wisdom or intelligence from any other creature, and here is the beginning of the Fall, that is, accepting understanding apart from God and admiring worldly wisdom. It is noted that the serpent went to Eve and not to Adam because Eve is distinguished by emotion, so she could be won over to sin through her emotions; moreover, Eve is Adam's helper and companion, the creature nearest to him, and she could influence him, so although his mind might reject the words of the serpent, his relationship with his wife and his sympathy with her helped his fall into sin. The serpent's question to Eve provoked her against God and was false at the same time, for it said to her as if it were a question, but what was meant was to provoke her to become vexed with God, so it said, "Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?", in order to draw her into dialogue with it, so that it could win her over and make her fall into sin.

The woman denied the serpent's words and declared that God had not forbidden them to eat of all the trees of the garden, then she accepted dialogue with Satan dwelling in the serpent and said that God had forbidden them only to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil planted in the midst of the garden, and she fell into the sin of exaggeration, saying that God had said to them not to touch this tree nor its fruit, although God had not said this, and she declared the punishment for eating of the tree, which is death.

The evil of Satan dwelling in the serpent appeared when he ascribed falsehood to God and offered the woman a false comfort and a lying promise that they would not die if they ate of the tree. Yet the woman did not take heed and withdraw from this evil dialogue with the serpent.

Satan continued in his lie, ascribing cruelty and selfishness to God in depriving man of knowledge and greatness, for by his deceit he presented the knowledge of good and evil as something great that would make them equal to God, although they already knew the good, while evil is not an addition but a deprivation and the opposite of good, as darkness is the opposite of light. So Satan presented the knowledge of evil as something attractive and drew the woman's heart to it, and by accepting Satan's words the woman and Adam fell into pride, the pursuit of a strange knowledge apart from God, and submission to Satan's guidance, and these are some aspects of the first sin into which man fell.

By Satan's words desire was stirred in Eve's heart, so she saw the tree and its forbidden fruit as beautiful, appetizing and pleasing, although she had not seen it so before, and this was because she accepted dialogue with Satan. The woman yielded to his seduction, so she put out her hand and ate of the tree, and by this she was separated from God by disobedience and fell into evil. And when she fell, her feelings were defiled, so she wanted to make her husband fall into evil too, and she was no longer a helper to him but a means of making him fall into sin. As for Adam, he loved his wife more than God, so that he accepted her word and rejected God's commandment, and fell into sin.

The eyes of Adam and Eve were opened to evil and they lost their first purity, so they felt their nakedness and shame and tried to cover their shame with leaves. They took fig leaves and tried to join them to one another, that is, to sew them, to cover their nakedness, and of course these leaves would dry and fall off easily and would not cover them. These are human attempts to heal the shame of sin, which are of no avail, but God's tenderness would cover them with coats of skins, as we shall see in (v. 21).

Do not accept dialogue with Satan in the form of thoughts that disturb you to no purpose and even lead to your withdrawal from God, for these are the marks of Satan's thoughts, whereas God's thoughts are constructive and restful to the soul. And do not give Satan an opportunity through free time, to enter you through it, and keep away from stumbling media or conversation with bad friends, and occupy yourself with God and with every good work you choose for your benefit, and you will keep your purity at all times.

Although Adam had lost much of his understanding after the Fall, because of his close relationship with God he still knew the sound of His footsteps, and no one can know the sound of another's footsteps unless he has had a strong relationship with him for a long time, so this confirms the fellowship and the strong relationship between him and God. This time, unlike all the previous times, he did not hasten to meet God, whom he loved and always longed to see, but fled because of his sin, which had separated him from God, and in his great ignorance he hid among the trees, forgetting that God sees everything everywhere and that the trees do not hide anything from His sight.

And it says "in the cool of the day", that is, at the blowing of the wind of the day, which is a type of the Holy Spirit, for wind and spirit come as renderings of one word, so God draws near to man to fill him and satisfy him with His Holy Spirit. The voice means the Word of God, who calls man and seeks his salvation. When man sinned he did not go to God but sank into his shame and embarrassment, so the love of God appeared, who took the initiative toward him to seek his salvation, for the strong goes to the weak to support him (Rom 15:1), and sin is a weakness that pains and shames the one who commits it, so he keeps away from apology and needs someone to help him and raise him up in love from his sin.

Would that you feel the weakness of those who sin against you and forget yourself, your dignity and your love of possessions, so that you pray for them and even go to them in love to rebuke them, restore the relationship with them, forgive them for what they did and give up what they seized from you, to be like God your Father, who comes to you in His love to raise you from your falls and urge you to repentance, so you experience fellowship with Him and win all those around you.

God knows and sees Adam in his hiding place, but He calls him to invite him to repentance and to the confession of his sin, and had he done this, Christ would have become incarnate and redeemed him at that time.

Adam declared the reason for his fleeing from God, which was the shame of sin that he felt after the Fall, that is, his feeling of nakedness, and his answer shows his understanding that God knows his place but is calling him to repentance and confession, but unfortunately he did not do so because of his absorption in the feelings of sin, that is, fear and shame.

When you sin, do not sink into feelings of grief because of your fall, but know that God loves you and calls you to return to Him. So hasten to repentance and ask His help to make up for what you lost because of the fall and to resist the devil so that he flees from you.

When God saw man in his shame, unable to acknowledge his sin, He helped him and encouraged him to repent by asking him, "Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?" For the compassionate God not only accepts the repentance of the sinner but encourages him to it and is patient with him.

Unfortunately Adam did not confess his sin, but on the contrary ascribed the fault to Eve and justified himself, and by this he also ascribes the fault to God, because it was He who created Eve for him.
Likewise the woman did not confess her sin but ascribed the sin to the serpent that deceived her, and by this she also ascribes the fault to God, who created the serpent.
God first decreed the punishment of the serpent, and what is meant more is Satan, who worked in it, which is why Satan is called the old serpent, and the punishment was:
1- The divine curse, that is, the loss of every blessing and exposure to many troubles.
2- The loss of its beautiful appearance, for it appears that the serpent was upright at first, but when God cursed it, it came to crawl on its belly.

3- It came to cleave to the dust of the earth, which enters its mouth instead of food. It is a type of every wicked person who is bound to evil desires, so that his level declines and he returns to the dust from which he was taken, having lost the loftiness of the spirit that God gave him.

4- The existence of continual enmity between the serpent and man, so the snakes seek to bite man on his feet, which are near them because they crawl on the ground, while he treads on its head to crush it and kill it. The serpent, as we mentioned, is a type of Satan, who tries to bite man with his evil desires, but man by the grace of God is able to crush all his power and overcome him.
The seed of the woman who bruises the serpent's head is Christ, who crushes Satan and binds him on the Cross and frees His children who believe in Him from his grip and transfers them to Paradise.

As for the punishment of the woman, no mention of a curse came in it, because she, with Adam, is the image of God, so she is not cursed, and she would be redeemed by Christ in the fullness of time. This punishment included two things:

1- The pains of childbirth, that is, there is no life or existence for the woman's offspring except through pain. The pains of childbirth are found only in human beings, while the animals do not suffer pains during birth, so that the woman, throughout her generations, would remember her sin and repent and guard against the wars of the devil, for whenever she shares with God in creation and in giving life to a newborn, she remembers the death into which she fell because of her sin and repents.

2- The corruption of the relationship between man and woman, for Adam at first longed for her and she responded to him with longings of love, but after the Fall she longs for him with many emotions, while he inclines to lordship and domination. She longs for him to do her will and he dominates her to do his will, and by this they lost the spirit of oneness and love, which would return to them in Christ the Redeemer through the sacrament of marriage and the work of the Holy Spirit in them. Therefore the inclination of either party to dominate the other, whether the woman by her wiles or the man by his control, is a return to the state of sin and its evil results.

God created the earth for man and blessed it to give him fruit to eat, but when man fell the earth was cursed because of him and lost the blessing, so it no longer gave him rich fruit as it had before but dry plants whose leaves turned into thorns that hurt him.

It is noted that God did not curse Adam, because, as we said, he is His image, but He cursed the earth, so that when man finds that it does not give him the fruit he wants, this leads him to repentance and to seeking spiritual fruits instead of the fruits of the earth. It is noted that Adam's punishment was the following:
1- The cursing of the earth because of him, so that dry plants that hurt him spread in it, such as thorns and thistles. Thistles: a thorny plant whose fruit is rough.

It is noted that Christ bore the crown of thorns on His head, that is, the punishment of sin, and died on the Cross for the redemption of man, that he might enjoy happiness in the Paradise of bliss and the Kingdom of Heaven.

2- Toil in work, for it was no longer pleasant as it was before the Fall, but pain and weariness began, as He said, "In sorrow shalt thou eat of it" (v. 17), "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (v. 19), and this weariness and pain continue throughout man's life.
3- Man dies bodily and is laid in the dust, and his body even decays, for as he was created from the dust, he returns to the dust.

If you feel God's presence with you, you will do everything for Him and love work and reject laziness and rejoice in every work you do because you offer it to God, so you experience happiness on earth and then the joys of heaven.

After man was driven out of the garden, Adam felt hope in God's promise of salvation, which would come from the seed of the woman, so he called his wife "Eve", that is, the mother of all living, so that from her seed would come Christ the Living One, the Source of life, and give salvation to Adam and his sons who believe in Him.

God slaughtered an animal, took its skin and made from it coats, that is, garments, which He put on Adam and Eve, and He taught man the rite of slaughtering an animal and offering it to God, because man had not yet begun to eat meat or animals. The meaning of this is that God taught him how to offer the animal as a burnt offering to Him after seeing its blood shed, so that he might learn that without the shedding of blood God is not pleased with him, nor does it cover his shame, nor does He forgive his sins. Man's attempt to cover himself with fig leaves did not avail, because they would dry and fall off, but by God's work, by the shedding of the blood of the animal, which is a type of the blood of Christ, man obtained coats of skins that last with him.

Adam knew the good, but when he ate of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the knowledge of evil was added to him, and his nature became corrupt and inclined to doing evil. So God in His care wanted to protect him from continuing in evil and being immortal in it, lest he live separated from God and perish, so it was necessary to drive him out of the garden in which he had refused to live with God by eating of the tree, and lest he eat of the tree of life, which gives immortality, and so be immortal in evil.

Adam used to work in the garden, but after his expulsion he lived with his corrupt nature, inclined to earthly desires, so his direction became toward the earth from which he was taken and not toward God, who breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and he was a lover of bodily things, keeping away from spiritual things to a great extent.

After God clothed man with the coats of skins and taught him how to pray by offering burnt offerings, He drove him out of the garden and placed at its gate angels of the order of the Cherubim, which signifies divine justice, and in the hand of these angels was a flaming sword which turned every way, signifying the Word of God, which cuts off all evil from man. The fire declares that our God is a consuming fire who consumes every sin in man and purifies him, and thus man dies in the hope of salvation, and Christ, after His redemption, brings him in and returns him to Paradise, but with a new nature after clothing him with righteousness.

How beautiful is Your love for me, O God, that even while I am fallen You seek to return me to Your embrace and teach me the way of repentance and prayer and holding fast to Your redeeming blood, that I may be rid of all evil in me, and You establish Your fear before my eyes, that I may reject evil with Your help, longing for the pure life in Your hands.
We note that Adam is a type of Christ in the following:
1- Adam is the beginning of the human race, and Christ is the beginning of the new man after the human race became corrupt.
2- God cast a deep sleep upon Adam and then took a rib from him and made Eve, and Christ died on the Cross and there came out of His side blood and water, with which He acquired His Church.
3- Adam was united with Eve to become one flesh (Gen 2:24), and in Christ divinity and humanity were united, and likewise He is united with the souls of those who believe in Him.
4- Adam was the head of all creation, to govern it and order it to glorify God, and Christ reigns over all the believers to lead them in the praise of God.
5- Adam named the animals by their names, and Christ the Good Shepherd calls His sheep by their names. Abel and Cain

entries.section: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

paragraphs.text: Knew: what is meant is the bodily relationship, and this means that it is not merely a material relationship but is acquaintance, affection and love that lead to a bodily relationship.

After the sentence of death was passed on man, the bodily relationship began as an expression of love and for the begetting of offspring and the preservation of the kind. This relationship is not connected with sin but is a holy relationship that God placed in His plan when He created man, for He said to Adam and Eve after creating them, "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" (ch. 1:28). And when Eve conceived, she bore a son and called him Cain, because she rejoiced in the grace of God given to her, as she said, "I have gotten a man from the LORD", because God had promised that her seed would bruise the serpent's head, so Eve rejoiced at the beginning of the offspring who would crush Satan so that she would obtain salvation.

entries.section: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

paragraphs.text: Eve conceived and bore a second son, Abel, and it is implicitly understood that she bore daughters who are not mentioned, and they are the ones whom her sons married.

Abel worked as a keeper of sheep, which gave him quiet ways and an inclination to contemplation and prayer, while Cain worked in tilling the ground, so he was rougher and more occupied with material things. Abel is a type of those who love contemplation and prayer, while Cain is a type of those occupied with the works of the world and earthly pleasures.

entries.section: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

paragraphs.text: Cain offered some of the plants that he cultivated in the ground as an offering to God, and He did not accept it, while Abel his younger brother offered of the best of his sheep a sacrifice to God, and God was pleased with it and accepted it .. and there are differences between the two offerings:
1- Abel obeyed the word of God that He had taught his father Adam, to draw near to Him by offering animal sacrifices and burning them, while Cain did not care and offered some crops.
2- Abel offered of the best of his sheep (firstlings), while Cain offered some plants, not the best of them nor the firstfruits of his produce.

3- Abel believed that this animal sacrifice was a type of the sacrifice of Christ the Redeemer in the fullness of time, as he learned from his father Adam, and as is mentioned in the Epistle to the Hebrews, "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain" (Heb 11:3).

entries.section: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

paragraphs.text: When God rejected Cain's offering, he did not examine himself to repent and correct his mistakes in what he offered to God, but was angry in pride because his offering was rejected by God while his brother's offering was accepted. His fall into sin is expressed by "his countenance fell", that is, he did not think spiritually and heavenly, but was vexed with his brother instead of benefiting from him.

entries.section: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

paragraphs.text: When God saw Cain fallen into sin in his thought, He warned him to repent and called him to good conduct by lifting up his heart to God, because if he did not think well, sin would take control of him and turn from thought into deed. For it was still at the door of his heart, and by his will he could reject it, but if he was negligent, sin would rule over him, that is, he would fall into actual murder, because the sin of anger, if it increases, reaches murder; therefore Christ warned against anger when He mentioned His commandment, Thou shalt not kill, and commanded us not to be angry (Mt 5:21, 22).

God warns you in various ways to turn back from your sins, so do not neglect His warnings, and respond to His call to draw near to Him in prayer and to abide in His Church and her sacraments, so that Satan will not prevail against you.

Cain harbored evil against his brother Abel, so he pretended to talk normally with him and drew him out to the field, lest, if he tried to kill him at home, his parents or his sisters would stand before him. And when he found a suitable opportunity in the field, far from the eyes, he stretched out his hand and killed him, as he had seen the animals slaughtered and die. All this shows the hardness and roughness of Cain's heart.

God in His love went to Cain to call him to repentance, and asked him about his brother Abel, perhaps he would confess his sin. But he, impudently, answered God that he did not know where his brother was. By this he is a liar and even insolent toward God, blaming Him for His question by saying that he had not been charged with guarding his brother.

Since Cain refused to repent, God confronted him with his sin, that he had killed his brother, and that He does not keep silent about injustice, but that even if the wronged one has died, God demands his right, and the wrongdoer must bear his punishment for his wrong.

God pronounced His punishment on Cain by the curse, that is, the loss of blessing, and the earth he used to cultivate bears witness to his wrong to his brother, since his shed blood fell upon it, and therefore it would not give him blessing in its produce.
He added to the punishment, besides the loss of blessing, restlessness and wandering in the earth, and indeed from his restlessness he flees from place to place and never feels rest.

Cain felt the hideousness of his sin when the punishment was pronounced on him, and even declared his inability to bear this punishment, whether the loss of blessing or the restlessness leading to wandering, and he added also that he had become liable to death at the hand of whoever met him, and by these he means:
1- His parents and brothers.
2- Any persons in the world whom he had not seen before, since he had come to fear the unknown.
3- The fear of the animals attacking him and killing him.

Of God's mercy to Cain was His promise that whoever killed him would be punished sevenfold, and He did not promise him that he would not be killed, perhaps so that his restlessness would lead him to repentance, but unfortunately he did not repent. On the other hand, He gave him a divine sign that protects him from death and frightens whoever tries to kill him, and some say it was the sign of the Cross or some other sign that we do not know.
Cain departed from God and was separated from Him because of his sins and dwelt in the land of "Nod", which means wandering, and thus he lived in the punishment of sin all the days of his life.

If you suffer from the results of your sins, do not complain, but return to God in repentance and be confident that He will forgive you, then rise to make up for what you have lost with a deeper relationship of love with God and love for those around you.
He confirms here that the bodily relationship, as we mentioned, is acquaintance, understanding and love.
Cain's wife was his sister, for this was permitted, since there were no women except his sisters, and they are not mentioned, but their birth is implicitly understood.

And Cain begot his first son Enoch, which means disciplined or trained, for Cain, who was far from God, tries to bring up his children in a sound upbringing, but this is not possible so long as he has departed from God, so only the name remains for him, without the deed.

And since Cain felt wandering and flight from the presence of God (v. 14) because of his sin, he needed to settle down, so instead of returning to God in repentance to regain his peace, he tried to solve his problem in a material way, so he built a city and called it after the name of his son Enoch, pretending settledness and discipline, although he had lost all this because of his insistence on staying far from God.

He mentions the descendants of Cain: Enoch begot Irad, and the meaning of his name is city, to confirm the illusory settledness that he made for himself by building a city. And Irad begot a son whom he named Mehujael, that is, smitten of God, and this confirms his sense of guilt and God's anger against him. And Mehujael begot Methusael, which means a hero from God, for his heart turned to material power and to oppressing others, and claims that this is from God. Then Methusael begot Lamech, and the meaning of his name is strong, and he means the same meaning as Methusael, that is, material power.

If you fall into any sin, hasten to repentance and do not try to cover it with justifications and pretend the opposite, for all this is like the fig leaves that Adam made for himself, which are of no avail, but keep man away from God. And would that the names of your children have meanings that benefit them spiritually.
This is another proof of absorption in material things, and it is the first mention of a man marrying two wives.

Adah means beauty and Zillah means shadow, that is, he was immersed in preoccupation with material desires and their shadows. This is a natural result of being far from God, of not repenting, and of relying on human strength and material settledness and not on God.

Adah's first son was Jabal, who worked in tending sheep, so he was a nomad dwelling in tents, and his sons followed the same trade, which is shepherding. The meaning of his name is wanderer, and it is suitable for his trade, which is shepherding.
The second son of Adah she called Jubal, and its meaning is the player of musical instruments such as the harp and the pipe, and that was his work for which he became famous.

As for the second wife, Zillah, she bore a son whom she named Tubal-cain, and its meaning is copper, and he discovered the copper found on the surface of the earth and made from it musical instruments on which he played, and it was also used in various works. Then she bore a sister of his whom she named Naamah, and its meaning is beauty or beloved, because this was their chief preoccupation, that is, material beauty.
To my wounding: my breaking, for "shadakh" means to break.

Lamech stood before his two wives boasting in pride that he was strong and able to overcome any man who stood before him, and whoever tried to wound him or break him he would kill at once, and he wrote this sentence, with the following verse, in poetry, since he was boasting and singing of his material strength. Perhaps he used the sword that his son Tubal-cain invented from copper, and therefore some commentators call these two verses the song of the sword.

Going further in his pride, he says that if God had promised to avenge sevenfold whoever killed Cain, then whoever tried to kill Lamech, God would avenge him seventy and sevenfold, although God had not promised him anything, but his pride made him think this.

When Eve bore Cain, she thought he was the seed through whom the bruising of the serpent's head would be fulfilled, as God had promised. But unfortunately Cain turned away from God and killed his brother Abel and walked in the way of evil, so God gave Eve a son whom she named Seth, and its meaning is substitute or appointed, that is, he was a substitute for Cain, who turned away, and for righteous Abel, who died. Appointed, that is, God appointed him to be the head of the blessed offspring.

Seth lived with God, then begot a son whom he named Enos, and its meaning is man, and he lived like his father with God, praying and offering animal sacrifices, that is, burnt offerings, to please God, and by this the blessed offspring began to increase, and he took care to mention the name of God and to live with Him.

If you have lost something, whether of the material things of this world or the spiritual things, by your falling into sin, be confident that your merciful God, if you return to Him, is ready to compensate you for all you have lost, that you may thank Him and return to your strong spiritual life and enjoy fellowship with Him.
The generations of Adam

Methuselah: he is the man who lived longest on the earth, reaching the age of 969 years, but his life also ended in death, so what matters is not the length or shortness of life but life with God, as was testified of Enoch (v. 27).

Noah is the tenth from Adam, and the meaning of his name is rest or repose, and perhaps what is meant by the name is the rest that man enjoys after the Flood, evident in God's care and promises, in addition to Noah's rest throughout his life, since he found grace in the eyes of God. The Book mentions Noah's three sons, "Shem, Ham and Japheth", who became the heads of the tribes that were formed after the Flood and populated the earth.

You can find grace in the eyes of God like Noah if you hold fast to your faith however much those around you cast doubt on you, and you are also able, if you keep His commandments and try to apply them in your life, to feel His presence with you and to be distinguished by an inexpressible joy and happiness and to be saved from all dangers.
The life of Adam can be summarized as follows:
1- The creation of Adam from the dust and the breath of God (ch. 2:7).
2- God's commandment to him in the garden not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (ch. 2:16, 17).
3- Adam names the animals by their names and works in the garden (ch. 2:19).
4- God creates Eve from Adam's side (ch. 2:21).
5- The fall of Adam and Eve (ch. 3).
6- The expulsion of Adam and Eve from the garden (ch. 3:24).
7- The begetting of Cain and Abel and Cain's killing of Abel (ch. 4).
8- The begetting of Seth (ch. 4).
9- The death of Adam and his descendants (ch. 5). Noah's ark

entries.section: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

paragraphs.text: The sons of God: that is, the sons of Seth and Enos, who lived with God and bore His blessed name (ch. 4:26). The daughters of men: they are the descendants of Cain, and they were called so because they lived preoccupied with the flesh and the material concerns that belong to men.

People multiplied and increased, and the descendants of Seth lived with God, separated from the descendants of Cain, who were preoccupied with honor and possessions and abandoned the worship of God. The sons of Seth admired the material beauty of the daughters of Cain and married them, so good was mixed with evil and evil prevailed in all the world. Thus the sons of God did not keep their separation from evil; when they became negligent they lost their purity, and everyone was occupied with the desires of the world and departed from God.

Let your heart be praying for the whole world, and even seek the souls of all by every means, but beware of mixing with the evil of the wicked in their talk, their gatherings and their evil desires. Hold fast to the commandments of God and reject every evil however small, to please God in all your works.

entries.section: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

paragraphs.text: Shall not judge: My Spirit will not continue to reprove the wicked man forever, since He was reproving them through the conscience, but they reject its voice.
His straying: his departure from God and his absorption in evil desires.
He is flesh: he is a man who inclined to material desires.
His days shall be a hundred and twenty years: God gives him a last opportunity to repent, 120 years, which is the time of building the ark.

God was grieved by man's increasing evils and his refusal to repent, so He decided to destroy him because he rejected Him, but in His fatherly tenderness He gave him a last opportunity to repent, a long opportunity of 120 years, during which Noah would proclaim the destruction of the wicked if they did not repent.

entries.section: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

paragraphs.text: Tyrants: the sons of Cain, who sought honor, position and domination.

The giants: the sons born from the intermarriage of the sons of Seth with the daughters of Cain, who lived in evil and in seeking earthly glory and honor, so they had a name on the earth but were rejected by God. Evil and domination were not limited to the sons of Cain but spread in the whole world through the mixing of the sons of Seth with the sons of Cain, so all the offspring became wicked, and they all sought material power and not God.

entries.section: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

paragraphs.text: God noticed the spread of evil in the world and people's continuing in this evil every day and their constant refusal to repent, and for this the Holy Spirit portrays for us the extent of God's grief, because man did not fulfill His purpose, which is friendship with Him and walking in the way of righteousness.

entries.section: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

paragraphs.text: It repented him: a human expression that literally means "regret..", but what is meant here is a portrayal of the extent of the grief of God's heart.

God decided to destroy the wicked because man would not benefit from remaining on the earth but would increase in evil, so a greater punishment awaited him. So out of His mercy and justice He decided to end his life, and at the same time gave him a last opportunity to repent, that perhaps he might return to Him. Also He destroyed the beasts, although they had not sinned, but they were defiled by the evil of man for whose sake they were created; he did not thank God for these animals but on the contrary used them in his desires.

Note, beloved, how evil grieves God's heart and how your repentance and return rejoice Him, so be a source of making His heart glad, and do not let the enemy use you to hurt Him, lest you fall under the authority of His discipline.

entries.section: (3) The corruption of the earth and the destruction of man

paragraphs.text: It appears from these verses not only the spread of evil and corruption in the world, but also that every man had done evil and therefore he is responsible for corrupting himself, for God does not take anyone for the fault of another. Noah's boldness with God also appears, as He tells him of the decision to destroy the wicked world, because he was the only one, with his household, who believed in God, and he is the one who would carry the message of repentance for 120 years to the whole world by building the ark before them, that perhaps they would return to God and leave their sins and enter the ark with him.

Do not make light of the voice of God that calls you to repentance and to turning back from your sins, whether in the Holy Bible, in the Church or on the tongue of those around you, for God loves you and awaits your return. So offer repentance today and renew your covenant with Him, that you may regain your peace and gladden your heart.
Gopher: it is the wood of the cypress or camphor, trees whose wood is durable, does not rot, and whose height is great.
Rooms: stories, so the ark was to be of three stories, lower, middle and upper.
Pitch: it is the asphalt that is formed from petroleum residues.

God commanded Noah to make the ark, which is a large ship covered from above, and the ark consists of three stories that he makes from the durable gopher wood that does not rot, then he is to pitch it within and without with pitch to prevent water from seeping through the wood. The pitch signifies the importance of man's protecting himself from the entry of the thoughts of the world into him, so that he may enjoy the purity that appears outwardly in his conduct and inwardly in his thoughts and the intentions of his heart.

The dimensions of the ark are 300 cubits, that is, 135 meters, because the cubit is the cubit of a man, that is, 45 cm, and the breadth 50 cubits, that is, 22.5 meters, while the height is thirty cubits, that is, 13.5 meters. The length (300) is the product of (100 x 3), and the number 100 signifies the people of God, as He said in the parable of the lost sheep (a hundred sheep), while the three signifies the Holy Trinity, and the meaning is the people of God who believe in Him.

As for the breadth of fifty, it is like the fiftieth Jubilee year in which slaves are set free and those sentenced to death for having killed someone by mistake, and the day of Pentecost (the fiftieth) is also the day on which the Holy Spirit descended, so the number (50) signifies the forgiveness and love of God. As for the height, it is (30), like the elevation of Joseph to the throne of Egypt at the age of thirty, and the meaning is elevation to God, that is, hope in Him, and therefore the meaning of the dimensions is faith, love and hope.

He commanded him to make windows for the ark, which are to be in the upper story, since the ark has three stories, and they are to be a cubit from the roof of the ark. They are for seeing the heaven and the rains through them, and they signify man's looking to heaven, that is, being spiritual.

As for the door, it is to be in the side of the ark for man and animals to enter through it, and being in the side of the ark it signifies the pierced side of Christ, through which we find our salvation and redemption.

He declares the purpose of building the ark, which is to protect man and animals from perishing in the Flood that comes upon the world because of its evil, and everyone who believes in God enters the ark and is saved from destruction. Therefore the churches are built in the form of an ark, because in them we find our salvation, and there is no salvation outside the Church.

God's covenant with Noah is that He would keep him from destruction because of his faith. For a covenant is always between two parties, each fulfilling his duties: man's duty is faith and life with God, and God's responsibility is to keep man from destruction and give him life and happiness with Him.

Would that you enjoy covenants with God, for He is ready to give you His infinite love and keep you in all your ways if you remain faithful in carrying out your covenants, and if you fall short, He is long-suffering, so return to Him quickly.

He also commanded him to take two of every animal, that is, a male and a female of all animals of their different kinds, whether beasts, creeping things or birds ... etc., so that offspring might remain for them.
God also cared for the food of Noah and the animals, so He commanded him to gather of the plants enough for him and all who were with him, and Noah obeyed all God's commands.
The Flood

The greatest testimony to Noah is what God said of him here, that he was righteous, indeed the only one in his generation who believed in God and feared Him, so He commanded him to prepare to enter the ark, he, his wife, his three sons and their wives, to save them from destruction with the wicked.
Are you righteous in the eyes of God, that is, do you believe in Him and live with Him, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, confession and Holy Communion?
Do not be much preoccupied with people's praise, for it will not bring you into the Kingdom, but always examine your heart to be pure before God at all times.

In the previous chapter God commanded Noah to take into the ark a male and a female of all animals and birds (ch. 6:19, 20), in order to preserve all animals and birds for reproduction so that they would not perish. Here he mentions more details, commanding him to take seven pairs of the clean animals and birds and one pair of the unclean animals. This means that clean and unclean animals were known before the Law of Moses, and probably God had made them known to Adam, while the Law of Moses confirmed them and wrote them down. He took seven pairs of the clean animals and likewise of the birds so that he could offer sacrifices from them to God, for the clean animals alone are permitted for offering sacrifices, and also to eat of them, as God would permit him after he came out of the ark. He takes seven pairs of the birds because by their soaring in the air they signify loftiness and looking to heavenly things. As for the unclean animals and the birds of prey, of which man does not eat, God was content to take one pair of each, for His wisdom in preserving the balance of creation.
Every living substance: every living thing, whether man or animal.

God specified the period remaining until the beginning of the Flood, which was seven days, in which Noah would prepare himself and bring in the animals and all his needs and theirs, and God also specified the falling of the rain that would make the Flood as forty days. The number seven signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in preparing man to be saved from the evil of the world and for salvation in Christ, and it also signifies His work in the Church throughout the seven days of the week, which point to man's age and his life on earth. As for the number (40), it signifies the children of God who work by His Ten Commandments in the four corners of the world, for all the believers receive salvation in the ark, that is, in the Church, throughout their life on earth, and are saved from destruction with the wicked.
Noah was obedient to God with all exactness in all that He commanded him.

Noah was 480 years old when God commanded him to build the ark, and he continued 120 years building it, and thus preaching repentance to the whole world, but unfortunately no one believed. At the end of this period he was 600 years old, and he began to bring in the animals of their kinds and also the plants he would need as food for himself and the animals, and this procession moved quietly toward the ark for seven days, amid the mockery of the wicked and Noah's grief over their destruction and his last attempts to call them to repentance, until he had brought in all the animals and also his household.

What happened in the days of Noah happens today before your eyes when the Church calls you to repent and to enter into her so that you may find your salvation. If you make light of her words and persist in sin, God and all His saints look upon you with sorrow at your insistence on destroying your soul, so repent and cling to the Church and do not waste the rest of your life.
Remembered: this does not mean that God had forgotten Noah, but it shows His love and concern for him at this time.

A wind: wind and spirit in the original Hebrew are one word, so what is meant here is a wind and at the same time it is the power of the Holy Spirit of God that moved this air strongly so that the waters would abate. Assuaged: that is, the waters became calm because the falling of the rains and the bursting forth of the springs stopped, so they began to abate. Throughout the following hundred and fifty days the scene was terrifying, to declare the fear of God that destroyed the wicked and kept Noah and those with him righteous, far from sin. Then God showed His love for Noah and those with him by beginning the abating of the waters, so that the Flood, that is, God's wrath at the evil of mankind, would end. So He sent a strong wind to help evaporate the waters, either because of the heat of these winds or because these winds made cracks in the earth that helped the water seep into them. Thus the waters became calm and began to abate.

The Flood is a type of Baptism, in which the old man dies, that is, the nature inclined to evil, and the new man is born, that is, the nature inclined to good, just as the wicked died in the Flood and Noah was saved in the ark, which is a type of the Church of the New Testament, in which is the sacrament of Baptism. The wind that blew is a type of the Holy Spirit working in the sacrament of Baptism to give new life to everyone who is immersed in it.

After 150 days God stopped the falling of the rain and the coming out of water from the springs of the earth, so the waters became calm and began to evaporate into the air with the help of the wind and to seep into the earth, so they decreased and abated gradually.

After 37 days from the beginning of the abating of the waters, the top of a high mountain appeared, the mountain of "Ararat", that is, on the seventeenth day of the seventh month, because the lunar month is 30 days.
Some commentators say that this Mount Ararat is the one in Armenia.
The waters continued to abate gradually, and in the tenth month the tops of other mountains, lower than Mount Ararat, began to appear.

Would that the tribulations passing through the world do not disturb you but establish the fear of God in your heart, for He is your tender God who keeps you from all evil, but His wrath is fierce against the one who rejects the pure life, so this urges you to reject the evil that causes these problems, and be confident that God turns everything to your good and keeps you pure in His hands.

Forty days after the appearance of the mountain tops that appeared at the beginning of the tenth month, that is, on the eleventh day of the eleventh month of the six hundredth year of Noah's age, he wanted to find out how dry the earth was after the rains had stopped for five months and the waters had gradually abated, in addition to the ark's having rested on Mount Ararat for nearly four months. So he opened one of the windows of the ark and sent out a raven to fly and find out how dry the earth was, and he noticed the raven's going to and fro, that is, its going down to the earth and returning to the ark several times, since it found the remains of some stinking carcasses and ate of them, then returned to rest on top of the ark and went again to eat of these carcasses and returned several times.
The raven spiritually signifies the souls that are in the Church but love the evil world and its stinking desires and waver between life with God and life in sin.

Noah did not learn from the raven whether the earth had dried completely or not, so he sent out a gentle bird, the dove, which flew and wandered about and found no place to settle because of the presence of water, even if a little, on the earth, so it returned to Noah, who took it from the window and brought it inside the ark.
The dove signifies the pure soul that lives in the Church and finds no rest in the world defiled by sin.
