Noah waited seven days for the remaining water on the earth to dry, and sent out the dove a second time. It flew all day, and in the evening it returned to him with an olive leaf in its mouth. This means that it found some shrubs or plants that had begun to appear in the slightly higher places, so it was able to settle on these shrubs all day and even eat of them, and it returned in the evening with this green leaf to announce to Noah the return of life on the earth in the form of some small plants, and therefore the olive signifies peace on earth until now.

Noah waited another seven days for the water to dry completely from the earth, and sent out the dove again and kept waiting for it until the end of the day, and it did not return to him, so he knew that the water had almost dried up in most places of the earth.

This search took about two months, during which anxiety covered Noah and his heart longed to know how dry the earth was, and he continued searching, but in the end he could not come out until God commanded him to. Would that he had kept silent and let God teach him at the proper time, but this is human weakness, which wants to know the facts by itself and cannot except with God's help.

Rely on God, confident of His ordering of your life, for He who has kept you throughout your past life is able to order your life in the future, so ask Him for your needs, and if their fulfillment is delayed, do not be troubled, for He is always with you as long as you want Him.
The covering: the roof of the ark, which was made of wood or animal skins.

Noah's anxiety and search about the dryness of the earth continued, so he removed the covering of the ark to see the sky clearly and look upon the earth. This was in the six hundred and first year of his age, on the first day of the first month of it, and he found that the earth had dried in most places, and he went on observing the earth over the days until the twenty-seventh day of the second month of the six hundred and first year of his age, when he noticed that the earth was completely dry. Thus this search of his took about two months, as we mentioned.

The first thing Noah did after coming out of the ark was to build an altar and offer sacrifices of the clean animals and birds, and it is implicitly understood that he learned this from Adam and his forefathers. Thus Noah's feelings toward God appear in his thanking Him for saving him, his family and all the humanity that would come after him from destruction, with all the animals, and in his obedience in offering the sacrifices that God had commanded for being pleased with man, which are a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, by which He gives us new life in Him.

God your heavenly Father gives you much and cares for you all day, so the least you can do is to thank Him for His gifts, and you rejoice His heart, and your heart too is filled with joy from your feeling of God who is with you, keeps you and blesses you.

God rejoiced in Noah's sacrifices and was pleased with him, or with mankind in his person, and promised not to destroy all men again with a total destruction, finding an excuse for man in that he is liable to fall into evil from his youth, that is, since the expulsion of Adam from the garden. And if He destroyed the whole world once by a flood, it was to declare to mankind His hatred of evil so that they might live in goodness, but in His tenderness He is long-suffering toward them and will no longer destroy them by a flood or anything else with a total destruction, and He will not curse the earth, but it will be blessed, it and all creatures, for the sake of man who loves God and worships Him.

God declares the existence of natural changes through the year, which He permits in order to alert man to repent and return to Him. For every year there is a time for sowing and also a time for harvesting the crops, and there are also the seasons of the year in which the temperature of the air differs: in winter and its extension, spring, the air tends to be cold, while in summer and its extension, autumn, the air tends to be hot. These seasons suit man psychologically and physically, but he should not be alarmed by them, for they will not turn into a total destruction for him, and so God declares His love for man, that perhaps He may draw him to Himself. Thus the fear of God that man sees in the Flood mixes with His love that he sees in His promise not to destroy man again, and the two help man to leave sin and live with God.
God's covenant with Noah

God gave a blessing to Noah and his sons that they might multiply and bear sons and daughters with whom to fill the earth, as He blessed Adam of old with the same blessing (ch. 1:28), because Noah is the beginning of the new humanity after the Flood.

May you have spiritual fruits and virtues, and may you grow in the love of God and fill the earth around you with works of goodness, lifting up prayers and praises, so that every day you fulfill the purpose of your creation and truly become the head of creation and the light of the world.

Since man pleased God, He gave him authority over all the animals, for although many of them are bigger and stronger than man, he rules over them by his wisdom and God's guidance to him, and thus God confirms that man is the head of creation. Man's food until this time was the plants and the fruits of the trees, but God now permitted him to eat meat, animals and birds, whether those on the earth or in the sea and everything that flies in the heaven; that is, man was a vegetarian until the Flood, and therefore his life was long.
God warned mankind against drinking blood or eating flesh with its blood, and Christianity confirmed this at the Council of Jerusalem in the year 50 AD (Acts 15:29), for the following reasons:
1- Drinking blood excites the instincts.
2- Blood represents the life of animal and man, and God alone is the Giver of life, so not drinking blood is respect for the mystery of life and for God who gives it.

God also warns man against presuming, after slaughtering an animal, to slaughter or kill a man. He declares the importance of man's life in His sight and that He will punish the killer, whether an animal, as is stated in the Law of Moses (Ex 21:28-31), or a man, either by God's punishing him directly or by means of the civil laws that punish the killer, because man is the image of God, so his life is precious.
He confirms the same meaning of God's blessing mentioned in (v. 1).

God's fatherhood appears in His concern for man, who may live in fear of total destruction as happened in the Flood. So in order to give him reassurance, He made a covenant with him in the person of Noah, but it was given to his sons and all the humanity that would come from him and to all the animals that serve him. This covenant is a gift of love from one side, which is God, not tied to man's faithfulness and response to God, to show the love of God, His tenderness and His long-suffering, which remind man of the hideousness of sin and its punishment, that is, destruction, and how God holds it back from man to give him an opportunity to repent.
The covenant is not to destroy mankind by a flood again.

The sign of the covenant appears when the rains fall, so that man would not fear their increasing to the point of the world's destruction, God gives a sign in the heaven that appears in the clouds, which is what is known as the rainbow, that is, the refraction of the sun's rays on the water particles in the clouds, so the seven colors of the spectrum appear. And this covenant is still fulfilled until now whenever the rains fall heavily.
And as God's wrath was expressed through nature in the Flood, He also gave the sign of His love and care through nature in the rainbow.

The sign is a bow, for as man defends himself by using the bow and arrows, God defends His children and protects them from the punishment of their sins by the sign of the rainbow, to alert them to His love and call them to repentance so that they may obtain their salvation.

In the Book of Revelation God shows His love by the appearance of a rainbow around His heavenly throne, a sign of His love and care for His children (Rev 4:3, 10:1). In the New Testament God shows His love in bearing our sins on the Cross, then gives us the sign of His love perceptibly in the sacraments of the Church.

And when He says "I will remember my covenant", it does not mean that God had forgotten, but He expresses Himself in the way that men understand, and means to alert them to His constant mercies and His concern for them, so as to reassure them and keep them away from evil.

Contemplate God's mercies upon you in your past life, and if you can, write them down for yourself so that your heart may be at rest, and do not worry about the circumstances around you but thank Him and strive to cling to Him and give up your base desires. We note that Noah is a type of Christ in the following:
1- Noah found grace in the eyes of God because of his righteousness, and the Father called to Christ from heaven, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17).
2- Noah obeyed God and built the ark by which He saved those who believed in God, and Christ obeyed the Father and acquired His Church, by which He saves all who believe in Him.
3- The world rejected Noah's message of repentance and entering the ark, and the Jewish nation of Christ rejected His message and mocked Him and even crucified Him.

4- Noah and those with him were saved in the ark that floats on the waters and came out to a new life, and Christ saves those who believe in Him in the water of Baptism and begets them with a new birth.
5- Noah offered a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God after coming out of the ark, and Christ offers His Body and Blood as a sacrifice of thanksgiving (Eucharist) on the altar every day.

6- God promised Noah not to destroy the world by a flood again and gave him a sign, which is the rainbow, and God promises all who believe in His Son salvation and the Kingdom and has given them the sign, which is the Cross.
He mentions Noah's sons, who began to beget in the earth, and mentions the name of the son of one of them, Canaan the son of Ham, because of his part in the following event when Noah became drunk.

It appears that Noah, after coming out of the ark, was occupied with building dwellings for himself and his sons, and when the affairs of living were settled he began to work in farming, so he planted a vineyard.

Life became comfortable, so he sat drinking the fermented juice of the grapes inside his tent and was absorbed in the pleasure of drinking, so he drank much until he became drunk and lost consciousness and was uncovered, stripped of all his clothes. This conduct was extremely strange, because it concerns a saint who kept himself pure for 600 years despite the many wicked people around him who were absorbed in their desires, among them drunkenness, which leads to nakedness and to falling into various sins. But it appears that after he received the divine covenant and was at rest in all the matters of his life, he gave up his exactness and his vigilance against sin, so he allowed himself to be absorbed in pleasure until he became drunk, and the effects of the sin of drunkenness appeared, which is the shame that came upon him when he was uncovered.

Be exact throughout your life and do not be lax with evil, and when God keeps you from the wars of the demons, seize it as an opportunity for spiritual growth, and do not be lax with sin however small, lest you be stripped of the garments of your righteousness.

Ham, the son of Noah, passed by his father's tent and noticed his drunkenness and nakedness, and he did not cover him and shield him, but on the contrary mocked him and went to expose him before his brothers Shem and Japheth. It appears that Canaan shared with him in seeing Noah naked and in mocking him, and Canaan may have been the first to see his grandfather uncovered and told his father Ham, who came and saw him and shared in mocking and exposing him, and therefore the curse came afterward upon Canaan.

The conduct of Shem and Japheth was entirely balanced, for they did not lose their respect for their father because of his sin, but thought positively how to cover him. So they took a garment, probably in the form of a cloak, and went to the tent, and before they came near it they turned their backs to the door of the tent, put the garment on their backs and walked toward the door, and covered their father without seeing him in his nakedness, and they did not share in mocking their father, and they may even have rebuked Ham and Canaan for what they had done.

When Noah awoke from his wine and saw himself covered with the garment, he asked his sons and learned what they had done, and was vexed at the conduct of Canaan his grandson toward him. In the spirit of prophecy he punished Canaan, saying that he would be a servant to his brothers, that is, that his descendants would be enslaved to the descendants of his brothers, and he did not curse his father Ham because God had blessed him with his brothers (v. 1). This actually happened with the domination of the descendants of Shem and Japheth over the Canaanites, for the people of God under the leadership of Joshua entered the land of Canaan and dominated them. As for the descendants of Shem and Japheth, he prophesied blessing for them, and this actually happened, for the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob came from the descendants of Shem, and likewise the people of God and Moses and then Christ. He also blessed the descendants of Japheth, who are those who dwelt in the continent of Europe. The curse was upon Canaan only, the son of Ham, and not upon all the sons of Ham, such as Cush and Mizraim, who dwelt in Africa. And the descendants of Japheth, that is, the Europeans, dwelt in the East, Africa, the Americas and Australia, as Noah prophesied for them.
Noah lived long and completed 950 years, so he is the third man in length of life after Methuselah and Jared, but after that man's life became shorter.
The life of Noah can be summarized as follows:
1- Noah finds grace in the eyes of God among the wicked. (ch. 6)
2- God's command to him to build the ark. (ch. 6)
3- Building the ark and bringing in the animals and then his family. (ch. 6, 7)
4- The Flood (ch. 7)
5- The abating of the waters and the resting of the ark on Mount Ararat (ch. 8)
6- His sending out the raven and the dove and then his coming out of the ark. (ch. 8)
7- Building an altar and offering a sacrifice of thanksgiving. (ch. 8)
8- God's promise not to destroy the world again by a flood and His giving him the sign of the rainbow. (ch. 9)
9- His drunkenness and nakedness, his two sons' covering him, and his cursing of Canaan. (ch. 9)
10- The death of Noah and his descendants. (ch. 9, 10) The descendants of Noah
Abram: a name meaning exalted father or honored father.

God's call to Abram came first in Ur of the Chaldees, as we mentioned, but it was delayed because of the attachment of his father Terah to him, who preferred to stay in Haran for about 14 years. Then God renewed the call to Abram a second time, to go out from the place where he was living. This shows God's long-suffering and His love for Abram, the only man in the world who worshipped God, together with Sarai his wife and Lot his nephew, who was attached to him, while the rest of the world worshipped idols. So God made allowance for Abram, who was ashamed to oppose his father and deprived himself of dwelling with God in the new land for no short time; and when God repeated the call to him, he obeyed this time. This call includes the following:

1- From your country: that is, Ur of the Chaldees, or Haran, which lies to its north, so that he might keep away from the worship of idols. Spiritually it signifies leaving the perishable earthly attachments for the sake of God.

2- From your kindred and from your father's house: that is, all his relatives to whom he was attached emotionally, and who represented protection and reassurance to him, because they were bound to the worship of idols and his staying with them would hinder him from worshipping God.
3- To a land that I will show you: God did not specify a place for him to live in; it was enough for him to be with God in any place He chose for him, and this is reliance on God.

If you believe in God, do not fear the future or be troubled by any strange thing that comes upon you, but leave God to order your life as He sees fit, for He knows your good better than you do and chooses what is best for you.

4- I will make you a great nation: although Sarai was barren and Abram was 75 years old, God promised him not only offspring, but that his seed would become very numerous and be a great nation. In proportion to a person's obedience to God's commandments, which may seem hard, God gives him an indescribably great blessing and helps him to carry out His commandments, for God is rich and cannot be indebted to anyone.

5- I will bless you and make your name great: Abram would not be an ordinary person but one blessed by God in his health and his possessions, and everyone with him would enjoy his peace; indeed he would be great in the eyes of all around him. This is God's grace to His children who obey Him.

6- You shall be a blessing: not only would he be blessed by God, but a blessing to those around him, so that everyone who clings to him receives a blessing, as Christ promised His children that they would be the light of the world (Mt 5:14).

7- I will bless those who bless you: part of God's blessing to Abram is that everyone who treats him well, praises him and follows his example, God blesses, because Abram is the image of God among the Gentiles, that they may learn from him and God may bless them, just as every Christian is the image of God in the midst of society.

8- I will curse him who curses you: on the other hand, God promises wrath and vengeance on everyone who opposes or wrongs Abram, for He gives him awe in the eyes of all around him, so that they fear to wrong him lest divine wrath fall upon them, and thus the fear of him is in the hearts of all.

9- In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed: Abram becomes a blessing to the whole world, and this is fulfilled in Christ, who comes from his seed and gives salvation to the whole world, to everyone who believes in Him.

Abram obeyed God's word in spite of its difficulty. He left the fortified cities, his family and his loved ones to go to an unknown place and live among people he did not know, but he would enjoy God's presence with him, and this surpasses every pleasure in the world; it is paradise on earth. Abram took with him his wife Sarai and Lot his nephew, who loved his uncle and was attached to him, and he took his light belongings such as clothing and tents, and likewise his servants, and moved with God, who led him to the land of Canaan; so he crossed the river Euphrates to enter it.

Shechem: it is present-day Nablus, about 41 miles north of Jerusalem and five and a half miles southeast of Samaria. It is a valley, with Mount Ebal extending to its north and Mount Gerizim to its south. Jacob also lived in it and bought a piece of a field in it; Dinah, Jacob's daughter, sinned with Shechem the son of Hamor in it, and Reuben and Simeon, the sons of Jacob, killed the men of the tribe of Shechem; and Joseph was buried in it.
The terebinth (oak) of Moreh: a region with many large oak trees, and Moreh means teacher. It seems that a teacher used to sit in this place and people would come to him.

The Canaanites: they were distinguished by city life and the building of houses and cities, and they were wicked, immersed in many lusts. Abram arrived at a region called Shechem in the land of Canaan, stayed in it for a time, and then moved to another region called the oak of Moreh (maps 5, 6).

God appeared a third time to Abram when he reached the land of Canaan, and declared His promise to give him the land of Canaan in which he dwelt. Abram thanked God and expressed his thanks by building an altar to God there and offering thanksgiving sacrifices to Him. Thus the land of Canaan was blessed for the first time with prayer and worship offered to God instead of the worship of idols, and a sacrifice was offered to God that signifies Christ, who would come in the fullness of time to the land of Canaan to redeem all mankind.

Do not leave any place you pass through in your whole life without raising a prayer to God, so that the place is sanctified by prayer, you feel God's presence with you, and He also blesses those who are in it. And if you cannot stand to pray, then at least lift your heart to God, who sees you and rejoices in your prayers.
Bethel: it means the house of God, and it lies east of Jerusalem, midway between it and Nablus (Shechem); its old name was Luz.
Ai: it means a heap of ruins, and it lies east of Bethel.

Abram moved to Bethel and settled to its west, with the city of Ai lying to its east. Thus he moved from Shechem toward the south, and this declares that he was a stranger in the land, moving with his tent from place to place, and he was not influenced by the behavior of the wicked Canaanites around him; rather he cared for his relationship with God, so he built a new altar beside Bethel, offered sacrifices and raised prayers, and so sanctified this place also.

Abram continued his journeying with his tent toward the south of Palestine, and in every place he went to he pitched his tent and built an altar. These are the two clear marks in Abram's life throughout his days: the tent and the altar, that is, being a stranger to the world and loving God.

The land of Canaan depended largely on rain for agriculture, so it seems that the rains had diminished, the crops were affected and a famine occurred. Abram did not think of returning to Mesopotamia, his original country, because God had commanded him to leave it, but he thought of going to Egypt, known for its wealth and abundant crops because of the Nile River in it; yet he did not wait for guidance from God to go there. Here Abram's weakness appears, in that he could not bear the distress of hunger, although it is not said of it that it was a severe famine as the Scripture says of the days of Jacob (ch. 43:1) or of the days of Joseph (ch. 47:20), and despite his knowing that the Egyptians were sensual and wicked, since he feared that they would kill him and take from him his beautiful wife Sarah. That is, he went to evil by himself, and his heart was tormented when they took his wife from him.

Endure the afflictions that come upon you and ask for God's help, and He will support you. Do not be troubled and rush into actions that take you away from God, or rely on crooked ways to save yourself, lest you fall into many troubles.

Abram continued in his weakness. While he was traveling on his way to Egypt, with Sarai his wife, Lot his nephew and Lot's wife, and his servants, he feared the wicked Egyptians when they would see his beautiful wife Sarai, even though her age at that time was nearing seventy, or at least beyond sixty-five; but because of their immersion in lust they could take her from him and kill him. So he said to her, "Say you are my sister" so that they would not kill him. Although she was his sister from his father, that is, not his full sister (ch. 20:12), the error here is clear: he lies, because he wants to deny that she is his wife so that they would not kill him. This is not only the sin of lying but also selfishness, since he thought of preserving his own life and did not think of Sarai, whom the Egyptians would take and do with her as they pleased; and it is also the sin of giving up his manhood and chivalry, since he was ready for his wife to be taken from him and married to another, without showing zeal to protect her.

It appears here that Sarai's beauty was very great, so that all the Egyptians admired her, and the news reached the king's palace, and the princes, the counselors of Pharaoh, praised her, so they took her to his palace to join his wives.

Pharaoh admired her beauty and rejoiced in her as a wife for himself, and offered her brother Abram a large bridal gift, as is customary from any bridegroom toward the family of his bride; and because this was the king himself, he gave many animals to Abram, knowing that his work was herding.

When God saw Abram's inability to defend himself, and saw also his spiritual weakness, He made allowance for him out of His fatherhood, because Abram was the only man in the world who worshipped God. For the sake of his faith He covered for him and intervened by striking Pharaoh and all who were with him with severe diseases, and then informed him that this was because he had taken Abram's wife. This divine intervention was swift, before he touched Sarai, so that Abram would not be tormented all his life because of his weakness and negligence ... It is the divine tenderness that surpasses all understanding.

Pharaoh was greatly afraid of Abram's God, who had struck and rebuked him, and he respected Abram very much. So he hurried to summon him and reproached him for not making clear that Sarai was his wife, and asked him to take his wife and leave Egypt, because he was afraid of him on account of the power of his God.

Pharaoh did not take back the gifts he had given Abram as a bridal gift for Sarai, and took care to send his servants to see him off with great honor as he returned from Egypt to Canaan. Thus God spoke with Abram by means of Pharaoh, who sent him back to Canaan, where God had commanded him to live. Yet when Abram obeyed God in simplicity, God used to speak to him directly and not through people; but in any case it shows the love of God, who brings His children back to life with Him however much they fall on the way and go far from Him.
The separation of Lot from Abram
So he went up: because Canaan lies north of Egypt.
Abram and all who were with him returned from Egypt to the south of Canaan, where he had been living before he went to Egypt.

Although Abram had erred, God covered for him and rescued him and restored Sarai to him, and even made him ashamed by the abundance of Pharaoh's gifts, in addition to God's blessing first upon his flocks, so that he became very rich in the animals he owned, and he even had much silver and gold, because he believed in God and accepted to leave his family and kindred to dwell in the wilderness.

In proportion to your faith, your reliance on God and your obedience to His commandments, however difficult they may seem, He will bless you with spiritual and material blessings, until you are ashamed at the abundance of His love, and He confirms your faith and your obedience to Him increases.

Abram moved north in the land of Canaan, shifting his tent from place to place until he reached Bethel, where he had been living (map 6). Thus he returned to the same place. Although he had needlessly wasted a time of his life by going down to Egypt and being exposed to a hard trial, he benefited from it and learned that his life is settled only in the wilderness, that is, in detachment, and before God's altar, where he raises prayers and sacrifices and finds his rest.

Do not stay away from the altar and from partaking of the Holy Mysteries, for they are your life. On the altar you lay all your requests, so you receive your strength, rise from your sins, enjoy fellowship with God and keep your peace in the midst of the world's turmoil.

God blessed the sheep and possessions of Lot as He blessed the possessions of Abram, because he believed in God and accompanied his uncle on the path of faith, detachment and renunciation for God's sake.

Because of the abundance of livestock, the pastures and springs of water became less than their needs, and each party of herdsmen tried to seize the better pastures when they went out each day to graze together, so clashes and troubles occurred between them. At the same time the tribes of the Canaanites and the Perizzites lived around them, and their herdsmen also went out with their livestock to graze, so it was an ugly sight, namely the quarreling and strife of believers, that is, Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen, before the pagans who inhabited the land.

Abram intervened when he heard of these quarrels and disputes among the herdsmen, and spoke with Lot to stop them. He addressed him with all humility, saying to him, "We are brethren," although Abram was the elder and his uncle, and he gave him the right to choose the land and the better pastures. He said to him, let us live together but separate a little, so that each one has the opportunity to graze freely, and let us stop the troubles so as to keep our peace and our love.
Here appears the importance of the spiritual leader, the head of the family or the servant in keeping peace for those with him and in solving problems.

Care for your peace above every other concern, whatever the cost, and humble yourself before all, give up any material thing and bear the offenses of those around you, for by this peace of yours you can continue your spiritual life, live in joy and win the love of many, and consequently be able to influence them and draw them to God.
The plain of Jordan: that is, the Jordan plain or the Jordan valley beside the river.
Well watered: water is abundant in it, whether from the Jordan River or from the pools that were abundant there. Sodom and Gomorrah: two cities lying south of the Dead Sea.

Zoar: a small city at the edge of the Jordan valley, southeast of the Dead Sea; it will also be discussed in (ch. 19). It seems that Lot went up on a hill and began to look for the most fertile place, or through his wandering in the land of Canaan and what he heard from its inhabitants, he learned that the plain of Jordan was a fertile land in which pastures and water were abundant, resembling in its fertility and wealth the land of Egypt, and he even likens it to the garden in which Adam and Eve lived, because of its great fertility. This plain includes the country of Sodom and Gomorrah and other lands; so he rejoiced in it and chose it to live in. Here appears Lot's material outlook, which troubled him greatly: although he believed in God, the love of material things blinded his eyes, so that he chose wealth rather than nearness to his uncle Abram, the leader of the path of faith. He could have moved a little way off so that no quarrels would occur between the herdsmen, and at the same time stayed in a close relationship with him to be taught at his hands, but he preferred material things over the spiritual life with Abram.

Beware of the love of money, for it is the root of all evils, and use everything in the world in moderation, and do not be immersed in its lusts, so that you give your faith the chance to grow and your love toward God to increase, and so you find the salvation of your soul.

Abram remained in the wilderness of Canaan, where there is detachment and being a stranger to the world, while Lot dwelt in Sodom, where the land was fertile, although he knew that the people of Sodom were wicked. But he made light of it and lived among the wicked, so his heart was tormented every day by what he saw of their evils, and even he and his family were influenced by them. It is the love of money that blinds a person from seeing God, so that he is lenient with evil.

God appeared a fourth time to Abram because he had returned to the life of detachment in the wilderness and let God choose for him the place where he would live, whereas Lot chose for himself material wealth. Thus Abram, the detached one, enjoyed seeing God many times, and even received great promises from Him, for He said to him, "Arise, walk" in the four directions, to declare to him that all the land in which he lived He would give to him and to his seed. Abram believed this although he had not yet been given offspring. His walking in the four directions is in the likeness of the cross, through which we receive all spiritual good things. And God's saying that He gives the land to Abraham's seed forever means by it throughout life on the earth, if they live in the same faith as Abram; but when they abandoned the faith they lost the land, as happened in the captivity and when they refused to believe in Christ, so Jerusalem was destroyed.

God promised him abundant offspring, which He likened to the dust of the earth, which cannot be counted because of its multitude, and then He asked him to walk through the land, confident that it had become his possession by God's promise.
Mamre: the name of an Amorite man.

Hebron: its meaning is companionship or union, and it is a village 20 miles south of Jerusalem, whose place is now the city of Hebron (al-Khalil), named after Abraham, the friend of God; it was first called Kirjath-arba, after a man named Arba, one of the chiefs of the tribe of the Anakim.

Abram rejoiced in God's promise and continued the life of a stranger, so he moved his tents to a region with some oak trees called the oaks of Mamre, beside a village called Hebron, and there he practiced his spiritual life by building an altar on which he offered many sacrifices and prayers (map 6).

When you read the Holy Bible and see the many promises of God offered to you, hold fast to your prayers and your estrangement from the world, so that God's blessings to you increase and God appears in your life and you enjoy Him.
Abram rescues Lot and meets Melchizedek
Shinar: it lies in northern Iraq between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
Ellasar: it lies beside Shinar.
Elam: present-day Iran.
Goiim (nations): it lies northeast of Babylon (northern Iraq and southern Iran). Chedorlaomer: it means servant of Lagamar, who was one of the gods of the Elamites.

The power of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, emerged, and he defeated many kings and subjected their cities to himself, as far as the land of Palestine, and they paid him tribute for 12 years. But some of them rebelled against him and refused to pay the tribute, so he set out, allied with three kings who lived around him, namely the kings of Shinar, Ellasar and Goiim, on a punitive campaign to subdue these rebels.
Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim: four cities lying south and west of the Dead Sea.
Zoar (Bela): it lies east of the Dead Sea.

The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim united, and the king of Zoar joined them, and they rebelled against Chedorlaomer, refusing to pay him tribute. So he rose against them to fight them and subdue them to himself again, and they united together to fight him.
The Valley of Siddim: a plain beside the Dead Sea, which is called the Salt Sea or Lot's lake. It is called the Valley of Siddim because pits and fissures abound in the ground there.
The five kings mentioned in (v. 2), that is, the king of Sodom and those with him, went out to fight Chedorlaomer and those with him, and took their stand in a plain called the Valley of Siddim.
It was explained before in (v. 1). After Chedorlaomer had enslaved the kings of Sodom and those around it for 12 years, they rebelled against him in the thirteenth year.

Chedorlaomer prepared with an army united with the three kings who lived around him, and they came to fight the king of Sodom and those with him in the fourteenth year. When they drew near to Sodom, they fought some countries on their way to Sodom, countries lying east of the Dead Sea, namely the Rephaim, the Zuzim and the Emim, in order to subdue them to himself and to frighten the king of Sodom and those with him, so as to make sure they would not support the king of Sodom and that no king in the region would try to stand against him.
Then Chedorlaomer turned south toward the Horites who lived in Mount Seir, extending from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Dead Sea, and defeated them in the plain of Paran, northwest of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Then Chedorlaomer returned, heading north, and defeated the Amalekites and the Amorites west of the Dead Sea at En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and then at the strongholds of Hazazon-tamar, very near the western side of the Dead Sea.
Battle was joined between Chedorlaomer and the three kings with him, against the king of Sodom and the four kings with him.

Chedorlaomer defeated the five kings, that is, the king of Sodom and those with him, in the Valley of Siddim, which is full of fissures and pits, and in which there were also slime pits, which is mineral bitumen. So the armies of the king of Sodom and those with him fled, and many of them fell and perished in the slime pits, and the rest of the armies fled to the surrounding mountains.

When the armies of the king of Sodom and the armies united with him fled, the armies of Chedorlaomer entered and seized their country, took its inhabitants captive and plundered their spoils; and among the captives was Lot, who lived in their country.

Lot loved the fertile land and was content to live in Sodom, which was full of evil and enslaved to Chedorlaomer, so his heart was tormented by the evils he saw. And since he did not repent and move away from it, God allowed him a severe affliction, namely his being seized as a captive when his country was defeated before Chedorlaomer, and he gained nothing from the wealth and comfort but entered into the affliction of captivity. I wish, my brother, that you would not drift with the current of the world which pursues money, for it is bound up with evil and exposed to many afflictions that God allows for you, perhaps that you may repent; and if afflictions meet you, return quickly to the love of God and put away the love of money.

Some of the people of Sodom escaped, and one of them came to Abram to tell him that his nephew Lot had been taken captive with many of the prisoners, because of Chedorlaomer's victory over the five kings. Abram moved quickly and gathered from his servants 318 men trained for war, young men who were born in his house because their fathers were servants of his. This teaches us the strength of Abram, who had many servants who herded and guarded the livestock he owned, and he chose 318 of them for the war.

Abram was living beside the Amorites, among whose chiefs were the three brothers Mamre, Eshcol and Aner, and there was a peace treaty between Abram and them. When they learned what had happened to Abram's nephew, they showed their readiness to help him because of the treaty between them and him, and a considerable number of them went out with Abram, as appears from (v. 24). Some of the Fathers say that just as the 318 men of Abram's servants rescued Lot and all the captives, so the 318 bishops gathered at Nicaea rescued the Church from the heresy of Arius.

Abram himself went out with the fighters, although his age at that time was over eighty, but because of his detachment in the wilderness God filled his heart with zeal and love for the weak and needy, so he went out by God's power to rescue his nephew Lot and those with him.

Abram headed north to overtake the armies of Chedorlaomer, and reached them at Dan, which lies in the north of Palestine. He made ready and attacked them by night, dividing himself into two companies to surround them in his attack. He struck them a severe blow while they were asleep and defeated them, so they fled from him, and he pursued them to the city of Hobah, which lies near Damascus (the present capital of Syria).
Abram was able to rescue Lot and the captives with him and to recover the spoils that Chedorlaomer had taken, and he returned with them to his place.

In proportion as you detach yourself from material things and depend on God, you receive strength and your heart opens in love toward others, so you become influential on all around you and draw them by your life to Christ.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: The Valley of Shaveh: a deep plain lying north of Jerusalem at a distance of a quarter of a mile, and it is called the King's Valley because kings used to gather in it.

The news of Abram's victory over Chedorlaomer and those with him, and his bringing back of the captives and the spoils, reached them, and the kings who had been defeated rejoiced greatly. Their chief, the king of Sodom, went out to meet Abram returning from the region of Damascus, and met him north of Jerusalem in a plain called the Valley of Shaveh.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: Melchizedek also went out to meet Abram. He was king of Salem or Shalem, that is, Jerusalem, and was a priest at the same time. He offered a strange offering, not animal sacrifices as people were accustomed and as God had taught Adam; this offering was bread and wine, which is of course the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of Christ. He is therefore a clear type of Christ, for which the Jews are unable to offer an explanation.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: Melchizedek blessed Abram, who was returning after his victory, with a blessing from God Most High and not by the gods of the Gentiles, at a time when no one worshipped God except Abram, and all around him in the world were pagans. This confirms that he is a clear type of Christ, to whom Abram, the father of the Jewish people, submitted, from whom came the Aaronic priesthood, that is, the priesthood of the Jews. The meaning of this is that Melchizedek, that is, Christ, is the one who blesses the Jewish priesthood, that is, that the priesthood of Christ is higher than the Jewish priesthood, as the Epistle to the Hebrews makes clear (Heb 7).

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: Melchizedek made clear that the victor was God, by the hand of Abram; the cause of the power was not Abram but God working in him. So Abram rejoiced in this blessing and submitted to Melchizedek and gave him a tenth of the spoils he had brought after his victory over Chedorlaomer.
Melchizedek was a type of Christ, as appears in the following:
1- Melchizedek was king of Salem, that is, the city of peace, and Christ is the King of peace, indeed the King of kings.

2- Melchizedek was priest and king at the same time, and Christ is the Great High Priest who offered the sacrifice of Himself on the cross, and He is Priest and King at the same time like Melchizedek.

3- The Holy Bible mentions no father or mother or genealogy for Melchizedek, like Christ, who has no bodily father and also no mother with regard to His divinity, and who was born in the fullness of time but has existed from eternity.
4- Melchizedek offered a sacrifice of bread and wine, like the sacrifice of Christ in the New Testament, which is bread and wine and not animal sacrifices.
5- Melchizedek blessed Abram, the father of the people of God, and Christ blesses His people, the Christians who believe in Him.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: If Abram had defeated Chedorlaomer and those with him, he had the right to take the spoils and even the captives, but because the king of Sodom knew Abram's love and breadth of heart, he asked him to give him the captives and to be content with the spoils.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: A sandal strap: a shoelace.

Abram raised his heart in prayer to God, the source of his strength and blessing, and then said to the king of Sodom what he did not expect, for he said to him: take the captives and also all the spoils, and I will take nothing of it, even something small, so that all of Abram's wealth may be from God, and neither the king of Sodom nor any person may think that he was the cause of his riches.

It is to be noted here that this is the first time a person declares an oath, "I have raised my hand to the Lord, God Most High, the Possessor of heaven and earth," and the first time a priest is mentioned, and likewise the first mention of a war.

entries.section: (3) Melchizedek and the king of Sodom

paragraphs.text: Abram completed his speech to the king of Sodom, saying that he would take nothing of the spoils except what the men of war had eaten on the way from the spoils, so that they would not faint. And although Abram had given up all his rights, his partners in the war did not lose their rights, namely the chiefs of the Amorites, that is, Mamre and his brothers and the fighters with them. Here appear Abram's justice and his respect for the rights of others.
Trust in God's blessing for you, for in proportion as you give up, God blesses you and enriches you, so that you need no person, but you are a blessing to those around you and help every needy one.
See the map at the end of the book.
God's covenant with Abram and the divided sacrifices
Shield: a wooden piece covered with leather and having a handle through which the soldier puts his hand; the shield is used to ward off the arrows cast at him, protecting his face and body with it.

God appeared to Abram for the fifth time while he was inside his tent by night. It is clear from this that God appeared to him many times, so that he was called a friend of God, because he detached himself from the world, lived in the wilderness and devoted himself to knowing God, so God appeared to him often and they became friends. God's speech with him includes three matters:

1- Do not be afraid: of Chedorlaomer and all who are with him, should they try to fight you, for I am with you. And do not be afraid either of the tribes around you or of anything that comes upon your life.

2- I am your shield: God offers Himself as protection for Abraham, like the shield with which a soldier protects himself. And as the shield moves to protect the soldier, whether his head or his body, how much more God, who surrounds Abram and protects him with complete protection.

3- Your reward shall be exceedingly great: if you, Abram, have given up the spoils that you took from Chedorlaomer, then in proportion to your self-restraint I give you a blessing that no mind can imagine, namely that your seed will be like the stars of heaven and you will be a blessing to the whole world through Christ, who comes from your seed.

Always remember your strong and loving God, who protects you and keeps you in all your steps, so do not be troubled by the changes of the world or the threats of the wicked or the unknown future. Always remember, and repeat every day, God's word to Abram, "I am your shield."

Abram rejoiced at God's appearing to him, and with the boldness of love and friendship he asked Him about the details of the great reward, since he was not content with possessions but reminded Him of His promise to give him offspring, although up to now he had no son, but if he died his closest servant, the chief of his servants, Eliezer of Damascus, who was born in his house because his father and mother were his servants, would inherit him.
God declared to Abram that He would give him offspring from his wife Sarah, and that none of his servants would inherit him.

To confirm God's promise, He brought Abram out of the tent by night and said to him, look toward the stars of heaven and try to count them. They are of course very many and cannot be numbered; so shall your seed be, as numerous as the stars, and it cannot be counted.

Here appears Abraham's great faith in God. Although the word surpasses reason, since he is an old man and God promises him offspring that cannot be counted, he believed, and this became a proof of his righteousness and goodness.
God repeated His promise to him to give him the land of Canaan as an inheritance for him and his seed, as He had told him when He brought him out of his city Ur of the Chaldees.

Abram's question was not doubt but a request for a sign, for he did not say how but whereby, just as the Lady the Virgin asked the angel Gabriel about her giving birth to Christ while she wished to remain a virgin, and he informed her that the birth is from the Holy Spirit and not from a man.

Have boldness before God and ask Him for what you wish, so that He may confirm your faith and support you, for He is your Father who loves you. And if any doubt about God's word fights against you, repeat any psalm or prayer so that you may stand firm in your faith.

People in that time were accustomed to make their covenants by slaughtering an animal, cutting it in two and placing the halves on the two sides, with the covenanting parties passing between them as a proof of confirming the covenant. This is a type of the blood of Christ, which confirms the covenant between us and God, and which we partake of in the New Testament as true Body and Blood. So God asked Abram to make a covenant with Him in the same manner that people made in his time, and asked him to bring a heifer three years old, a female goat also three years old, and likewise a ram of the same age, and to cut the three, each into two halves, and place each half opposite the other, leaving a space between them for him and God to pass between. God also asked him to slaughter a turtledove and a pigeon without dividing them, and perhaps he placed them one opposite the other on the two sides.

Their being three years old is a symbol of the Holy Trinity. The animals signify souls that incline to animal desires, and the birds signify souls that incline to heavenly things; and the dividing of the animals signifies the divisions and factions that occur among those who incline to desires and the world, whereas among the spiritual no divisions occur.

Abram slaughtered the sacrifices, divided them and placed them from the morning, waiting for God to appear in the form He saw fit so that He might pass with him between the divided sacrifices. The birds of prey drew near trying to eat these sacrifices, so Abram sat beside them, watchful, and drove them away.
The birds of prey signify the evil thoughts that attack a person and that he cannot prevent, but he can drive them away by prayer and by asking God's help.

Abram waited all day for God to appear until the sun went down. Then he fell into a deep sleep and felt in his sleep a great fear and darkness, that is, obscurity, because he did not know what God would say to him and how He would appear and make the covenant with him. This shows the fear of God that was in his heart in spite of his enjoying friendship and boldness with Him.

God spoke with Abram and informed him of the future of his seed: that they would go to a foreign country and the people of that country would enslave them for 400 years. God did not mention the name of the country, which is Egypt, so that they would not be afraid to go there.

God promises to judge this nation, that is, Egypt, which enslaves the seed of Abraham, and this is what happened in the ten plagues and the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea. He also promised him that his seed would take great possessions, which are the jewelry and clothing that they borrowed from the Egyptians, who gave them in abundance and let them go out quickly with them so that God's wrath upon them might stop.
God informed Abraham that he would die before these afflictions came upon his seed, and that he would die in a good old age, that is, in peace, after a blessed life and a pure life with God.

God also promised that the seed of Abraham would return to the land of Canaan in the fourth generation, that is, after four centuries, where they would destroy the inhabitants of the land of Canaan and take possession of their lands. The reason for delaying the possession of the land of Canaan by Abram's seed for 400 years was to give the Amorites an opportunity to repent; and if they did not repent, their iniquity would be complete and they would exhaust all their opportunities for repentance, so God would destroy them by the hand of Joshua and those after him.

After God finished speaking with Abram about the future of his seed, the sun had completely set and darkness covered the earth. Then there appeared a pillar of fire surrounded by smoke, which passed between the divided sacrifices, and this was a divine appearance, because our God is a consuming fire who rejects all evil, and He is strong and able to fulfil His covenant and crush everyone who resists Abram. God alone passed between the divided sacrifices and did not take Abram with Him, because man is liable to error and to going back on the covenant, so God alone made the covenant to confirm its effect and fulfilment.

This is the rest of God's word to Abram, for He promised him that his seed would possess the lands from the river Euphrates to the river of Egypt, which is a seasonal river that fills with rainwater and floods and lies in Sinai.
God mentioned the peoples who live in the land that the seed of Abraham would possess, and they are:
1- The Kenites: they lived in the land of Midian, east of Sinai.
2- The Kenizzites: the meaning is hunters, and they are among the Canaanite tribes.
3- The Kadmonites: their meaning is the ancients.
4- The Hittites: the sons of Heth the son of Canaan, who lived in the south of the land of Canaan.
5- The Perizzites: that is, the villagers, who lived in scattered places in the land of Canaan.
6- The Rephaim: that is, the giants, who lived first east of the Jordan and then were driven out and lived in western Palestine.
7- The Amorites: that is, the mountain dwellers because they lived in the mountains.
8- The Canaanites: named after Canaan the son of Ham, and they lived in the cities throughout the land of Canaan.
9- The Girgashites: they lived east of the Sea of Galilee in the north of Palestine.
10- The Jebusites: they lived in Jerusalem and around it.

God's blessing is great for His children, but if the matter requires, He allows them afflictions for a limited time for the sake of their salvation. So accept affliction with thanksgiving so that it brings you nearer to God, and trust that because of your submission to Him He will bless you and compensate you with great blessings.
Abram and Hagar

Sarai heard God's promise to her husband Abram that He would give him offspring, but ten years had passed for them in the land of Canaan and Sarai had reached the age of 75, so she became sure of her inability to bear children. She thought of giving her maid Hagar to her husband to lie with her, so that if she bore a son he would be counted as the mistress's and not the maid's, according to the custom of that time. Perhaps Sarai thought that the cause of the barrenness was her husband, so that if he lay with another woman and did not beget, she would be sure of that and not be the cause.

Abram obeyed his wife's advice, not to fulfil a desire but in an attempt to fulfil God's promise by a human method and to obtain offspring, and he did not ask God about this. His obedience to Sarai was an error, because he sought with her a human means to fulfil God's promise, as if God were unable to fulfil His promises; and in spite of his friendship with God he neglected prayer and consulting Him in this matter. Perhaps he tried to please his wife, but he should have obeyed God more than his wife.

Sarai gave Hagar her maid to her husband, and at that time polygamy and union with maidservants were permitted, and Abram's self-restraint appears in that it was Sarai who pushed him to it. When he lay with her she conceived, and she became proud toward her mistress, since she was distinguished from her by the ability to bear children, and she began to look at her mistress with contempt, which distressed Sarai greatly.

If God gives you gifts and distinguishes you above others, do not be proud, for the gift is from Him and not from you, and hasten to thank Him if He gives you in spite of your many sins and does not give to others who are better than you. In this way you keep your humility and secure God's gifts to you.

Sarai suffered greatly from her sense of helplessness before her maid, and then realized that the problem of not bearing children was her own responsibility and not her husband's. But this did not move her to repent of relying on her own reason to fulfil God's purposes; rather she accused her husband of wronging her, although it was she who had wronged him by marrying him to Hagar, and she asked God to vindicate her right and discipline her husband, for she said, "The Lord judge between me and you." As for Abram, he bore it in silence, making allowance for her because of her sense of helplessness, and he did not reproach her.

Abram gave Sarai the freedom to do with Hagar what she wished, because the latter had become proud, and it was her mistress's right to discipline her for that. But Sarai disciplined her severely, to the point of humiliation, either with many tasks or with bad treatment, so that Hagar could not bear it and fled from the house, although she was pregnant and in need of care and rest. Perhaps Hagar felt that her mistress was wearying her with work beyond her strength that could cause the loss of the child, so she fled.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: Hagar: it means stranger.
The way to Shur: it is the caravan road in the wilderness.

In her flight Hagar headed to the wilderness of Paran, north of Sinai, and perhaps she was returning to Egypt, her original country, and was heading for the way to Shur, a well-known road traveled by caravans. She rested at a spring of water, perhaps the Springs of Moses, and the angel of the Lord appeared to her, and perhaps it was a divine appearance, as evidenced by the fact that she afterwards addressed him as God.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: The angel of the Lord called her Sarai's maid to declare to her her natural position, for her place was Sarai's house and not flight, and he asked her, "Where are you going?" and she confessed that she was fleeing from her mistress's harshness toward her.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: The angel asked her not to flee but to return to her mistress Sarai and submit to her, because she had erred by her pride when she conceived, and for this reason Sarai humbled her; so she must return and behave submissively toward her mistress as she used to behave in former times before she conceived.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: God comforted her because she was humbled, and it seems she asked for His help, so He promised her a son, "Ishmael," that is, God has heard her, and He also promised her abundant offspring from him.

God hears you when you are in distress and call on Him, and He keeps you, blesses you and guides you to your good. And if He asks of you the opposite of what you wished, submit to His will so that you find rest.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: He prophesied that Ishmael would be fierce in temper like the wild beasts, attacking those around him to dominate them, and others would rise against him and wrong him as he wrongs them. He also determined the dwelling place of him and his seed, that it would be before his brothers, that is, the seed of Isaac, and indeed the seed of Ishmael settled in the Arabian Peninsula, facing the land of Canaan in which the seed of Isaac and Jacob settled.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: You are El Roi: You are the God whom I have seen.

Hagar declared that she had seen God at the spring of water, so the well was called Beer-lahai-roi, that is, the living God appeared in this place. This well lies between the city of Kadesh, which means holy and is south of Jerusalem, and Bered, which means cold and lies west of Kadesh.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: Hagar returned and submitted to her mistress Sarai, who received her, and the days of her pregnancy were completed and she bore a son, and Abram called him Ishmael as God had declared.

entries.section: (2) Hagar's flight and the birth of Ishmael

paragraphs.text: Abram's age when Ishmael was born was 86 years, and he begot Isaac at the age of one hundred, so Ishmael is fourteen years older than Isaac.
Circumcision

God's appearances to Abram follow one another, and covenants between them are repeated, to confirm his faith and that of all his seed. Adam in Paradise had no need of covenants, since he moved freely in love and friendship with God; but after the fall man needed covenants and signs, such as the rainbow in the days of Noah and circumcision for Abraham, so that he might stand firm in his faith and not be shaken by the evil surrounding him.

Abram reached the age of 99 years and the fulfilment of God's promise of offspring drew near, so God appeared to him to prepare him spiritually, declaring Himself to be Almighty, for He is able to do everything, even what surpasses reason, namely that Sarah should bear a child at the age of ninety.

Walk before Me: that you may know that I care for you and so be reassured, and that I watch over you and so live in My fear and keep away from evil. Be perfect: walk in the way of perfection so as to please Me in all your thoughts, words and deeds.

Remember always that God sees you and cares for you, so do not be troubled by the evils around you or the afflictions that can harm you, for He is able to protect you even if you enter into affliction, and if you fall, He raises you up. Remember in all your dealings that God is with you, so do not anger Him, and likewise in your times alone, so that you keep your mind and all your senses pure.
Walking in the way of perfection is the condition for receiving the divine covenant and the abundant blessing in offspring.

Abram felt the greatness of God Almighty and His kindnesses and surpassing love, so he prostrated himself in reverence to Him, in thanksgiving for His love and in asking for His help so that he might be able to walk in the way of perfection. And since he submitted, God declared His readiness for more abundant blessings, and God continued His speech with him.

Along with the promise of blessing and circumcision, God changed his name from Abram, that is, exalted father, to Abraham, that is, father of a great multitude. For every person loves his name and the meaning of the name affects him, and for this reason one who receives a priestly rank has his name changed, and many prefer to give new names to their children when they receive the sacrament of Baptism, as a declaration of the new blessing they receive. Thus Abraham becomes the father of all believers until the end of the world.
God promised an abundance of offspring and the formation of many nations or states that live by Abraham's faith and have kings and rulers from his seed over them.
God pledges to be a God and shepherd not only to Abraham but to everyone of his seed who lives in the faith, and this care continues not only in the world but forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.
He completed His promise to Abraham to give his seed the land of Canaan, and this was accomplished by Joshua, and this land was a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

Abram was given the sign of the covenant, which is the circumcision of every male, himself and his seed and all who live with him. God wanted the sign to be in the body of man throughout his life so that he would not forget his covenant with God. The cutting of a part of a man's flesh means cutting evil out of his life, to live pure with God in a faith that differs from that of all the people around him, that is, the pagans of that time.

God wanted this cutting to be in the reproductive organ, which shares with God in begetting offspring and giving them life, so that man would remember that his life has become new in God, and would also care for his children when he circumcises them into the new life with God.

Every male is circumcised and not the females, because the woman is sanctified in the man, so the circumcision of the man includes the covenant with the woman also. This is not to belittle her, for He took care to circumcise the servants, who are of course no better than their mistresses. It is also known that the circumcision of a man is beneficial to health, whereas the circumcision of a woman is harmful.
Here the details of carrying out circumcision are declared, and they are:

1- A son of eight days: the time of circumcision is fixed, the eighth day after the child's birth. The number (8) is the day of Christ's Resurrection, which came after the Sabbath, the seventh day, and the Resurrection is the new life; likewise circumcision is a type of Baptism, for it too is the beginning of the new life with God, and for this reason the Church is keen on the baptism of infants.
2- Born in the house: the servants born in the house, who are strangers not of the seed of the head of the household.

3- Bought with your money: the servants who are bought and are circumcised after their purchase; that is, all servants are circumcised, whether after being bought or as their sons whom they beget inside the house. This means God's covenant and care for the poor as for the rich, or for the despised as for the great, for God is Father of all.
4- An everlasting covenant: circumcision is a type of Baptism, which gives us eternal life with God.

If a person refuses to be circumcised, he rejects the covenant with God, that is, he is dead in God's sight and has no new life; and to show this, God commanded that he be cut off and removed from the people of God, that is, that he not become a Jew.
Remember at the beginning of each day the sacrament of Baptism which you received, so that you may live with your new nature with God, cling to Him and offer your love to everyone you meet.

With the covenant of circumcision God changed the name of Sarai, that is, my princess, to Sarah, that is, princess, for she is not a princess to Abram only but a mother of all believers, so she is called a princess in general.

It is declared here openly that Sarah will bear a son although her age had reached 89 years, and He even promises that her seed will become very numerous and that nations and states with kings will be formed from it.
Abraham rejoiced greatly and prostrated himself on the ground, thanking God for the second time in the same meeting.

His laughter here was not doubt but joy and glorification of God's miraculous work, as evidenced by the fact that God did not reproach him as He did Sarah when she laughed (ch. 18:13), and this is confirmed by the faith of the Apostle Paul in (Rom 4:18-20).

Thank God for His gifts and submit to Him by prostration, and His heart will rejoice and He will give you more and more, that you may enjoy His fatherhood. Thank Him every morning and in every prayer.

Abraham felt the greatness of the divine promise and that he did not deserve it, and he was still attached to his son Ishmael and thought the promise would be fulfilled in him, so he asked God to bless him that he might live before Him, that is, live in God's way and fear.

God made allowance for Abraham, because he was the first person in history with whom this miracle happened, of begetting from his aged wife of ninety years. So God was long-suffering toward him and assured him that the promise would be fulfilled through Sarah with offspring, and He fixed the name for him, Isaac, which means laughter, because his parents laughed when they heard the news of his birth, and indeed everyone who heard marveled and rejoiced. And God added in His assurance that He would bless the seed of Isaac and care for them with mercies, not only in this world but forever in the heavenly Kingdom.

God also paid heed to Abraham's request for his son Ishmael, that God bless him, so He promised him great offspring, 12 sons; for although he would live far from his father and depart from the faith, the number of his offspring would be great.

He returned and affirmed that the promise is of Isaac and not of Ishmael, and fixed the time of his birth a year from that time, that is, when Abraham would be a hundred years old and Sarah ninety, while Ishmael would be 14 years old.

God's speech with Abraham ended, with the covenant of circumcision, the changing of names and the promise of Isaac, and then God went up, that is, the appearance in which God had appeared to Abraham vanished. It is not specified here what this appearance was, whether a cloud, a light or some other great sight.

After Abraham received the blessing of circumcision, which is a type of Baptism, God appeared to him, for circumcision or Baptism is the beginning of a departure into a new life with God. Abraham was sitting not only to rest but to watch the road, perhaps to do good to a stranger passing by, especially at this time of day when the heat is intense; and the word Mamre, as we said, means vision.

Three men: one of the appearances of God the Son in the Old Testament before His incarnation, and with Him two angels. Abraham saw three men from afar passing through the desert, and hurried to them to host them and give them rest in this heat. Here appears Abraham's love of doing good and his haste to it although he was an old man, indeed 99 years old, and his humility also appears in his bowing down to them in respect and honor, although he did not know that they were God and His angels.

Care for doing good, for it is your opportunity to offer something to God in the form of the needy, and if you feel that it is offered to God you will hasten to it and humble yourself as you offer your love to them, because it is a great blessing to you which you do not deserve, that God should accept something from you; and you will then rejoice in His love that covers you and satisfies you.

Abraham spoke with the one distinguished among the three, whom he afterwards learned was God, and showed him respect when he said, "My Lord," and begged him to accept his hospitality and rest a little at his tent.

Abraham begged to perform for them the customary duties of hospitality at that time, namely washing the feet, because they walked in open footwear (sandals) in the sand. This act means love and great humility on the part of this wealthy old man who owned hundreds of servants and very many livestock, and was a great father with a continual relationship with God, yet forgot all this to wash the feet of three men passing in the desert before him.

With humility also he asks them, after washing their feet and their resting under the shade of the trees, to let him offer them a little food, which he describes as a morsel of bread, although in truth he would offer a great feast. They agreed and accepted his hospitality and headed toward the tent.
A measure: it equals approximately 7.5 liters.
Fine meal: the fine white flour.
Cakes: bread made on a stone after it is heated with embers, and it is a choice kind of bread.

Abraham's love of doing good appears in his haste toward Sarah and his calling her to hurry to prepare the choicest bread, with an ample quantity of flour, three measures. The number three signifies the Holy Trinity, or faith, hope and love.
Tender: young, so it is easy to cook and the taste of its meat is delicious.
Abraham continued his haste in preparing the feast, so he took a young calf and gave it to one of his servants to slaughter and cook.

After the food was prepared he set the meat and bread, and also butter and milk, before his three guests, and he stood, in spite of his old age, to be at their service if they needed anything while they ate. In his humility he did not find himself worthy to eat with them but stood to serve them, and did not assign this work to one of his servants. Of course God and His two angels have no need of material food, but they acted in a miraculous way in eating the food, because it is easy for the spiritual to do the material acts of human beings.

Let your giving be generous, as God has given to you generously, for the abundance of your giving expresses the overflow of your love. So care for the needs of others, especially those around you, and give them more than they asked, so that in your giving they feel God, who cares for them more than they ask.

The three men spoke, and perhaps what is meant is the great man among them, that is, God, with Abram, and they asked him about Sarah his wife, and he answered that she was in the tent. Perhaps he marveled that they knew his wife's name, Sarah, without his having told them, so he began to understand that they were not ordinary men but spiritual beings from heaven.
The time of life: about a year, since life is divided into periods which are years.

The great person among the three, who is God, promised Abraham that He would give him offspring from Sarah after about a year. Sarah heard these words, for she was standing inside the tent beside its door, while Abraham was standing in front of the door speaking with the three men.

Abraham had reached the age of 99 years and Sarah had reached 89 years, so they were advanced in age and Sarah had lost her ability to bear children, since the custom of women had ceased with her, which shows the ability to bear children.
Sarah laughed, either from shame, for how would she conceive when she was old, and what would people say about her; and this is the opinion of St. Clement of Alexandria.

St. Augustine, however, says that she laughed with joy at this happy news which she had longed for through many long years. There is a third opinion, that she laughed in doubt about the possibility of conception for an old woman and her aged husband, who had no natural ability to bear children, and this is the more probable opinion. And she said, how shall I have the delight of conceiving at this age, and she humbly called her husband her lord and described him as an old man for whom it is hard to beget.
God reproached Abraham because of Sarah's laughter and the weakness of her faith, affirming His ability to fulfil His promise of Sarah's conceiving, because He is able to do everything.

Sarah was afraid and lied and said, "I did not laugh," because she did not yet know that it was God; but God affirmed that she had laughed. This shows that the Holy Bible did not hide the weaknesses of the saints, but showed Sarah's sin, so that we the weak may be encouraged, whatever our sins, to live with God and advance in holiness.

If Abraham and Sarah offered love in hospitality to strangers, God blessed them with a greater blessing, which was Sarah's conceiving, because God is not indebted to anyone. Trust in God's blessing for you so as to advance in the way of your love for all around you, especially the needy or those fallen into evident sins, to show tenderness to them and encourage them, and then God will have compassion on you.

After the talk about Sarah's conceiving, the three men rose and walked on the road to Sodom, and Abraham walked with them to see them off, and this shows his care in completing all the duties of hospitality.

God spoke within Himself and said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing" concerning Sodom and Gomorrah? This shows God's surpassing love for Abraham and His unfathomable humility, to the point of caring for the children of the saints and revealing His secrets to them.

For in spite of the vast difference between God and His human creatures, He raises them to the level of friendship, so that He cannot but give them His secrets, and He even accepts their intervention and dialogue with Him in the management of the world ... It is a love that cannot be expressed.
God gave reasons for His friendship and His care in revealing His secrets to Abraham, and they are:
1- He will become a great nation, which is the chosen people of God, so he has great value in God's sight.
2- He will be the cause of blessing for all the peoples of the world through Christ, who comes from his seed.
3- Because God has known his faith, his love and his pure conduct, he deserves to be a son of God.
4- So that he may command his seed to love God, worship Him and walk in uprightness.
God declared before His angels and before Abraham that the sins of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah had greatly increased, and through their enormity had become like a cry rising toward heaven.
Sodom: it means burning.
Gomorrah: it means flood.
They are two cities lying south of the Dead Sea, and it is understood from the meaning of their two names that they deserve divine punishment by burning and flood.

God continued His speech, saying that He had come down from His heaven to examine the two cities and know the extent of their sins and whether they deserved punishment or not, to show His justice in not hastening to judgment but examining well first, to declare the guilt or innocence of every person. God uses human expressions so that we may understand His purposes, such as "come down," but God is present everywhere and does not move from place to place, and He also knows everything and has no need to come down in order to examine.

After this part of the talk about Sodom and Gomorrah, the two angels departed and went to Sodom, while Abraham was still standing with the great man whom he now knew with certainty to be God, because He declared His knowledge of the sins of Sodom and that He is the just Judge who is able to punish the wicked or acquit them.

Abraham's tender heart was moved with pity for the people of wicked Sodom and Gomorrah, to give them an opportunity to repent, and he relied on a matter connected with God's justice, namely the presence of some righteous people in these two cities, and God's justice does not allow the destruction of the righteous with the wicked. So he asked God to spare the two cities if there were 50 righteous persons. Here another important truth appears, namely the importance of the life of the righteous, which becomes a cause of obtaining God's mercies not only for them but for all around them.

God accepted Abraham's intercession for the two cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and agreed to spare them if 50 righteous were found in them, and this confirms the importance of intercession with God, but sadly these fifty were not found in Sodom.

Abraham took courage with the boldness of sonship and continued his speech with God, but he did not forget his weakness as a human being, so he humbly declared that he was dust and ashes. He did not count himself great because God accepted to reveal His secrets to him, converse with him and hear his intercession, so he made a second request, that the fifty righteous be reduced by five, that is, that God spare the city if 45 righteous were found in it, and God agreed, but sadly these righteous were not found in it.
Abraham continued his intercession and made a third request, to spare the city for the sake of only 40 righteous in it, and God agreed, but sadly they were not found.

With love Abraham continued his intercession and asked God's leave that He not punish the wicked if only thirty righteous were found, and God agreed, but Abraham discovered that these thirty did not exist; then he reduced them to twenty, and God agreed, and again He did not find twenty righteous in it.

Abraham asked leave to make his last request of God in this intercession, after God had been very long-suffering toward him and had accepted all his requests, and he begged that He spare the city if ten righteous were found in it, but He did not find these righteous in it.
