So Abraham was ashamed of himself and became certain of God's mercy joined with His justice, so he fell silent and God vanished from before him, while he returned to his tent filled with feelings of love toward God and grief for the wicked who were about to perish.

Have pity on sinners however great their evil, and ask God to forgive them, and help them with your love so that they repent and are satisfied with God's love, so that they have no need of sin but discover its bitterness.
The burning of Sodom

The two angels, who were the two angels present at the meeting with Abraham, arrived at Sodom and entered by the gate of the city, where there is usually a square in which the judges and the people sit. It was evening and most of the people of the city had gone off to their houses, so Lot hurried to them to host them, and bowed down in respect and welcome to them.

Lot offered them his love by hosting them in his house, so that they might wash their feet, eat and rest, and then continue their journey the next day. But they refused Lot's invitation and wanted to spend the night in the square, as a declaration of their rejection of the city's evils and of not mixing with them, and an implicit rebuke to Lot for accepting to live among the wicked.

Lot held on to them and repeated his invitation many times until they accepted the invitation and went to his house, where he offered them unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven, which can be made quickly, and they ate at his house.

The men of Sodom gathered around Lot's house and asked him to give them the two men, his guests, so that they might sin with them, because this whole city had fallen into the sin of homosexual perversion, so that this sin was called the Sodomite sin.
When the cries of the men of Sodom rose, demanding the guests, Lot went out to them and begged them not to do evil to these two guests.

The cries of the men of Sodom increased, so Lot showed his readiness to offer these wicked men his two virgin daughters to sin with them instead of the guests, and perhaps he wanted by this to shame them so that they would leave and let him be. But in any case he erred by this wicked offer, and perhaps he said it because he was influenced by living among the wicked, so that he accepted, if only in intention, to offer his two daughters for fornication.

The men of Sodom rejected Lot's offer of his two daughters, insisting on taking the two men, because they were attached to homosexual perversion to a degree beyond fornication with women, so they moved toward Lot's house to break it down and rape the two men.
The two men, that is, the two angels, hurried, opened the door, pulled Lot into the house and shut the door before the men reached him.

The two angels struck the men of Sodom with blindness, so they were alarmed and stumbled against one another. Strangely, they did not repent of their evil after this calamity, the blindness that befell them, and they kept searching for the door to burst into the house, blind as they were, to rape the two men, but they were unable to reach the door and, blinded, wandered away from it.

Do not be lenient with sin, lest you grow accustomed to it and cling to it and even justify it, and so blind your heart to God and the truth. Hasten to repentance so that you may discover your sin, trust that by God's power you can overcome it, and partake of the Holy Mysteries, so that you taste the sweetness of God and shelter by His power from your evils.

The two angels declared to Lot that God would destroy Sodom and Gomorrah and all the cities of the plain because of their immersion in evil, and said to him, bring out whomever you have in the city, whether those who live in your house, the believers in God, that is, his wife and his two virgin daughters, and also his married daughters with their husbands, who are called Lot's sons-in-law. Although his sons-in-law were from the people of Sodom, God was ready to save them if they believed in Him and showed it by going out with Lot.

The angels' speech was at night, so Lot hurried to warn his sons-in-law and his daughters so that they would prepare to leave Sodom, but they did not believe his words about the destruction of the city and considered them jesting and not true. Sadly, Lot's married daughters lost their faith in God and their trust in their father's words and were carried along after their husbands' words, so they perished with them and with the rest of the people of Sodom.

The night passed with his sons-in-law and his daughters insisting on not obeying God's word, so the two angels intervened, warned Lot of the nearness of the city's destruction and asked him to hurry out, he and his wife and his two virgin daughters.

Lot kept lingering over leaving because of his attachment to his daughters and sons-in-law and his longing that they obey so as to be saved, and perhaps he was also thinking of his possessions, all of which he would leave behind in Sodom. So the two angels had to seize him and his wife and his two daughters and pull them out of the city that was about to burn.

When the angel brought Lot and those with him out, one of the two angels, the leading one, commanded him not to look back, he and those with him, that is, to cut off every attachment to the material things he had left in Sodom, since all had been defiled by evil, and to flee away from the city with all speed, leaving all the plain (the Jordan plain), which means the whole region of evil, and to go to the mountain, where escape lies in height and spiritual elevation.

Lot asked leave of the angel who was speaking to him that He spare the small city which lies at the edge of the plain of the Jordan, east of the Dead Sea, and which was called Bela, so that he might flee to it and not live in the mountain, lest wild beasts attack him or he suffer harm in this wilderness.

It was weakness of faith in Lot to fear living in the mountain although it was God who commanded him to, and to ask to live in a city which truly lies at the edge of this evil region but could have been defiled, if only partly. I wish you would obey God however difficult His commands seem in your eyes, and not rely on your reason against God's commandments, for He knows your good better than you ... only believe in Him and you will find your salvation and rest.
I have favored you also concerning this thing: I have honored you and agreed to your request.

God agreed to Lot's intercession for this small city and did not destroy it for his sake, and this is clear proof for the second time of the importance of intercession, after Abraham's intercession for Sodom and Gomorrah.

The angel asked Lot to hurry toward Zoar so that God might carry out His word by burning Sodom and all around it, and he called the city of Bela by the name Zoar because it is small, as Lot said. Here God's great care for His children appears, that He cannot do any harm to the wicked that could touch His children, even a little. It is fitting here to compare Abraham and Lot, and the following appears:
Abraham | Lot
1- He lived in the wilderness. | 1- He lived in the fertile city.
2- He let God choose for him. | 2- He chose for himself.
3- He saved Lot by God's power. | 3- He was weak, so he was taken captive by Chedorlaomer.
4- He took nothing of the spoils after his victory | 4- He was absorbed in the pleasures of Sodom.
over Chedorlaomer.
5- God and two angels visited him. | 5- Only two angels visited him.
6- God and the two angels welcomed entering his place. | 6- The two angels refused to enter, and after urging they entered his house.
7- God promised him blessed offspring. | 7- The two angels warned him of the destruction of the city.
8- He entered into dialogue with God. | 8- His speech with the two angels was brief.
9- He believed in God. | 9- He believed the words of the two angels but obeyed with difficulty, so they pulled him out of the city.
10- He increased with the birth of Isaac, and his possessions were many. | 10- He lost his wife, his married daughters and all his possessions.
11- He lived in the wilderness and enjoyed many appearances of God. | 11- He refused to live in the mountain and asked
12- He interceded for the wicked, that they might repent, that is, that Sodom be rescued. | to live in Zoar (Bela). 12- He interceded for Zoar so that it would not be destroyed for
13- God kept him because of his faith and obedience. | his own personal benefit.
13- God kept him because of Abraham's intercession.

entries.section: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

paragraphs.text: God's mercies appear in His waiting for Lot's entry into the city of Zoar at the beginning of the day at sunrise, and immediately God rained fire and brimstone from heaven on Sodom and Gomorrah and all the cities of the plain, and everything in them burned, human beings, animals, plants and all that existed. The following appears from this:
1- God's long-suffering and His mercies toward those who believe in Him, whereas His wrath on the wicked and the obstinate is very heavy.
2- The Holy Trinity appears in (v. 24): "The Lord (the Son ...) rained ... from the Lord (the Father)."

entries.section: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

paragraphs.text: Lot's wife did not obey God's word and looked back at Sodom, which had begun to burn, either from her attachment to her daughters or her possessions, so she became a pillar of salt, that is, she became a memorial for the soul that does not obey God. For after God had rescued her, her heart was still attached to wicked Sodom and what was in it, so she perished at once.

I wish you would look to your goal, who is God, at the beginning of each day, and put away your former sins of which you have repented, for remembering evil makes you fall into it again. Be obedient to God even if His word is against your material desires or your feelings, and so be rescued from the wicked world.

entries.section: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

paragraphs.text: Abraham had been occupied with his speaking with God to save the city of Sodom, that perhaps the wicked in it would repent, and also to save Lot and his family, and perhaps he was occupied with this all night. So he rose early and walked on the road leading to Sodom, on which he had walked with God the day before.

entries.section: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

paragraphs.text: Abraham looked toward Sodom and found the smoke of its fire rising toward heaven, and he grieved over its destruction. God did not forbid him to look at Sodom because he sought its salvation and return to God, whereas He forbade Lot and his family to look at Sodom, to stop their attachment to material things and to human feelings toward the defiled city and those in it, even if they were his daughters.

entries.section: (3) The destruction of Sodom and Lot's wife

paragraphs.text: God looked at Abraham's righteousness and intercession and rescued Lot and those with him from destruction, for because of the righteous man God has mercy on those around him, as God blessed the house of Potiphar for Joseph's sake.

entries.section: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

paragraphs.text: Lot relied on his own thinking and chose to live in Zoar for fear of living in the mountain, but then he became afraid of living in Zoar, either because of the presence of wicked people in it or because of his lack of prompt obedience to God in living in the mountain, so he left Zoar and lived in a cave in the mountain.

Let your obedience to God's commandments be swift, for it is the shortest way to rest and reassurance. Material things or reason cannot give you peace, and the only source of it is God and obedience to His commandments.

entries.section: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

paragraphs.text: The fear that was in Lot's heart was also in the heart of his two daughters, for they worried that there were no men to marry them, although there were tribes spread through the desert, but it was an anxiety they had acquired from Sodom through their mixing with the wicked in it.

entries.section: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

paragraphs.text: The two daughters thought of a way to bear offspring, which was to lie with the only man before them, their father, but he would refuse, so they thought of making him drink wine until he lost his discernment, so that they might lie with him, and they actually carried out the idea. From this we understand that Lot had been defiled by his association with the Sodomites and loved wine, so that he accepted that his daughters prepare wine for him and drank much of it until he was drunk and lost his discernment, and moved in a lustful way toward his daughters; so the elder approached him and lay with him while he did not discern that she was his daughter or that he was lying with a female, and perhaps he thought himself in a dream ... and the same was repeated the next day, and the younger lay with him. However much the commentators try to find an excuse for these two daughters in their attempt to preserve the offspring, their error is great, for this is plain fornication and the use of a means, which is wine, to make their father lose the ability to discern so that he does what he does not want without awareness. As for Lot's sin, it is his accepting to drink much wine until he became without will or awareness, so his two daughters exploited this weakness of his before the love of wine.

entries.section: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

paragraphs.text: It seems that the two daughters' lying with their father was not merely two consecutive nights but perhaps lasted for about a month or two until they conceived by their father, and this means Lot's immersion in the love of wine.

entries.section: (4) The sin of Lot's two daughters with their father

paragraphs.text: The elder daughter bore a son whom she called "Moab," that is, from the father, because she bore him by her father, while the younger called her son "Ben-ammi," that is, son of my people, ascribing him to her people and not her father. In any case, two peoples hostile to the people of God, the Jews, came out of them. Moab and the sons of Ammon lived east of the Jordan River, worshipped idols and lived in evil far from God.

Thus the story of righteous Lot ends with a sad event, the begetting of evil, because he loved the world and material things and was defiled by them and lost much of his purity, and likewise his family departed from God and his seed walked in the way of evil. Abraham in Gerar

Abraham lived more than 20 years at the oaks of Mamre west of the Jordan River, and then moved to Gerar, which lies in the south of Palestine about five miles from Gaza, between Kadesh and Shur, which lie in the south of Palestine and were discussed before. Perhaps the reason for his moving was a search for fertile pastures for his flocks or a famine in the region where he lived (map 6).
Abimelech, which means my father is king, was a title of the kings of Gerar like the title Pharaoh for the kings of Egypt.

Abraham, great in faith, fell this time also in weakness of faith when he feared for himself from the people of Gerar and their king, lest they take his wife Sarah for her beauty and kill him. He repeated the sin of lying and said she was his sister, relying on the fact that she was his sister from his father and not his full sister. But the intention here was a lie, as we said, to protect himself from the possibility that the people of Gerar would kill him.

When Abimelech learned that Sarah was Abraham's sister and saw her beauty, he was dazzled by it although she was approaching ninety years, so he sent and took her to his palace to be his wife. Sadly Abraham did not speak but let them take her because of his fear of them, forgetting God's appearances and His promise that she would bear, after some months, the son of promise, Isaac.

Accept detachment in your life, and even afflictions, for they protect you from many sins you do not know, and ask for God's help and it will suffice you and support you. And do not move in your life except after prayer and asking God's guidance, and so you will live reassured and pure.

God appeared to Abimelech in a dream by night, and it seems that He had struck him with a disease that made him unable to approach Sarah and fearful of death, and God told him that he would die because of his taking Abraham's wife by force.

Abimelech answered God that he had not approached Sarah, but in lowliness begged Him not to destroy him and his people, because he did not know that she was married, indeed Abraham had said she was his sister and she had said he was her brother. He therefore did not intend to do any evil and consequently did not deserve to be destroyed, he and all his people, because of his sin, for he had taken her to marry her with a pure heart.

God accepted Abimelech's plea and even said to him, because I know the purity of your heart in this matter, I kept you from erring in marrying Sarah, and perhaps that was by the sudden illness that God allowed Abimelech in this night, so that he was occupied with his illness, and it also afflicted his wife and maidservants with a disease that prevented them from bearing; it may have been pains and inability to give birth, as appears from (v. 18).

God describes Abraham as a prophet, that is, a great devout man near to God, so as to make Abimelech afraid to approach Sarah; indeed He asked Abimelech to beg Abraham to pray for him so that God would remove the diseases from them, and at the same time threatened Abimelech with death if he did not obey, although he had not yet erred, but to keep him away from error.

Abimelech feared God, who had appeared to him in a dream of the night, so when he woke early he hurried to gather his servants who helped him in leading the people and told them what he had heard from God. They were assured of it because all the women about to give birth suffered from inability to give birth, which increased their fear of God and their belief in the king's words.

Abimelech summoned Abraham and reproached him for his lie in saying that Sarah was his sister, which exposed the king and the kingdom to a great danger, namely marrying a married woman and angering God so that He would take vengeance on them. The king asked him what had made him do this great deed. God allowed Abimelech to reproach and rebuke Abraham, the man of faith, so that he would be humbled and repent and not think himself better than others because of his faith.

Accept the voice of God on the tongue of all around you, even if it is your child or any person who seems less than you, for you need to learn from every person to complete your repentance and spiritual striving, and by this you grow spiritually and the devil cannot overcome you.
Abraham did not apologize for his error but sadly offered unsound justifications, which are:

1- His feeling that the people of Gerar had no fear of God, perhaps thinking them like the people of Sodom, so that they would kill him in order to take his wife by force. By this he fell into judging others, indeed into a false accusation, because in truth they had the fear of God, as evidenced by the obedience of Abimelech and the whole kingdom to the word of God who appeared to him in the dream.

2- That Sarah was his sister from his father and not his full sister, and he had agreed with her to hide that she was his wife in any strange place they went to, so that no one would harm him. The truth is that this is a lie, since it hides his marriage to her and exposes her to a strange man's lying with her, so she errs and makes the one who lies with her err ... This is a wicked agreement on sin and is not acceptable, for a sound end does not justify a wrong means.
The fear of God was in Abimelech's heart, and it made him not only refrain from touching Sarah but also appeared in his treatment of Abraham, and this appears in the following:
1- He reproached him for not declaring that Sarah was his wife, as mentioned before, for he wants to live pure and not take anyone's wife by force.
2- He returned to him Sarah his wife.
3- He honored him by giving him gifts of sheep and oxen.
4- He also gave him menservants and maidservants.
5- He welcomed him to live in the land of his kingdom in any place he wished.
A thousand pieces of silver: that is, a thousand shekels, and the shekel equals approximately 15 grams.
A covering of the eyes: honor and restoration of reputation.
You are vindicated: nothing harmed you, but you received compensation and a sufficient apology.

6- He gave Abraham also a thousand pieces of silver, a valuable gift at that time by comparison with what Sarah or any of the people around them had, as an apology and restoration of honor, that she was exposed to being a wife, or was nominally called the wife of Abimelech for a short time, until God showed him that she was Abraham's wife.

Abimelech's great generosity and liberality are to be noted, as well as the delicacy of his feelings in his apology to Abraham and his offering him these gifts after learning that Sarah was his wife, and not as a bridal gift as in the case of Pharaoh.

Be generous in your dealings with others as long as you are able, for your generosity shows your love, especially if you have wronged another or another has felt distress for any reason, for your gifts and your care make his heart rejoice and restore his peace.

Had closed up every womb: He made the pregnant women who were about to give birth unable to do so despite their pains, or caused the fetuses to fall from the wombs of their pregnant mothers so that the term was not completed in their bellies, that is, He closed the womb from completing its work of maturing the fetuses.

After this evident love and generosity of Abimelech, God covered for Abraham and showed him to be a prophet and a man of blessing, and made him pray for the healing of the wife and the maidservants of Abimelech, so God healed them and they regained their ability to conceive and give birth.
The birth of Isaac

entries.section: (1) The birth, circumcision and weaning of Isaac

paragraphs.text: Visited: God remembered Sarah and granted her to conceive as He had promised her.
Sarah conceived as God had promised her and gave birth at the time He had set (ch. 18:10), and she and Abraham rejoiced, and they named him Isaac as God had called him.

Trust in God's promises to you, for they are faithful and true and must come to pass however adverse the surrounding circumstances, and even ask God for His promises in faith and hope for blessed eternity, and so you will rise above all pains.

entries.section: (1) The birth, circumcision and weaning of Isaac

paragraphs.text: Abraham took care to carry out God's word by circumcising every male, so he circumcised Isaac on the eighth day. His age at that time was a hundred years, and he rejoiced at begetting the son of promise, who was a clear and miraculous gift from God.

entries.section: (1) The birth, circumcision and weaning of Isaac

paragraphs.text: God has made me laugh: He has given me great joy.

All who hear will laugh with me: everyone who hears of Isaac's birth rejoices and congratulates Sarah and Abraham. Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children: people's amazement and joy at Isaac's birth and Sarah's nursing him, and their congratulations to his parents.
Sarah declared her joy at Isaac's birth and at people's congratulating her on the birth and the nursing despite the old age of herself and Abraham.

entries.section: (1) The birth, circumcision and weaning of Isaac

paragraphs.text: It is customary in the East that a child be weaned at about two years of age, so Isaac was weaned at this age, and Abraham rejoiced at this event, which represents Isaac's maturing, and made a feast for his loved ones and neighbors. He did not make a feast at the birth but at the weaning, out of his concern for his son's maturing.

Hagar and her son Ishmael, who was sixteen years old, were vexed when Isaac was weaned because of the great feast that was made for Isaac, whereas no feast was made for Ishmael when he was weaned; and because Hagar thought that her son was the only heir of Abraham, and now Isaac had appeared, who rivals him and may even take a larger inheritance than he because of Abraham's care for him. She passed these feelings to her son Ishmael, who began to trouble the child Isaac with mockery and scorn. The Apostle Paul describes this joking as persecution, that is, he was troubling him severely (Gal 4:29).

Sarah was greatly distressed for her child Isaac, persecuted by his older brother, and feared that he would harm him, so she told Abraham to cast out the maidservant and her son, so that Ishmael would not inherit anything of Abraham's possessions but all would be Isaac's.
Abraham was greatly displeased at Sarah's words because he loved his son Ishmael, who had become a young man, and felt that Sarah's words contained selfishness and injustice toward Ishmael.

God agreed with Sarah's words and told Abraham to listen to her voice. Even if there was in her words distress at Ishmael or injustice to him, yet on the other hand only Isaac is the son of promise, whereas Ishmael was born according to human will and not the will of God. Nevertheless God promised Abraham to bless Ishmael after he cast him out together with his mother, and to give him great offspring.

Obey God's commandments even if they are against your will or your feelings, because His wisdom surpasses all understanding and He knows your good, and what seems bad in your eyes may be the best. Know that you are not more tender toward people than He is, so accept His will in all your life.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

paragraphs.text: The wilderness of Beersheba: it lies on the southern border of the land of Canaan, that is, Palestine.

Abraham obeyed God as was his habit, rising above his fatherly feelings, and gave her bread, that is, food, and a skin of water, which Hagar and her son Ishmael carried on their shoulders, and they headed south toward the wilderness of Beersheba. He sent them away early, perhaps that they might reach a suitable place to stay before the day ended.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

paragraphs.text: The water in the skin ran out after they had walked a long time in the desert, and Ishmael began to thirst until his strength failed. His mother feared he would die of thirst and could not bear to see him die before her eyes, so she sat him down, faint, under a tree, while she sat far from him, looking at him and watching him, and praying and weeping to God to rescue her and her son. Ishmael could not raise his voice in weeping because of his weakness from thirst, but his heart was asking God to rescue him without speaking, or perhaps he was whispering a few words. A bowshot: the average distance an arrow travels from the one who shoots it to the place it reaches when shot from the bow, a distance that is not small but within sight.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

paragraphs.text: Hold him with your hand: support him and take courage.

Hagar heard the voice of an angel speaking to her from heaven, and perhaps she saw him in a beautiful form or a great light, and he reassured her that God had heard Ishmael's prayers, which came from his heart or in faint whispers he raised to heaven while he lay under the tree, for Ishmael had learned much about God from his father Abraham. He informed her that God would keep him and bless him, and even give him many offspring, so that he would become a nation great in number.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

paragraphs.text: God guided her to a well that was near her, which perhaps had been hidden behind some trees, so she saw it and hurried to it to fill the skin from it and give her thirsty son to drink, so that he regained his strength, and she also drank with him, and they were strengthened and continued their journey.

entries.section: (3) The casting out of Hagar and Ishmael

paragraphs.text: An archer: a hunter of animals.
The wilderness of Paran: it lies north of Sinai.

Hagar and her son Ishmael reached the wilderness of Paran and lived there, and her son learned to hunt animals, and she chose for him a wife from Egypt, of her own race, so he married and settled in the north of Sinai.

God hears your prayer, especially in distress, when it comes from your heart, for He is near you and rescues you and strengthens you however weak you are, and solves your problems however impossible they seem. So accustom yourself to take refuge in Him every day in your various needs.

entries.section: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

paragraphs.text: Phichol: that is, the mouth of all, and it was probably the title of the commander of the army, who was considered as the prime minister, next to the king directly.

Abimelech sensed Abraham's success and the blessing of God that was with him during his stay in Gerar, so he feared his power and asked to make a treaty of safety between himself and Abraham so that he would not harm him; and he reminded him of his kindness to him, as he had welcomed him in his land and he had lived in peace throughout the previous period. Abraham agreed to make the treaty and to swear not to expose him to harm or wrong him.

God gives awe and favor to His children in the eyes of those around them, so do not fear those around you, but hold fast to God's commandments and live a life of repentance, and He will bless you and keep you and make those around you hold you in awe, for they feel the power of God that is in you, even if you are quiet and silent.

entries.section: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

paragraphs.text: Abraham reproached Abimelech about a well that he had dug and that Abimelech's servants had seized, and Abimelech apologized to Abraham because he had not known of this wrong and wished that Abraham had told him so that he could have prevented it. From this appear Abraham's strength and Abimelech's gentleness, respect and fear of Abraham, and it also appears that the spiritual person has the right to demand his rights as long as this does not cause problems and clashes that make him lose his peace.

entries.section: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

paragraphs.text: Abraham welcomed Abimelech's visit and his request for a treaty and offered him gifts of sheep and oxen, and they swore not to wrong each other and made the treaty.

entries.section: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

paragraphs.text: Abraham set seven ewe lambs aside and Abimelech noticed that and asked him about them, and Abraham said to him, this is another gift I offer you to establish my ownership of this well that was before them, a well that Abraham had dug. Abimelech accepted it, and this was wisdom on Abraham's part, for he established his ownership in a gentle way, and for this reason this well was called "Beersheba," in reference to the seven ewe lambs. Then Abimelech departed and returned to his country (map 6).

entries.section: (4) The treaty of Abraham and Abimelech

paragraphs.text: A tamarisk tree: tall trees with strong wood and thread-like leaves, regarded as windbreaks, planted around a place to enclose it and protect it from the sands.
Everlasting: eternal and without beginning, that is, lasting without beginning or end.

Abraham planted tamarisk trees, and this was a declaration of his settling in this place, and he built an altar to God and offered sacrifices and prayers, so he blessed the place and lived in it, in the south of the land of Canaan, for a long time.
The sacrifice of Isaac

After God had appeared to Abraham many times and confirmed His promises of blessing to him, and after He had given him Isaac, the son of promise, and had blessed his possessions and strength when he defeated Chedorlaomer, so that a strong friendship arose between him and God, He appeared to him this time to test him, to bring out his virtues and increase him in love. This is of course different from the temptations that Satan devises to make us fall into sin.

Your son, your only son: Isaac became Abraham's only son after the sending away of Ishmael, and he was a young man; the Fathers expect that his age was not less than 25 years, and some say that he had passed thirty.
Whom you love: because he was the son of his old age and in him all the divine promises of blessing are fulfilled.

The land of Moriah: its meaning is teacher, or vision, or the Lord provides, because there God taught Abraham self-giving love, and Abraham saw God, and He spoke with him, and God prepared a ransom for his son. It is said that it lies east of Jerusalem, at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, where David built an altar and God stopped the plague (2 Sam 24:24), and there also Solomon built the temple. There is another opinion that it lies north of Jerusalem, where Mount Gerizim is, and it is said that Golgotha was in the land of Moriah.

God asked Abraham for an exceedingly hard thing, that he offer Isaac, his only son, so greatly beloved to him, as a sacrifice to God, and go to the land of Moriah, and there He would guide him to a mountain to go up on and offer Isaac as a sacrifice there.

If a commandment seems hard to you, do not be troubled, for God will give you help to fulfil it, and in carrying it out your love for God appears, your faith grows and you receive countless blessings.

entries.section: (2) The way to offering the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Split wood: that is, he prepared it to burn quickly and arranged it as sticks suitable for burning.

God appeared to Abraham in Beersheba by night, and Abraham rose early and prepared the wood with which he would kindle the burnt offering, that is, his son whom he would slaughter, and here his immediate obedience to God appears. He did not tell Sarah lest she hinder him by her motherly feelings from carrying out God's command. He took with him two young men of his servants to carry water and food for the journey, rode a donkey and went on the road toward the land of Moriah, that is, toward Jerusalem, with Isaac his son.

entries.section: (2) The way to offering the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Abraham walked with Isaac from Beersheba to Jerusalem for three days, and when he reached the land of Moriah God guided him to the mountain on which Isaac would be offered, so he told his two young men, his young servants who had come with him, to sit at the foot of the mountain with the donkey while he and his son Isaac went up the mountain to offer a sacrifice and then return to them. This proves Abraham's faith in God's power to raise his son after he slaughtered him, so that he would return with him and meet the two young men.

entries.section: (2) The way to offering the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Isaac, the young man over twenty-five years of age, carried the wood of the burnt offering, as Christ carried His cross, while Abraham held the fire and the knife, and the two of them walked together going up the mountain.

entries.section: (2) The way to offering the sacrifice

paragraphs.text: Isaac wondered, as he walked with his father Abraham to offer a burnt offering to God, that there was no animal with them to slaughter, so he asked his father about the animal that they would slaughter. This was a very painful question to the heart of Abraham, the tender father, but his faith in God and reliance on Him made him hold himself together and answer his son with reassuring words, that God who commanded us to offer a sacrifice to Him will Himself prepare for us the sacrifice that we shall offer. So Isaac fell silent and walked with his father.

If some questions from those around you wound your feelings or stir your emotions, do not doubt your faith in God's commandments, and bear the pains for His name's sake, and you will receive God's great blessings.

Abraham told his son Isaac that he would be the sacrifice offered to God as He had commanded, and Isaac submitted and obeyed although he was a young man able to resist an aged old man like his father Abraham, and in this he is a type of Christ, who emptied Himself and obeyed unto death by His own will. So Abraham built an altar with the help of Isaac his son, arranged the wood on it, bound Isaac and laid him on the wood ... How painful this was to the heart of Abraham, the father and the old man, but for God's sake he obeyed and raised the knife to slay Isaac.

Trust that God seeks your good and cannot harm you, so obey His commandments however heavy they seem and He will support you to fulfil them, and by this you show your love for Him, experience Him and enjoy a rest and joy that surpass all understanding. Slay your own will so that you may enjoy the will of God.

At the decisive moment, before the knife came near Isaac, the angel of God appeared and called to Abraham and prevented him from bringing the knife near Isaac, and praised him that he feared God and loved Him to the degree of offering Him the dearest thing he had, his only son, in whom he would receive the promises. When it says of God "Now I know," it does not mean that He did not know before, but He expresses Himself in a way we understand as human beings, declaring Abraham's righteousness before all generations; He means, now Abraham's righteousness has appeared.

God directed Abraham's sight, and he looked behind him and found a ram caught by its horns in one of the trees, which God had prepared, and He commanded him to offer it as a sacrifice in place of Isaac, so Abraham slaughtered it and offered it as a burnt offering before God. By this Isaac is a type of Christ the Redeemer in the following:
1- Isaac carried the burnt offering as Christ carried the cross on the way to Golgotha.
2- Isaac was bound and laid on the wood as Christ was bound and hung on the cross.
3- The knife was raised to slay Isaac as Christ died and was slain on the cross.
4- Isaac returned alive after the ram was offered in his place as Christ rose on the third day.
5- The offering of Isaac showed Abraham's love and great sacrifice and Isaac's submission and love for God, as the cross showed the love of the Father and the submission of the Son.
6- Isaac used to go out into the field in the evening to meditate (ch. 24:63), and Christ used to withdraw to pray.

Abraham rejoiced at the rescue of his son Isaac from death and at seeing God and experiencing His fatherhood and tenderness, so he called the name of this place Jehovah-jireh, that is, he saw God in this place, and this expression became a proverb said in all the following generations of everyone who relies on God and obeys His word, of whom it is said that he has seen God and experienced Him.

After God had prevented Abraham from slaying his son and given him the ram in his place, He called to him a second time from heaven by His angel, renewing the covenant with him clearly because of his surpassing love in accepting to offer Isaac as a sacrifice to God.
God renewed His covenant to Abraham and promised him the following:
1- He gives him a great blessing in his spiritual and material life.
2- He multiplies his seed greatly although he now has only one son.

3- He gives strength to his seed so that they overcome their enemies. What is meant by the gate is the entrance of the city, for every city has a gate and whoever storms it can gain dominion over it. This happened in the victory of the children of Israel over the peoples who lived in the land of Canaan by the hand of Joshua, and then appeared even more in Christ's victory over Satan and his binding by the cross.
4- The seed of Abraham, that is, Christ, since He did not say seeds, in whom is the salvation of mankind that believes in Him.

Abraham came down from the mountain with Isaac and found the two young men, his servants, waiting for him, and he returned riding his donkey to Beersheba, where he lived, a distance of three days, which signifies Christ's Resurrection after three days. Beersheba also signifies Baptism, which is the entrance to the Mysteries and which the believer receives from the blood of Christ, slain on the cross, as the sacrifice was offered on the mountain.

God's blessings to you are very abundant if you respond to His love, for He is rich and at the same time a tender Father who wants to give you much ... only rely on Him and do not be troubled by the circumstances of the turbulent world, and hold fast to His commandments, and He gives you a blessing and strength that remain with you forever.

Because of Sarah's great obedience and her trust in God in accompanying Abraham on the journey of faith from his departure from Ur of the Chaldees, the inspired text took care to mention her age, unlike the rest of the women in the Holy Bible: she lived 127 years, and she had borne Isaac at the age of ninety. For this reason the Fathers expect that Isaac's age when he was offered as a sacrifice had exceeded twenty-five or thirty, since his age at the death of his mother was 37 years.

Sarah died in the town of Arba, which was later called Hebron. It is in the south of the land of Canaan, near Beersheba. It seems that Abraham had gone out from Hebron to look after some of his work and his shepherds, and when he returned he found that Sarah had died. He grieved over her greatly, and wept and mourned for her, that is, he remembered all her virtues, her love, her companionship with him on the way of faith, and her bearing of many hardships. This is the first time it is mentioned that Abraham wept, because Sarah was the companion of his life, and this shows his love and esteem for her.

Care for the faithfulness and sincerity of those around you, praise them for it, and enjoy their love as long as they live with you, because they are an image of God's love offered to you, so let us thank Him for His gifts.
The sons of Heth: the sons of Heth were descendants of the son of Canaan; they became a great people called the Hittites and lived in the south of Canaan.

Abraham went to one of the cities of the Hittites that was near Hebron and entered their city. At the gate of the city there is a square, as is the custom of cities, where the leaders and judges of the city gather. So he went in to ask them for a place in which to bury Sarah, since he had not owned any place throughout his life, but moved about with his tent in the wilderness, he and his flocks.

Abraham declared to the sons of Heth that he was a stranger dwelling among them, despite his greatness and the abundance of his possessions. But he was humble and felt himself a stranger to the world because his heart was attached to heaven. And he asked them for a place in which to bury Sarah.

The sons of Heth showed their love for Abraham and their honor toward him, and said to him that his standing among them was that of a great prince, because they saw his wealth and the blessing of God that was with him. And they gladly agreed that he should bury Sarah in whichever of their tombs he chose.
The cave of Machpelah: that is, double, because it consists of two chambers, an inner and an outer.

Abraham bowed down in humility before the leaders of the people and those sitting in the square, and asked them that he might buy the cave of Machpelah, which lay at the edge of the field of one of the inhabitants of the city, Ephron the son of Zohar. Here Abraham's adherence to his faith appears: he did not bury Sarah in the land of his fathers in Iraq, because they were far from the worship of God, nor in one of the tombs of the Canaanites, the sons of Heth, because they were idolaters, but asked to buy a private burial place for his wife.

Ephron, the owner of the land and the cave, was sitting among those sitting in the square. He rose in the midst of those gathered and declared that he was offering his field and the cave in it as a gift to Abraham, with those sitting there as witnesses to it. This shows Ephron's generosity, Abraham's standing among the Hittites, and their effort to honor him.

Abraham confirmed his respect and humility by bowing down a second time before the Hittites, and asked Ephron, whom Abraham had not known personally before, to let him buy the field and the cave and not have it be a gift from him. For Abraham had lived as a stranger all his life and had owned nothing except a tomb, that is, death, and he believed God's promise of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which would be fulfilled for his children.
Four hundred shekels of silver: a shekel of silver is approximately 15 grams, and therefore four hundred shekels equal six kilograms of silver.

When Ephron saw Abraham's insistence on paying the price of the land, he accepted that he should buy it, declaring that the love between them was more important, and that if he wished to buy it, let it be as he wished.
Current money with the merchant: that is, pure silver approved by the merchants and all those dealing in buying and selling.

Abraham weighed out the silver, the price of the field, before the elders of the Hittites and gave it to Ephron, and thus Abraham came to own the field, the cave, and the trees that were in the field. So Abraham never owned any land throughout his life, and when he did own some, he owned a burial place, that is, estrangement from the world.

May you lift your eyes toward heaven and not be preoccupied with the possessions of the earth, because they pass away. And if you own anything, consider yourself a steward over it, managing it faithfully, so that you will give an account of it on the day of judgment, and use it to show love toward those around you and not for your selfishness and your own pleasures.

Finally Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah. Afterward Abraham himself was buried in the same cave, along with Isaac and Jacob; the bones of Joseph were also carried to it, and likewise Rebekah and Leah were buried in it. The marriage of Isaac

entries.section: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

paragraphs.text: Abraham grew old, and his age drew near to 140 years, because Sarah died when he was 137 years old, and after a period of about three years he thought of marrying his son Isaac. God's blessing upon him was great in possessions, in addition to the spiritual blessings.

entries.section: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

paragraphs.text: Abraham summoned the chief of his servants, Eliezer of Damascus, who was the manager of his possessions and affairs, and asked him to swear to him by putting his hand under Abraham's thigh ... but why?
1- Swearing by putting the hand under the thigh, near the place of circumcision, is an oath by the covenant of God, and by sonship and belonging to Him.
2- It is an oath by the offspring from whom Christ would come, so it is a great and certain oath.

entries.section: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

paragraphs.text: The oath that Abraham asked Eliezer to swear was that he would not choose a wife for his son Isaac from the Canaanite women who lived around him, but that Eliezer should go to Abraham's family living in Mesopotamia and choose a wife from there, because the Canaanite women were wicked and immersed in the worship of idols, while Abraham's clan, though they too were idolaters, were better than they in the knowledge of God.
And he did not send Isaac to choose a wife for himself, for the following reasons:
1- Lest his heart become attached and the wife influence him, so that he would settle with her in her land and abandon God's covenant of dwelling in Canaan.
2- It was the custom of the rich at that time to send their servants to choose wives for their sons.

entries.section: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

paragraphs.text: Eliezer asked Abraham whether, if he found a suitable girl as a wife and she refused to come to Canaan, he should take Isaac to her and settle with her in her land.

entries.section: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

paragraphs.text: Abraham answered his servant as follows:
1- He warned him against taking Isaac back to the land of his clan, but that he should remain in Canaan in obedience to God's commands.
2- He reassured him that God, whom he worshiped, would send His angel before him, choose the wife, and make the matter easy so that she would come with him to Canaan.
3- If no suitable girl was willing to come with him, he would be free from this oath.
So Eliezer, the chief of his house, swore to him, by putting his hand under his thigh, that he would go and choose a wife for Isaac from his clan and his family.

Be assured that God will help you to carry out His commandments, and do not worry about the surrounding circumstances and the opinion of people, for God persuades them and gives you grace in their eyes, so that you may remain firm in your faith and in your life with them.

entries.section: (2) The sign of the chosen wife

paragraphs.text: Aram-naharaim: a region lying in the north between the Tigris and the Euphrates rivers.

The city of Nahor: it lies near Haran, between the two rivers in the north, named after Nahor the grandfather of Abraham, or Nahor the brother of Abraham, who went there after Abraham left it and went to Canaan.
Eliezer took ten camels and loaded them with some of the goods of God, as a gift and dowry from his master for the wife whom he would choose.

Eliezer is a symbol of the Holy Spirit, who chooses for believers their wives and orders their lives. The number (10) signifies holding fast to God's ten commandments, and the goods signify the blessings of the Holy Spirit which He grants to His children. And the choice of a wife from the Gentiles for Isaac is a type of the acceptance of the Gentiles into faith in Christ.

entries.section: (2) The sign of the chosen wife

paragraphs.text: He made the camels kneel down: he made them couch, that is, kneel and rest.
Eliezer arrived at the city of Nahor and stood at a well outside the city. It was evening, the time when the girls go out to fill their jars, when the heat of the sun's rays has abated.
The well is a symbol of Baptism, and the evening time signifies God's love that visits us before the day ends.

entries.section: (2) The sign of the chosen wife

paragraphs.text: Eliezer, who had entered into the faith and been circumcised by Abraham, prayed. He asked God, interceding by Abraham, the beloved of God and His friend, to make it easy for him to reach the suitable girl. He also asked Him for a sign: that he needed to drink, he and the servants with him, and the camels. He would ask the girls who came out to draw water to give him water to drink, and if one of them agreed, and even offered greater love of her own accord by watering him and his camels and all who were with him, she would be the girl whom God had chosen. Thus the sign was overflowing love, or generosity in giving.
Your love for those around you and your care for everyone in need is the sign that shows your Christianity to all people, so care for everyone in need and do not turn away anyone who asks you.

Immediately after Eliezer finished his prayer, he found Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, coming out to draw water. God had granted her great beauty. When she reached the well she went down to it, since it was in a low place, filled her jar with water, and came up to return to her home.
Eliezer ran to her and asked her to give him a little water to drink, and weariness was evident on his face from the toil of the journey.
Rebekah responded quickly, lowered her jar from her shoulder, put it on her arm, and tilted it so that he might drink from it.

After Eliezer had drunk, Rebekah offered love of her own accord, without his asking her, namely to water his camels also, which she saw beside him, and of course she also watered the servants who were with him. This was proof of her generosity and her care for the hospitality of strangers.
The trough: a basin in which water is placed for the animals to drink from.
Rebekah emptied her jar into the trough, and went to the well and returned several times to fill the trough with water, so that all the camels drank.
Eliezer was looking at her intently, seeing the sign he had asked of God being quickly fulfilled before him, and perhaps he kept on praying within himself that God would complete His work.

How beautiful it is that you rely on prayer in ordering the affairs of your life! Trust that God rejoices in your prayers and answers quickly according to your faith. Continue in your prayer even if God's answer is delayed for a wisdom He sees, for He gives you at the right time what is for your good.

Eliezer was sure that this was the girl whom God had chosen, after the sign was fulfilled, for he had great faith like his master Abraham. So he hastened and put a golden ring in Rebekah's nose and two bracelets of gold on her hands, and asked her who she was and whether there was room and food in their house for him and the camels.
The girl told him that she was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor by his wife Milcah, and she welcomed his being hosted, along with his companions and camels.

Eliezer rejoiced greatly and bowed down before God and thanked Him, because in the greatness of His love He had guided him not only to one of the clan of his master Abraham, but to the granddaughter of his brother Nahor.
Rebekah ran to her home and told her mother and her brothers what had happened to her.

When Laban, Rebekah's brother, heard her words about Eliezer and what he had done for her, and saw the ring and the bracelets, he ran to Eliezer, who was still standing by the well, welcomed him, and called him "blessed of the Lord" to honor him, and invited him to enter the house, since he had ordered the servants to prepare a place to host him and those with him.

Eliezer entered the house and put his camels in the animals' enclosure, and they gave them water and food, and welcomed him and set a table before him that he might eat. But he said, "I will not eat until I have told my errand," that is, I have declared the mission for which I have come.

Eliezer himself made known to Laban and Rebekah's family that he was Abraham's servant, and explained to them the wealth and possessions to which his master had come, in servants, cattle, silver and gold, and that he had one only son, Isaac, who was the heir of all his possessions. And that Abraham had asked him to choose a wife for Isaac from his kindred and clan and bring her to Canaan, and that he had sworn to him to do so, but that if the wife was not willing to come to Canaan, he would be free from his oath.

He told them how he had asked God for a sign when he reached the well outside their city, namely that he would ask for water, and the girl who agreed to give him water to drink and then offered to water his camels also would be the girl chosen by God. When he had finished his prayer, Rebekah came, and the sign was fulfilled in her, and when he asked her who she was, she told him that she was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor. So he thanked God, who had guided him to the house of his master's brother, and bowed down to Him, and put the ring and the bracelets on Rebekah's nose and hands as a dowry for her. Then Eliezer asked Rebekah's family whether they agreed to give Rebekah to Isaac or not, so that he might go on his way.

It is good that you obey God's word and trust in Him, and even ask a sign from Him to strengthen your faith, for He is a tender God, long-suffering, who cares for you and rejoices in your prayers and makes your way easy so that you may live with Him.

Laban and his father Bethuel agreed to give Rebekah in marriage to Isaac, for they understood from the story that God was the one who had chosen her, so they could not oppose Him, and they gave Rebekah to be the wife of Isaac. We note that Laban is mentioned before his father Bethuel, either because of his old age or his illness, so he left his son to lead the situation.

Submission to God's will gives your life rest, because you feel that He is the leader and director of your affairs, and He therefore guarantees your rest and your peace. Be careful to understand God's dealings with you, and if you do not understand, lift up your heart with many prayers, and He will reveal and make clear to you His will.

Eliezer thanked God for the success of his mission and bowed down to Him, for he was a man of prayer and humility like his master. And he gave gifts to Rebekah and her family, represented by her brother and her mother, as a completion of her dowry, namely vessels of silver and gold, precious things, and garments.
Eliezer ate and drank and spent that night in joy, and in the morning he asked leave of Rebekah's family to take her and depart to Abraham.
Rebekah's family tried to have her stay with them some days so that they might enjoy her before she left them, and they asked Eliezer for this, that he stay with them for that period.

Eliezer begged Rebekah's family not to delay him from departing, since God had declared His will and chosen Rebekah. Her family said, "Let us ask her whether she agrees to depart quickly," and she agreed. We note the girl's freedom in accepting her bridegroom, which is the right of every girl.
Thousands of millions: tens of thousands.
Possess the gate of those who hate them: overcome his enemies.

They bade farewell to their sister and daughter Rebekah and wished for her that God would give her offspring who would be a great nation reaching tens of thousands, and that her offspring would be strong and overcome its enemies. And they gave Rebekah, as was the custom of that time, her nurse, who was called Deborah, and the two went with Eliezer and the servants who were with him to the land of Canaan.

Rebekah went out from her house, she and her maidservants whom her family had given her, and they rode on the camels, and the caravan set out, led by Eliezer of Damascus, from Haran to the land of Canaan.

Isaac was living in the south of the land of Canaan, and he had gone to look after the shepherds and the cattle at Beer-lahai-roi, where the angel appeared to Hagar and Ishmael (ch. 16:14). At evening, as he was returning to his tent, he went out into the field to spend a time of solitude and meditation on God, as some of the Jews of old were accustomed to do, and many monks do at present. He saw from afar a caravan of camels coming toward the place where he lived.

How beautiful it is to set aside a time to be alone with God every day, or at least every week, sitting by yourself in a quiet place, whether a secluded place, or before a wide view, or in a holy place, or before an icon of Christ, and thinking on a spiritual subject and reviewing your life, so that you enjoy a quiet meeting and your feelings go forth toward God.

Rebekah noticed a man coming toward them, and out of respect for him she got down from the camel and asked Eliezer of Damascus about him, and he said that he was Isaac. So out of modesty she covered her face with the veil, as was the custom of women at this time.

The caravan arrived and met Isaac, and Eliezer told him all that had happened and presented Rebekah to him. Isaac rejoiced in her and brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and married her, and was comforted over the departure of his mother by the love that grew with Rebekah and his new life with her. Three years had passed since the death of Sarah, and Isaac had reached forty years of age.
The death of Abraham, the birth of Jacob and Esau, and the sale of the birthright

Several years after the death of Sarah, Abraham married a concubine named Keturah and had six sons by her, and they in turn bore grandsons, some during Abraham's lifetime and others perhaps after his death. Despite the multitude of offspring that came from her, she added nothing to Abraham's life, but it was a human need, one that one wishes he had not had; yet the Holy Bible shows the great men of faith with all their weaknesses. Although he had been content with Sarah throughout his life, he became weak in his old age and needed to marry one of his maidservants. As for his marriage to his maidservant Hagar during Sarah's lifetime, it was not out of desire or need but to please Sarah and a mistaken attempt to carry out God's promise.
May you walk in self-restraint throughout your life, not only in marriage but in food, clothing and possessions, for the more you give them up, the more your heart is freed and is satisfied with God.
The concubines: the maidservants whom Abraham married, namely Hagar and Keturah.
The east country: the Arabian Peninsula and southern Iraq.

Abraham remembered God's word about sending Ishmael away and giving the inheritance to Isaac alone, so he gave gifts to his sons by Keturah and sent them away, and they went east, and Isaac remained alone in Canaan. He thus became Abraham's only heir, not only in material gifts but rather in faith and the love of God. This is a type of the inheritance of the Kingdom, which Christ gave to His Church, which alone received the glad tidings of Him.

Abraham lived in faith and in a righteous life pleasing to God throughout his life, and died at the age of 175. He had gone out from Haran, which lies between the Tigris and the Euphrates rivers, at the age of 75 and gone to Canaan; then he fathered Ishmael at the age of 86, and after that he fathered Isaac at the age of one hundred; Sarah died when he had reached 137; when Jacob and Esau were born he was 160; and at his death Ishmael had reached 89 years and Isaac 75 years, while Isaac's sons, Jacob and Esau, were 15 years old.

When Abraham died, all his neighbors heard of it. Ishmael was living near Mamre, where Abraham died, and perhaps Isaac sent for him, so he came and joined him in burying him in the cave of Machpelah beside Sarah. As for Abraham's sons by Keturah, they lived far away and did not attend the burial of their father.

Isaac lived at Beer-lahai-roi, where the angel appeared to Hagar (ch. 16:14), and lived in the faith of his father Abraham. He took care to live in this blessed place where the angel of God had appeared, and God blessed him spiritually and materially.

Take care to cling to spiritual places and spiritual people, so that this may help you to remember God and be encouraged on His way, and not be carried along with the current of the world and its dazzling means of advertising, so that God may bless you and appear always in your life.
We note that Abraham is a type of Christ in the following:
1- Abraham left his family and his kindred in Ur of the Chaldees and obeyed God, and Christ left His glory in heaven and humbled Himself, becoming incarnate, in obedience to the Father.
2- Abraham lived throughout his life detached, in a tent, and owned nothing but a tomb, and Christ lived poor, having nowhere to lay His head, even to death, the death of the Cross.
3- Abraham built an altar in every place he went to and offered sacrifices, and Christ lifted up His prayer to the Father and offered Himself as a sacrifice of love on the Cross.
4- Abraham fled to Egypt and blessed it, and Christ fled to Egypt and blessed it.

5- Abraham triumphed over Chedorlaomer and all who were with him and brought back the captives, and Christ triumphed over Satan and bound him on the Cross, and brought out those held captive in Hades and raised them up to Paradise.
6- Abraham obeyed God and offered the dearest thing he had, Isaac his beloved son, as a sacrifice, and Christ obeyed the Father and offered His life on the Cross.
We can summarize the life of our father Abraham in the following points:
1- God's call to Abraham and his going out from Ur of the Chaldees with his wife Sarai, his father Terah and his brother's son Lot, and their going to Haran (ch. 11:31), (Acts 7:2).
2- God called Abraham a second time, and he went out from Haran and went to Canaan, and He promised him blessing. (ch. 12:1)
3- His journeys in Canaan. (ch. 12)
4- His going to Egypt. (ch. 12)
5- His parting from Lot. (ch. 13)
6- His victory over Chedorlaomer and the bringing back of the captives. (ch. 14)
7- His meeting with Melchizedek. (ch. 14)
8- God's appearance to him and His confirmation of the promise to him. (ch. 15)
9- His marriage to Hagar and the birth of Ishmael. (ch. 16)
10- God's covenant with him when He appeared to him among the divided animals, and His giving him the covenant of circumcision. (ch. 17)
11- God and the two angels as his guests, and the promise of Isaac. (ch. 18)
12- His intercession for Sodom and Gomorrah. (ch. 18)
13- His going to Gerar. (ch. 20)
14- The birth of Isaac, his weaning, and the casting out of Hagar and Ishmael. (ch. 21)
15- His offering of Isaac as a sacrifice. (ch. 22)
16- The death of his wife Sarah. (ch. 23)
17- The choosing of Rebekah as a wife for his son Isaac. (ch. 24)
18- His death and burial in the cave of Machpelah. (ch. 25)

Ishmael fathered 12 sons, whom the Holy Bible lists in order according to the years of their birth. They became chiefs of tribes that lived in the Arabian Peninsula, and some of them extended northward as far as Damascus and Iraq and took possession of the lands there and had many cattle, because God blessed them in number and possessions as He had promised Abraham, for they are his offspring, even if they did not live attached to him so as to live in his faith. Some of them formed famous tribes, such as Nebajoth, from whom came the Nabateans mentioned in the First Book of Maccabees (1 Macc 5:25; 9:35), who lived in the region between the Gulf of Aqaba and the Euphrates. Also Kedar, whose name means black, and whose tribe is mentioned in (Song 1:5), and from him came Geshem the Arabian who opposed Nehemiah (Neh 2:19), and from him the tribe of Quraysh came forth.
Havilah: it lies west of the Persian Gulf.
Shur: it lies southwest of Palestine.
Asshur: it includes all the lands from the Mediterranean Sea to the east of the Tigris River.
Ishmael, with his various tribes, lived in the north of the Arabian Peninsula, and some of his tribes extended into the region of Syria and Palestine. Ishmael lived to the age of 137 and then died.

If God blesses you and gives you material good things or offspring of renown, do not be preoccupied by this away from God, but use it to reach Him and thank Him for His blessings, for the aim of all God's gifts is to bind your heart to Him, so that you may enjoy a living faith and have a place in heaven.

entries.section: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

paragraphs.text: Padan-aram: the plain between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, now called the land of the Jazirah, and Aram was one of the descendants of Shem.
Isaac married, at the age of 40, Rebekah the daughter of Bethuel and sister of Laban, who lived in Padan-aram, and Eliezer of Damascus brought her to Canaan.

entries.section: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

paragraphs.text: Rebekah remained barren for 20 years, and Isaac's faith was not shaken, but he continued to pray, confident of God's promise, until she conceived.

Hold fast to the promises of God, who keeps you in all your ways and blesses your life, and be persistent with Him in prayer however long the time, that He may solve your problems, for He waits for the right time and gives you an opportunity for your faith to grow, but He never forgets you.

entries.section: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

paragraphs.text: Why am I thus: she was distressed by the pains of the movement of the babes and came near to death, so a feeling of despair attacked her and she said, why is my life, which is an expression of her distress at the severity of the pain.
She went to inquire of the Lord: she lifted up her heart in prayer, or went to the altar that her husband Isaac had built and prayed to God.

The time of delivery drew near, and Rebekah felt a crowding or struggle in her womb and suffered much, and in the extremity of her distress she hastened to God, asking Him to deliver her from these pains, perhaps fearing that she would die or that the one in her womb would die.

entries.section: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

paragraphs.text: Since her prayer was fervent, God reassured her and told her that she would give birth in peace and that she and the one in her womb would live; indeed He gave her the good news that she would bear two sons, each of whom would become a great people, and He also informed her that the offspring of the elder son would be enslaved to the offspring of the younger son. By this He means God's blessing upon the offspring of Jacob, who came to the Promised Land and killed the wicked original inhabitants of the land and took possession of their land.

entries.section: (4) The birth of Jacob and Esau

paragraphs.text: Esau: the name means rough or hairy, and he was surnamed Edom, that is, red.

At the birth a red child came out of her womb, and they called him Esau, and his body was covered with hair. Then the second son came out holding the heel of his brother, and they called him Jacob, that is, he holds, because he took hold of his heel. Rebekah rejoiced, and so did Isaac, who was then sixty years old.

The two boys grew and became young men. Esau worked at hunting wild beasts and lived in a moving tent in the wilderness, searching for the wild animals that abound in these regions in order to hunt them. As for Jacob, he worked at shepherding sheep and also lived in a tent, and was distinguished by meekness and a life of faith, so the Holy Bible called him perfect for his care for the spiritual life.

Isaac felt Esau's strength, which appeared in his courage and his hunting of wild beasts, so he loved him and preferred him to Jacob. But Rebekah the mother loved Jacob because of his righteousness and meekness and preferred him to Esau.

Esau went out on a hunting trip in which he exerted great effort running after the wild beasts, and when he returned to his tent very weary, he found his brother Jacob, who was then living next to him, cooking red lentils, that is, yellow tending toward red, and its smell was pleasant, while Esau was in great fatigue and hunger.

When Esau smelled the lentils and saw them with his eyes, he longed to eat of them and asked his brother Jacob for them. His asking for the red lentils was another reason for Esau being called Edom, not only because his skin tended toward red but also because of his asking for the lentils, whose color tends toward red.

Jacob took advantage of his brother's need for food and showed him his readiness to give him some of the lentils on condition that he sell him his birthright, because Esau was the one who came out first from his mother's womb, so he was the firstborn, and the birthright meant:
1- That he would act for his father in his absence in the headship of the family.
2- That he would receive a greater share of the inheritance at the death of the father.

3- In the days of Jacob the head of the family used to offer sacrifices on behalf of his family, that is, he was the priest of the family, and in the absence of the father the firstborn acted for his father in this priestly work.

This conduct of Jacob was not sound, for he took advantage of his brother's need for food, and perhaps he also realized Esau's disregard for spiritual meanings, so he asked him to sell him his birthright.

Esau despised the spiritual blessing of the birthright and said, I am about to die of hunger, so what importance has the birthright? Give me food, for it is more important than the birthright. This conduct too was very wrong.

May you care for the spiritual opportunities that God has given you, such as a church near you, a priest before whom you can confess, and your ability to read the Holy Bible and the Agpeya so as to pray and meditate; indeed seize every spiritual opportunity, in a meeting or a trip, to cling to God and grow in His love, and do not sell these opportunities because of what you call the occupations of life.
Jacob asked Esau for a confirmation of the sale of his birthright, namely an oath, and he swore to him. Thus he sold the great birthright for the cheapest thing, a mere meal of lentils.

Jacob gave his brother bread and lentils, and he ate and enjoyed the food and did not care about the birthright; rather, by this conduct he despised it, so it was lost to him, and he lost the salvation of his soul and all his faith, and formed a people alien to the faith, the people of Edom.
Isaac sojourns in Gerar

A famine occurred a second time in the south of Canaan, other than the first famine that occurred in the days of Abraham, because of which he went down to the land of Egypt. So Isaac moved from Beer-lahai-roi to Gerar, which lies southeast of Gaza at a distance of 5 miles from it, and Abimelech reigned over it, which is a title of the kings of Gerar.

God warned him against going down to Egypt, and it seems that Isaac had prayed to God, who commanded him to remain in Canaan, the land that was promised to Abraham, and that He was able to provide for him and keep him in it, and he did not need to go down to Egypt, lest he be exposed to troubles as his father Abraham was. And He renewed His promise to him of blessing and many offspring in the land of Canaan for the sake of Abraham his father, so he obeyed and dwelt in Gerar.

Take care to cling to the righteous, the pious children of God, so that you receive their blessing in your life, and seek the intercession of the saints, so that God sees your love for them and blesses your life.

Isaac feared for himself that the people of the place would kill him and take from him his beautiful wife Rebekah, so he lied and said that she was his sister, and thus fell into the same sin as his father and did not learn from what had happened to him.

When you see the faults of others, do not hasten to condemn them, but rather take heed yourself lest you fall into the same faults, and know that we are all subject to weakness and exposed to sin, and the wise man is the one who learns from everyone, even from the wicked.

Isaac lived for a time in Gerar and pitched his tent near the palace of its king, who was called Abimelech, because it was the title of all the kings of Gerar, and he was probably a different king from the one in the days of Abraham. One day Abimelech looked out of the window of his palace and saw Isaac in his tent caressing Rebekah as a husband with his wife, so he understood that she was his wife and not his sister.

Abimelech summoned Isaac and confronted him with his lie about Rebekah, and he admitted it but justified his sin by his fear that the people of the place would kill him and take his wife. This sin is not only a lie but an evil suspicion of the people of Gerar, whose fear of doing evil appears, as will be shown in the following verses.

Abimelech reproached him for his lie, because by it he exposed one of the men of Gerar to falling into the sin of marrying Rebekah as his sister, and thus falling into evil without knowing it, so that through this sin of his all the people of Gerar would have become guilty, and all this because of Isaac's negligence and his lie.

Abimelech was firm, and despite Isaac's sin he issued an order in all his city declaring that Rebekah was Isaac's wife, so that no one should try to think of her as a wife for himself or come near her, and whoever tried that would be put to death.

Although Isaac had sinned by his lie, he was still distinguished by his faith in God, in which he was unique in all the world, so God forgave him after his repentance and his acceptance of Abimelech's rebuke of him. And when he sowed a piece of land in the region of Gerar, God gave him an abundance in his harvest beyond all imagination, a hundredfold the usual harvest of that time, and He also blessed his sheep so they multiplied greatly, and thus he became the richest man in Gerar and owned many servants. The people of Gerar envied him for his rapid greatness and his superiority over them.

The people of Gerar expressed their anger and envy toward Isaac by stopping up the wells that Abraham had dug when he lived among them, which are considered the property of his son Isaac. So that he should not use them and increase in his wealth, they stopped them up, that is, they kept water from them, hoping that he would leave them. And since he stayed and bore these bad actions, Abimelech was compelled to ask him to depart from them, because he had become mightier than they, and might gain mastery over them or rule them.

God's blessing surpasses all understanding, for although Isaac was a stranger and in weakness, God blessed him, so he became stronger than the original inhabitants. Trust in the power of God that is with you, and He will bless you more than all who are around you and give you peace, so that others will fear you.
Isaac the peaceable moved from Gerar to a region near it called the valley of Gerar, a few miles away from it.

Isaac was not troubled by the envy of the Philistines and their stopping up of the wells that Abraham had dug, which were considered his property, but positively, when he found some of these wells in the valley of Gerar, he began to dig them out, that is, to remove the earth and stones that the Philistines, the people of Gerar, had thrown into them. He knew their places, whether from his father or from the servants who had helped his father and were still alive, or from their sons.

Isaac found one of the wells that Abraham had dug and removed the earth that was on it, and it again gave water. When the Philistines found this, they rose against him and claimed ownership of this well, so he left it to them for the sake of peace and called this well Esek, that is, strife.

Isaac did not despair and continued his positive work, and a new well appeared from among the wells that Abraham had dug, but the Philistines also rose against him and claimed that this well was theirs, so Isaac gave it up also for the sake of peace and called this well Sitnah, that is, contention.

Isaac continued his search for water and was not hindered by the harassment of his wicked neighbors, and a third well appeared. Since God saw his perseverance and his love, He made the Philistines leave him alone and not seize this well, so Isaac rejoiced and called this well Rehoboth, that is, God has made room for us and enabled us to settle and be fruitful in the broad land, and he thanked God.

After this he moved to Beersheba, where Abraham had lived for a time after he had dug the well there and given the seven ewe lambs to Abimelech as proof of Abraham's ownership of it. God appeared to him in this blessed place and renewed to him the covenant of blessing, so that he would not be troubled by the harassment of the wicked and would trust that God was with him. So he built an altar and thanked God, and also dug a well in this place and settled there for a time, pasturing his flock.

Isaac, while living in the valley of Gerar, was surprised by the coming of Abimelech king of Gerar, with his friend or counselor Ahuzzath and Phichol the captain of his army. As we have said before, Abimelech is a title of the kings of Gerar and Phichol is a title of the commanders of the armies of Gerar, and they were probably different from the two who were in the days of Abraham.

Isaac wondered at their coming to him while they showed him love and friendliness, and asked them, how is it that you drove me away from you, and now you have come to me and speak to me with friendliness and love?
