Abimelech and those with him acknowledged that the power of God and His blessing that was with Isaac made them fear him, and they came to him asking for a treaty of peace with him, so that he would not harm them.

Abimelech reminded him that although they had driven him away, they had not seized from him his wife or anything of his possessions ... and they asked for a covenant of peace and a treaty of peace between them because they felt that he was blessed by God.

Isaac's heart, broad with love, appeared when he made them a feast, that is, a table, and they ate and rested with him, and made a treaty of peace that neither would harm the other, and they swore to it and then departed from him.

Let your heart be broad with love toward everyone, even those who have wronged you, so that you forgive them and show them love and do not fear them, because God is with you and keeps you in all your ways, so you remain firm in your peace and your love.

Isaac's servants cleaned out the well that Abraham had dug in that place, or dug a new well, and it brought forth water, and they told Isaac their master, who rejoiced and confirmed the name of the place, calling it Beersheba (map 7).
His eyes were dim: his eyes were weary, that is, he had almost lost his sight.
Your quiver: the pouch or case in which the arrows are placed.

Isaac advanced in age and reached about 130 years, so he summoned his firstborn son Esau and said to him, I am old and the day of my death is near, so go and hunt an animal and prepare it as food for me, that you may show your love toward me, and I will eat and give you the blessing of the birthright before I depart from this life.

Although Isaac knew God's word that the elder would serve the younger, and had heard that Esau had sold his birthright for a meal of lentils to his brother Jacob, and was also troubled by his marriage to the wicked daughters of Heth, his fatherhood and his love for Esau moved him to give him the blessing, since he was the firstborn. Isaac could have been more self-restrained and blessed him without asking for food; rather, it would have been more fitting for him to pray first and seek God's guidance before proceeding to give the blessing to Esau.

It is good that you give gifts and help to your children and all those around you, but you need to pray first so that God may guide you, so as not to distress anyone while you are giving to another, and so that you may be just and doing God's will, meet the needs of those most in need and show love to all. Then you will not be troubled by opposing opinions, since you have no personal aim except carrying out God's will.
Rebekah was standing near Isaac when he spoke to his son Esau to prepare food for him and bring it to him, and she saw that Esau had gone out to hunt game and present it to his father.
Rebekah called her son Jacob and told him what Isaac had said to Esau, that is, that he should bring him food to eat, and then he would bless him.

She gave her son Jacob the advice that he should hasten to slaughter two kids from his flock and bring them to her, and she would prepare from them the foods that she knew his father loved, and he would go in with them to his father and pretend that he was Esau and take the blessing instead of him. Although Jacob was a perfect man living a life of righteousness and deserved the blessing according to God's promise, it was not right for Rebekah to use wrong methods to reach the blessing, but she should have left it to God, believing that He was able to give him the blessing in a sound way.

Jacob agreed in principle to the lying and the deceiving of his father, but he presented to his mother a problem, namely that his brother was hairy and he was smooth, so if his father touched him he would discover his deceit and be angry with him and curse him, and he would receive not a blessing but a curse.

Rebekah said to her son, Do not fear your father's curse, for it is on me. This is a strange saying without meaning, because a curse is not transferred from one person to another, but it is an attempt by the mother to encourage her son to the sin of deceit, and she considered the matter hers and not her son's, so she said to him, Fetch me two kids, and not, Fetch yourself two kids.

However good your aim may be, be careful in choosing the right means, and beware of encouraging another to sin, lest you and he fall into it, because all material gains are worthless in comparison with disobeying God.
Jacob brought the two kids to his mother, and she prepared from them many dishes of the kind Isaac loved.

Rebekah brought some of Esau's clothes that were in the big house, not those at his wives' homes, and put them on Jacob. Usually a person's smell, that is, the smell of his sweat together with the pleasant scents he is accustomed to using, is apparent in his clothes, so that if Isaac smelled him he would not doubt. She put goatskins on Jacob's hands and on his neck, so he became hairy like his brother Esau, and he took the food and went in to his father and called to him.

Jacob said to his father, I am Esau your son; arise, eat of my game and bless me. Isaac wondered at the speed of Esau's coming and said to him, How were you able to hunt and cook the food so quickly? Jacob said to him, Your God made everything easy for me. This was a spiritual answer that Esau was not accustomed to giving because of his distance from God, which increased Isaac's doubt.

Isaac asked his son to come near to him and touched his hands and found them hairy, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the feel of the hands appears to be Esau's, because the voices of twins, however close, and however much one tries to imitate the other, will have a difference. Then he asked him again to make sure that he was his son Esau, and Jacob answered, Yes. Isaac found nothing before him but to ask for the food and eat, and then he drank wine.

After he had eaten, he wanted to make sure one last time, so he asked his son to come near to him and kiss him as a sign of showing love, but in truth he wanted to smell him, and he found the smell to be Esau's, because Jacob was wearing the clothes of his brother Esau. Then Isaac pronounced the blessing and said that the smell of his son was like the smell of a field that the Lord had blessed, and wished him fields that would give many crops with a fragrant smell by God's blessing.

He also asked for him a blessing from heaven, namely the dew and the rains to water his crops, and likewise he asked God for him fertility in the earth to make his crops grow, and then asked for him abundance of corn and grain, and also wine, by which is meant all the fruits of the earth. The word wine here in the original also means fresh wine, that is, the fruits of the earth and not fermented grape juice.

He also gave him the blessing that he would rule over his brothers and have dominion over many peoples, and everyone who loved and blessed him would receive a blessing from God, while whoever opposed and cursed him, God would curse him, that is, he would lose every blessing. These blessings are material, and Jacob received them at different times, such as God's blessing on his flocks with Laban, God's blessing on his possessions when he returned to Canaan, and the good things he received in Egypt in the days of Joseph, in addition to his offspring's taking possession of the Promised Land. But with these blessings he also met tribulations, so that God might raise us to the spiritual blessing, which is the most important, with the coming of Christ from his offspring, who offers salvation and blessing to the whole world, and the world is made subject (to Christ) through faith.
Thus Jacob received the blessing, but he fell into the sins of stealing, lying and deceit.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: After Jacob had received the blessing from his father Isaac and departed, Esau arrived with his game and prepared his food, and went in to his father and asked him to arise and eat.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: Isaac asked him, Who are you? and he answered that he was his son Esau. Isaac was agitated and troubled and asked, Who is it who came to me and told me that he was Esau, so that I ate of his food and blessed him? And he will indeed be blessed, and the blessing will not be taken away from him.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: Esau grieved at this unfortunate surprise, for he had lost his blessing, so he cried out with a great voice to express his unbearable distress. Then Isaac answered him sorrowfully that Jacob had come and stolen the blessing. Esau was enraged and said that it was Jacob who had supplanted him and taken his birthright, and now for the second time he had taken his blessing; then he asked his father to give him some blessing. Sadly, Esau's concern was for the material blessing only and not the spiritual, and he did not regret in his heart his despising of the birthright, nor did he repent before God, but all his concern was in obtaining material things.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: Isaac said to Esau, Jacob has taken the whole blessing, for he has received dominion over his brothers and the material blessings of the fruits of the earth, expressed by the corn and wine.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: Esau said to his father, Have you but one blessing? ... Bless me, even me also, and he wept; but this was not the weeping of repentance but grief at the loss of material things, and of course he had no thought of the spiritual blessing, which is indeed one, because it is fulfilled in Christ, who comes from the offspring of Jacob.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: Isaac assured Esau that he would be without the blessing, so he would not receive blessings from heaven, expressed by the dew, nor from the earth, that is, its fertility.

entries.section: (3) Esau is deprived of the blessing

paragraphs.text: By your sword you shall live: he will enter into many wars.
Have the dominion: the disobedience of an animal toward the one who leads it, meaning the revolt and rebellion of the offspring of Esau against the offspring of Jacob.
His yoke: the crosspiece of wood placed on the necks of the animals that pull agricultural implements, meaning the rejection of the dominion of the offspring of Jacob over him.

He also prophesied to Esau that he would be fierce, inclined to war, and that his brother Jacob would have dominion over him, but that he would sometimes revolt against Jacob and prevail over him. The offspring of Jacob took possession of the land of Canaan and Edom, the offspring of Esau, was subject to them, but at times it rebelled and fought the people of Israel.

Do not despise the blessing when it is available to you, lest you ask for it at another time and not find it, and do not despise the opportunity of a lifetime for repentance before the day of judgment comes and all opportunities are lost to you.

Esau bore a grudge against his brother Jacob because he had received all the blessings while he was deprived of them, and because his thinking was entirely material he thought in a human way, namely to kill him so that he himself would receive all the blessings, not knowing that the blessings are spiritual in essence and are from God, before whom he cannot stand or whom he cannot oppose. But God put it in his heart to fear his father Isaac, so he postponed the matter until Isaac should die and his mourning, that is, his funeral, be completed, and then kill his brother.
Comforting himself: he calms himself temporarily concerning you until a suitable time comes in which to kill you.

Rebekah heard of Esau's resolve to kill his brother, so she told Jacob of this and advised him to flee to her brother Laban in Haran, which is between the two rivers in Iraq, and to stay there a short while until Esau's anger subsided, and then she would send and fetch him.

On the other hand, she told Isaac how distressed she was by Esau's pagan wives, the daughters of Heth, and her fear that Jacob would take a wife from among them, and her wish that he would marry from the daughters of her people. Isaac agreed, who had begun to feel the fulfillment of God's word and Jacob's right to the blessing.

Rebekah carried out what she and Jacob wanted, but she lost the presence of her son beside her and the distress of her other son with her and with his brother. As for Jacob, he bore much suffering, whether from Laban his uncle, or from his sons when they killed the men of Shechem, or his loss of Joseph ... all this God permitted as discipline for repentance. As for Rebekah, she is not mentioned in the Holy Bible after that, so it is understood that she died before Jacob returned to Canaan after 20 years, without seeing him.

Do not rush toward material gains or to carry out your will, however good it may seem, and seek God before every deed and think well, so that Satan does not exploit your impulsiveness and make you fall into sins foreign to you.
Here we summarize the life of Isaac as the Holy Bible relates it, as follows:
1- The birth of Isaac, the son of the promise (ch. 21)
2- The offering of Isaac as a sacrifice (ch. 22)
3- The choosing of Rebekah as a wife for Isaac (ch. 24)
4- Isaac fathers Esau and Jacob (ch. 25)
5- Isaac's sojourn in Gerar and his digging out of the wells of water (ch. 26)
6- Jacob steals the blessing from Isaac (ch. 27)
7- The death of Isaac (ch. 35) Jacob's ladder

Isaac summoned his son Jacob to bid him farewell and give him a parting charge before his journey. This shows Isaac's love for Jacob and his faith that the divine promises were being fulfilled in him, so he said to him, Do not marry any of the pagan, wicked Canaanite women among whom you live.

He also charged him to travel to the region of Padan-aram, which lies between the two rivers in the north, where his mother's family lives, his grandfather Bethuel and his uncle Laban, and to take a wife for himself from the daughters of his uncle.

He asked for Jacob that God would bless him with many offspring, and that his offspring would be a blessing to all peoples. This was fulfilled not in the people of Israel as a people proclaiming faith in God among the pagans, but rather in Christ, who offers salvation and blessing to the whole world.
He wished for him the fulfillment of God's promises to Abraham of the inheritance of the land of Canaan and the possession of it.
After that Jacob departed and traveled on his way from Canaan to Haran, where his uncle Laban lived.
Care for the advice of your parents and those responsible for you, for it is a message from God that helps you to a life of righteousness, so that you are joined to God and live uprightly.

Jacob went on his way from Beersheba in the south of Canaan, the land of the Philistines, to Haran, which lies in the north of Iraq, where his uncle Laban lived (map 8). After he had grown weary walking all day, he rested in a secluded place in the desert, because the sun had set and it was not possible to travel at night. He felt fear of being pursued by his brother Esau, who could kill him, and he also felt loneliness and estrangement in the wilderness and the loss of his parents' care and his well-equipped tent. From weariness he slept on the ground, and took a stone and made it a pillow for his head and slept there in this extreme poverty, and nothing remained to him but his faith in God. This stone is a type of Christ, the cornerstone on which we build all our life.

When things grow narrow for you and you lose much of what you lean on of material things and human relationships, know that God is then nearest to you, so seek Him and lean on Him, and you will find your rest.
He saw in a dream a ladder rising from the earth to heaven, and angels ascending and descending on it.

This ladder is a type of the Cross of Christ, on which the angels ascend, praising God for His redemption of mankind, and descend from it to proclaim the glad tidings of Christ the Redeemer to the world so that they may believe in Him. By this ladder, that is, the Cross, believers are raised to heaven, while those who reject it go down to Hades.
The ladder is also a type of the Virgin Mary, through whose Son we are raised to heaven and proclaim His name to the world.

Jacob heard the voice of God from above the ladder, who declared to him that He was the God of Abraham and Isaac his fathers, who had given them the promises, and now He was confirming His promise with him also, that He would give him the land on which he lay. He means the whole land of Canaan as He promised Abraham, and He would bless his offspring so that it would be very many like the dust of the earth, and keep him on his way to his uncle and bring him back to his land and never leave him, and in his offspring all the peoples of the earth would be blessed, that is, in Christ who comes from his offspring.
The meaning of until at the end of (v. 15) is not a particular time after which God would leave him, but that He would not leave him throughout his life and would fulfill all His promises to him.

When Jacob awoke from his sleep he was sure that this dream was a true revelation from God and that God was with him in this place, so he felt reverence, holiness and joy before Him, and declared that since God was in this place, it was His house, because the house of God is the place of His meeting with man, indeed it is the gate of heaven. This is the first clear reference to the Church, the house of God.
Jacob took the stone on which he had slept and set it up as a pillar and poured oil on it.

The stone, as we mentioned, is a type of Christ, the Rock of ages, and the oil is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the pouring of the oil means the consecration of the stone and the place, declaring that it is the place of God. He called the place Bethel, that is, the house of God, while the city near this place, which was called Bethel, was formerly called Luz because of the abundance of almond trees in it.

In view of God's care for Jacob and His appearing to him on the ladder, Jacob promised that if God kept him on his way to Haran and brought him back to the land of Canaan in which he had been living, and provided for his needs of food and clothing, he would do three things:

1- That he would continue to worship God throughout his life. The importance of this matter appears because Jacob and his father and mother were the only ones in the whole world at that time who worshiped God.
2- That he would build an altar to God in this place, and Bethel would become God's place for His worship.
3- That he would give God a tenth of the possessions that He gave him.
How beautiful it is that you make promises to God on every occasion, so that you may live with Him and be joined to Him by various spiritual means, which encourage you to spiritual growth.
Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel
Then Jacob lifted up his feet: he hastened on his way.
The land of the people of the east: the region of the Tigris and the Euphrates, which lies east of Canaan.
After Jacob was reassured, since God had appeared to him on the ladder, his spirit revived and he hastened on his way toward Mesopotamia, where his uncle Laban lived.

Jacob reached a field near the city of Haran, the city of Laban, which lies between the two rivers, and he found a well and three flocks of sheep waiting there with their shepherds, and on the well was a great stone covering it. They used to put it there to keep the water of the well from dust, and because it was large a group of shepherds would gather to roll away the stone and then water the flocks. When Jacob reached the shepherds, he asked them about Laban and how he was, and they said, We know him, and he is well. He asked them the reason for their waiting, and they said, Until all the flocks are gathered, so that it will be easy for us to roll the stone away. Then they told him that Rachel, Laban's daughter, was coming from afar with the sheep that she kept.

When Jacob finished speaking with the shepherds, Rachel had reached the well with the sheep of her father Laban, and Jacob rejoiced greatly at seeing her, so much so that he went up to the well and rolled away the heavy stone, alone or with the help of the waiting shepherds, and went forward and watered the flock of his uncle Laban. As for Rachel, she was looking with wonder at this man who cared for her and her sheep.

Jacob is a type of Christ, Rachel of the Church, and the well of Baptism, while the waiting flocks are a type of the world awaiting Christ the Savior. For Christ rolled away the stone, that is, the barrier of sin between Himself and mankind, and renewed His Church through Baptism, which became an image of the redeemed before the whole world, to draw them toward salvation.
Her father's brother: a nephew, whether sister's or brother's son, was sometimes called a brother.
My bone and my flesh: my relative, so you have the right of hospitality.

Jacob told Rachel that he was the son of her father's sister Rebekah and kissed her with joy, and she was delighted and ran to her home to tell her father of the arrival of Jacob from the land of Canaan.

When Laban heard of the arrival of the son of his sister Rebekah, he hastened to him, kissed him, and welcomed him into his house. Jacob told Laban all the events of their life in Canaan, their works and their possessions, and how he had a brother named Esau, and how he had taken the birthright and the blessing from him, so that Esau bore a grudge against him, which forced him to flee to Haran. His uncle reassured him and rejoiced in hosting him for a month, during which he helped his uncle in tending the sheep and all the work required.

As long as God is with you, He guides you in all your steps and gives you grace in the eyes of all, and even gives you strength to carry out His will, so be reassured and trust in Him and enjoy His presence with you.

Jacob was working diligently to help his uncle without wages, for mere food that he ate, and after a month had passed and Jacob had settled in tending the sheep, Laban asked him what wages he wanted to take from him.

Jacob loved Rachel, the younger daughter of Laban, and wanted to marry her, and since he had no possessions or money to give as a dowry to her father, he proposed to his uncle that he would serve him for free for seven years, and his wages during this period would be given as a dowry to marry Rachel. Laban accepted, declaring that it was better to give her to him because he was his relative and surer than strangers, especially as he had lived with him for a month and knew his character.

Jacob worked tending the sheep of his uncle Laban for seven years with all care and diligence, and did not complain of the length of the period or the amount of effort he exerted, but felt that it was the least he could offer as a dowry for Rachel whom he loved.

If you love God, you will accept toil for His sake in many prayers and fasts, and even service for His holy name, and you will see that the toil is sweet because it is a response to the divine love poured out on the Cross, so you will strive to please God whatever the cost and sacrifice, and press upon all your circumstances to be with Him.

entries.section: (3) Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel

paragraphs.text: Laban's exploitation of Jacob appears here. After waiting a month, he used Jacob in his service under the name of hospitality and then fixed his wages; now seven years pass, and we do not know whether the one who fixed them was Jacob or his uncle Laban. It is of course a long period and its wages great, since marriages did not then require expenses other than a tent and simple furniture. But in any case, at the end of the seven years Laban did not give his daughter to Jacob until he demanded it of him, so he was trying to exploit him as much as he could.

Take care not to exploit others, however weak they are or difficult their circumstances, and however great your authority, because God the Almighty sees you and is grieved by your greed. On the contrary, the more generous you are, the more God honors you, and the more you exploit, the more God deprives you of His blessings.

entries.section: (3) Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel

paragraphs.text: Laban made a wedding feast and invited his neighbors to rejoice with him at the marriage of his daughter to Jacob, and when night fell Laban gave his daughter Leah to Jacob and gave her a maidservant named Zilpah. So Jacob went in with his bride to the tent that Laban had prepared for them. The bride covered her face with a red veil, and because of the similarity of the voice and the darkness inside the tent, Jacob did not know who was with him and thought she was Rachel.

entries.section: (3) Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel

paragraphs.text: In the morning, in the light of day, Jacob discovered that the one he had married was Leah and not Rachel, and he was very distressed and hastened to reproach Laban for deceiving him. He excused himself by saying that it was not proper, according to the custom of the place where they lived, for the younger to marry before the elder, so he had been compelled to give him Leah. He then made a proposal, exploiting Jacob's love for Rachel and showing Laban's material greed, offering Jacob to complete a week of feasting with Leah as was the custom of that time, and then give him Rachel, on condition that he serve him another seven years for free as a dowry for the second wife.
Thus, as Jacob deceived his father and took the blessing, so also Laban deceived him, that God might make him taste the bitterness of deceit so that he would turn away from it.

When God permits you tribulations or wrongs from others, do not complain, but examine yourself to know your sins, which deserve far more than these tribulations, and in proportion to your submission to God's will and your acceptance of the tribulation, God will reveal to you many benefits of the tribulation.

entries.section: (3) Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel

paragraphs.text: After the week of marriage with Leah was completed, Jacob married Rachel, and her father also gave her a maidservant named Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah and served another seven years to complete the dowry, that is, he served 14 years for free to marry Rachel his beloved.

Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, which caused Leah distress, and this is one of the problems of polygamy, which disappeared in Christianity, and perhaps her distress was increased because she had agreed with her father in deceiving him. In any case, God felt her suffering and compensated her with children, while God withheld Rachel from bearing, since she was barren, lest she be proud against her sister.

Leah is a type of the Jewish people, to whom God gave many offspring, and from them came Levi, that is, the tribe of the priesthood, and also Judah, from whom Christ was born. As for Rachel, she is a type of the Gentiles, who were unable to bear spiritual children to God because of their distance from the faith, but Christ, of whom Jacob is a type, offered salvation to both, the Jews and the Gentiles, and afterward the Gentiles became fruitful in Christ after they believed.

Wonderful is God in His arrangements for the salvation of your soul: He supports you in tribulation and honors you so that you are not swallowed up by grief, and at the same time permits you tribulations if you are prone to pride or to dominating others, because He seeks the salvation of your soul by every means, so submit to Him and accept His will, for it is always for your good.
When Leah bore her firstborn son she rejoiced, since this would make Jacob love her, and she named him "Reuben," which means, behold, a son.
God gave Leah a second son because of her prayers before Him, and she called his name "Simeon," which means heard, because God heard her prayers to bear sons.
God gave Leah a third son and she rejoiced in him and called him "Levi," which means joined, because she said, With the birth of three sons Jacob will be joined to me and will not be distant from me.

God also blessed Leah with the birth of a fourth son, and she called him "Judah," which means praise, because she thanked God for the abundance of His gifts. Then she stopped bearing for a time, lest she too be proud against her sister.

How beautiful it is that you name your children with names that have spiritual meanings beneficial to them and to you, because a person's name is dear to him and he holds fast to it, so it is an opportunity that brings him near to God by its beautiful meaning.
Jacob's children and his wages

Rachel suffered because of her barrenness, and instead of taking refuge in God by prayer, she complained against her husband and demanded that he give her sons, and felt that her life without sons was like death and had no purpose. This shows the extent of her despair, because she had heard from Jacob of God's blessing on his offspring and saw that Leah with her children would obtain the whole blessing. Sadly, Rachel's absorption in the material inheritance appears here, and she did not perceive the spiritual inheritance and the importance of her attachment to Jacob in order to learn true faith from him.

May you accept God's arrangements for your life, because they lead to the salvation of your soul, and in proportion to your being spiritual you will understand God's purposes. Care for all that brings you near to God, because it remains forever, and do not be carried along with the current of the world, preoccupied with passing material things.
Jacob was angry at Rachel's complaining and directed her heart to prayer, because God alone is the giver of sons.
She shall bear upon my knees: that is, she will bear and give me sons whom I will carry on my knees.

Rachel did not benefit from the mistakes of her grandmother Sarah and repeated the same deed, asking her husband to lie with her maidservant, and the sons would be counted as Rachel's, as was the custom of that time. It would have been better for her to pray and wait for God to give to her if He willed, and if not, to thank Him and accept her condition and not depend on her human thoughts.
When Jacob lay with Bilhah she conceived and bore a son, and Rachel called him Dan, because she felt that God had judged for her and vindicated her, for Dan means judgment.

Bilhah bore a second son to Rachel and she called him Naphtali, that is, my wrestling, because she felt her wrestling and rivalry with her sister over bearing sons, for after her sister had borne four sons she was able to bear two through her maidservant. It is a bad thing that Rachel felt this struggle with her sister instead of love and friendliness, whereas the fruit, namely sons, is given by God.

Leah was influenced by the mistake of her sister Rachel and fell like her into the same mistake, giving her maidservant Zilpah to Jacob so that she might bear sons for her, because she had stopped bearing for some time. She bore her a son whom she called Gad, which means fortune, because she said that God had given to me with fortune, that is, made me happy by the birth of this son.
Then Zilpah bore a second son to Leah and she called him Asher, which means blessed, because she said that God had made me happy.
Do not rush to imitate those around you, for they may be mistaken even if they are the majority of those around you, but ask God first, and the Church, and they will guide you.

Mandrakes: the fruit of trees resembling the apple or the plum, which the common people call the jinn's apple, and they believe that it draws the husband to love his wife, and this is of course a belief with no basis of truth.

Reuben, the son of Leah, went out to the field and found a mandrake plant, and brought some of its fruit to his mother, who rejoiced in it, believing, like the people of her time, that it draws the husband to love his wife. But Rachel saw the mandrakes with Leah and asked her to give her some of them.

Leah was troubled by Rachel's request, because the struggle between them was great and the feelings of love between them had weakened, and because Jacob loved Rachel and was attached to her and neglected being with Leah after she had stopped bearing. So she said angrily to Rachel, Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband, and would you take my son's mandrakes also, so that Jacob may be more attached to you? Rachel said to Leah, Give me some of these mandrakes, and I will make Jacob lie with you tonight.

Do not let your relationship with those around you be material and utilitarian, but let your relationship with God be the basis of your relationship with them, confident that God blesses you from heaven as long as you trust in Him. Do not be troubled by the gains of others so as to be jealous of them and envy them, but ask God to give to you, and your soul will be calm and satisfied with His love and overflow with love to those around you.

Leah went out to meet Jacob when he returned from his work and told him what had happened with her sister and how she had taken the mandrakes in exchange for his coming to her. Jacob agreed and went in to lie with her, and Leah lifted up her prayers to God, and she conceived after having ceased bearing for a long time, and bore a son whom she called Issachar, which means he works for wages, because she said that God had given me my wages when I agreed to give my maidservant Zilpah to him. This is a hard thing for any wife, that her husband should lie with her maidservant, but she accepted this so that she might have more sons, so God granted her to bear again, and she bore Issachar.

Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son and called him Zebulun, that is, dwelling, because she said, Because I have borne six sons, now my husband will care for me and dwell with me, since he was bound more to Rachel and spent most of his time with her.

The Scripture mentions a daughter whom Leah bore and called Dinah, and the meaning of her name is judgment, being the feminine of the name Dan. Probably other daughters were born to Jacob, but it mentions Dinah because of an event in which Dinah will appear, namely her relationship with Shechem (ch. 34).

At the end of the fourteen years Rachel bore Joseph, and thus the difference in age between him and his firstborn brother Reuben was 13 years. Rachel's state of mind improved after she bore, and likewise Leah had become settled in mind after bearing six sons, so the struggle between them calmed. Jacob felt that he had worked 14 years for free for Laban, giving his labor during them as a dowry for his two daughters, so he asked to depart from him in order to begin work that would give him wages sufficient for his children and more, to provide for the needs of his large family, made up of two wives and two concubines and 11 sons, apart from the daughters. Jacob was longing to return to the land of Canaan, whose inheritance God had promised to him and his fathers.

Do not be preoccupied with the world and material things away from your goal, which is to be with God in the Church, where your true place is, but arrange your life so that its foundation is your relationship with God, and spend the rest in the works of the world and the needs of the body, so that your enjoyment of God may be continuous.
Jacob showed Laban how much he had toiled in tending his sheep and asked him to permit him to depart with his wives and children.
Laban said to Jacob, If I have found favor in your eyes, stay with me, because you have been a cause of blessing to me and my possessions have increased, and take whatever wages you see fit.
The Lord has blessed me for your sake: God gave you blessing because of me.

Jacob declared to Laban the extent of his toil in tending his sheep and how God had blessed him because of his service to him, so that the small flock that was with Rachel became very many flocks during the fourteen years. And he repeated to Laban that he needed to work and save for his large family.
Speckled: black in color with a few white spots.
Spotted: white in color with many black spots.

Jacob did not ask for a monetary reward for his work but asked to take some of the sheep, and specified them as the sheep whose color differed from the prevailing color among the sheep, which is white tending toward yellow. Some sheep are black or have black and white spots or have white stripes, and these strange colors, which are found rarely among the sheep, Jacob asked to be separated out and given to him.

Laban agreed to Jacob's request because it was a small wage, since the sheep of different color were few among the flocks, and he separated these sheep and gave them to his sons, who were the sons of Jacob, meaning his grandsons, or gave them to his sons to give them to Jacob. Because Laban's sheep were very many, he set a distance between his sheep and Jacob's sheep of a three days' journey, that is, about 40 miles. And Jacob continued to tend Laban's sheep in addition to his own sheep.
Rods: sticks of green plants.
Storax: a plant from which, if its outer bark is removed, a milk-white liquid flows, called balsam resin, and it is used in incense.
Hazel: the well-known plant that gives the fruit of the almond.
Chestnut: a plant found in the plains and on the banks of rivers.
Conceive: to crave while pregnant.
Troughs: the basins of water from which the sheep drink.

Many people in ancient times, and some even until now, believed in prenatal impression, which is that if a pregnant female, human or animal, sees something, the newborn comes out in the same form. This is of course a mistaken thought that Jacob believed, so he used rods from which he peeled parts so that they would be like his striped and spotted sheep, but God blessed this mistaken belief of his because he was wronged by his exploiting uncle Laban, so He blessed his flocks and they increased, as appears from the dream he saw in (ch. 31:12). Perhaps Jacob used a scientific method of breeding to increase his possessions: he brought green plant rods and peeled rings and spots on them so that they became spotted and striped, and from some of them even a milky liquid flowed, so the rods appeared mottled, resembling his mottled and striped sheep. He placed these rods in the places where the sheep drink at the mating season, so that when the white sheep look at these rods they become familiar with them and like them because they drink water beside them, which is essential for their life, and after they drink he puts before them his mottled and black sheep, so the white sheep mate with the mottled, and bear mottled sheep, that is, spotted and speckled. Thus the sheep belonging to Jacob increase, and Jacob separates them from among Laban's sheep and takes them for himself.

Jacob did another thing in breeding the sheep for his benefit, which is that at the mating season, if he found Laban's strong white sheep coming to drink, he placed the peeled rods at the water so they became familiar with them, and brought to them his mottled sheep so they mated with them. And if he found Laban's white sheep of the weak kind, he removed the peeled rods and let them mate with the rest of his white sheep. Thus the mottled sheep belonging to Jacob became strong and the white sheep belonging to Laban became weak.
By this Jacob's possessions increased and multiplied, and he bought many male and female servants. Jacob's return to Canaan

Laban's sons were troubled when they saw Jacob growing richer than their father, and they spoke with their father about this, so he too was troubled by Jacob and no longer treated him with love, and Jacob understood this.

Do not be troubled by the advancement of those around you and do not compare yourself with them, and if you see their advancement and want to be like them, ask God and wish them good, and God will give to you and to them.
God strengthened Jacob, who felt his estrangement among Laban and his sons and longed to return to the land of Canaan, by appearing to him and commanding him to return.

Jacob summoned his two wives, Leah and Rachel, to the field where he was working at shepherding, far from the eyes and ears of the servants, to speak with them about the decision to depart, and told them of the change in Laban's treatment of him because of God's blessing on his possessions, although he had served Laban with all his strength and great faithfulness for twenty years, including the fourteen years of the dowry and then six years working for wages with him. He mentioned to them how he had borne the bad treatment of their father, who changed his wages ten times during the six years in which he had fixed wages for him: sometimes he would say to him that your wages are the striped sheep, and when these striped sheep increased with him, he would return and say to him, from now on your wages are the black sheep ... and so on. Thus Laban wanted to take the best for himself, while on the contrary God was blessing Jacob in his sheep so they increased. By this blessing of God, God took away Laban's strength and wealth and gave it to Jacob.
Ringstraked: its skin is mottled like the skin of a leopard, with black and white spots.

Jacob informed his two wives of a divine dream he had seen: at the time of the mating of the sheep he saw the rams, striped, spotted and speckled, mounting the ewes to mate in order to produce mottled sheep, and God said to him, I am the one who blessed your work so that your wealth in sheep might increase. He reminded him of His promise to him, when He appeared to him on the ladder in the dream at Bethel, to bless him, when he poured oil on the stone, and then commanded him to leave Laban and return to Canaan, so Jacob was reassured by the blessing of God that was with him. This vision declares the blessing of God that was with Jacob, and perhaps it was He who guided him to place the rods in the watering troughs, and it answers everyone who accuses Jacob of trickery and deceit. For it was God who guided him to that in order to rescue him from Laban's greed in changing his wages and exploiting him in every way.

In proportion to the tribulations that pass over you, God reveals Himself to you and supports you, and the more you are submissive to Him, He directs you in all your steps, so you advance successfully however great the difficulties around you.

Leah and Rachel showed their distress at their father's greed, for he sold them in their marriage and received the price, which was Jacob's work of 14 years, and he did not give them many gifts as Bethuel, Laban's father, gave his daughter Rebekah at her marriage. Thus they lost all inheritance of their own from their father, and he counted them as strangers, and they felt that the wealth that God had transferred from Laban to Jacob was a recovery of their share taken away from their father's house. Thus they showed their support for Jacob and their readiness to depart with him and obey God's commands.

When you submit to God and walk with Him, He makes your way easy and makes those around you agree with you and submit to you, so you are not hindered in your spiritual growth and the carrying out of God's will.

God arranged that Laban should be busy shearing his sheep, and the days of shearing are days of joy because he gathers much money from the sale of the sheared wool, so Laban and all with him were busy with the shearing. Jacob seized this opportunity and gathered his wives, his children and his servants and mounted them, and likewise all his possessions, and set out with them and crossed the Euphrates River heading to the land of Canaan, that is, the land that God had promised to give him as an inheritance, where his father Isaac lived, and headed to the region of Gilead, which lies east of the Jordan River in Canaan.
Rachel did a strange and unexpected thing: she stole some of her father's idol images and departed with them with Jacob, and this was for one of the following reasons:
1- Either to exploit their material value in silver or gold, out of distress at her father's greed and his exploitation of them.

2- Or because of some attachment in her heart to the worship of idols, in which these images were used to seek counsel, protection and good omens, although she had lived in the faith with Jacob for many years.

Laban discovered after three days that Jacob had left the place, and he did not discover it at once because of his busyness with the shearing of the sheep, and he also noticed the theft of his images. So he gathered his brethren, meaning his relatives, and his sons and his mighty men, and pursued Jacob until he overtook him after seven days, that is, after a journey of about 100 miles, in Mount Gilead, which lies east of the Jordan River. When he saw Jacob and those with him from afar, Laban pitched his tents at the mountain.
Laban reached Jacob with strong men who could have taken away his children and possessions, but God, who protects Jacob, appeared to Laban and warned him against harming Jacob by any word or action.

Your God is strong and able to do all things, so do not be troubled if the wicked surround you and threaten you or wrong you, for He protects you and rescues you from their hands and troubles them, and even turns their wrongs to your spiritual benefit.
Each party saw the other's tents beside Mount Gilead, and Laban did not advance to harm Jacob after God's command to him.
Captives taken with the sword: the prisoners whom the enemy seizes in war.
The tabret: now called the riq, a wooden frame over which skin is stretched and to which cymbals are attached that make a strong sound when the skin is struck.
My sons: my grandchildren.

Laban reproached Jacob for his flight and for taking his daughters like captives fleeing in secret, and because he deprived him of bidding farewell to his daughters and grandchildren and kissing them, and did not give him the opportunity to hold a farewell celebration and a procession with songs and musical instruments.
Yesternight: the previous day.
Laban admitted that he had been determined to harm Jacob, relying on the strength of the men who were with him, but on the previous day God had appeared to him and warned him against harming Jacob.
Laban reproached Jacob because he had stolen his images and said to him, You longed to see your father, so why did you steal my gods?

Jacob justified his flight by his fear that Laban would take his daughters, that is, Jacob's wives, from him. As for the theft of the images, he denied it completely, because he did not know what Rachel had done, and therefore said, Search all my tents, and with whomever you find the images, let him be put to death, or become your slave, or not live a normal life because he sinned by this theft.
The camel's furniture: what is placed on the camel for a person to ride on, with large pockets in which belongings are put.

Laban went in to search the tents himself, and did not find them in any of the tents, not even Rachel's tent, because when he entered it she had put the images in the camel's furniture and sat on top of them, and excused herself to her father by her weariness from the pains of the monthly period that comes to women. He searched with his hand all through the tent and did not find them ... Thus the sin of stealing led Rachel to lying also, but God, for the sake of the wronged Jacob, covered her and did not reveal her sin.

Beware of being lax with sin, and if you sin, hasten to repentance, lest it lead you to other sins; on the contrary, care to acquire virtues, for just as the virtues are a chain in which each leads to the other, so also sins are a chain in which each leads to the other.
You have hotly pursued after me: you hastened after me impetuously to harm me.

Jacob reproached Laban for pursuing him to harm him and for this false accusation of theft, and even demanded that he bring the stolen things as evidence of the accusation and place them before his men who had come with him, to prove his accusation, otherwise let it be enough of wronging him.
He reminded him of his faithfulness in tending his sheep and keeping them for 20 years, so why did he wrong him and harm him despite this faithfulness, when he had not stolen from him a single sheep?

Of Jacob's faithfulness, and even his self-giving, was that he would make good to Laban any sheep that one of the wild beasts tore, although the owner of the sheep should have borne what was torn, but in order not to enter into dispute with the greedy Laban, he bore any loss that occurred, whether an animal tore it or a thief stole it.

Jacob bore the hardships of shepherding by day and by night, enduring the heat of the day and the cold of the night, which sometimes reaches the falling of rain and ice. And because of his care for the flocks he sometimes stayed up all night thinking how to manage and tend them.

Jacob reminded Laban how he had tried to exploit him throughout his service to him of twenty years and how he had changed his wages ten times in the last six years, the meaning being not the number ten but many times, and Jacob bore this and remained faithful in his service.

Jacob showed Laban's injustice and greed throughout his stay with him, and none rescued him and his possessions from his hands except God, who had promised Abraham and Isaac blessing, and out of respect for Isaac, the husband of his sister Rebekah, who was still alive. And the power of God appeared in warning and rebuking Laban against harming Jacob.
Be faithful in bearing your responsibilities and your service to God, whatever the faults of others, for He will keep you and protect you and bless your life.

Laban said to Jacob, Your wives and children are my children and your sheep also are dear to me because they are the offspring of my sheep, so we are united and all your possessions are dear to me, and therefore the natural situation is that neither of us should harm the other. Come, let us make a covenant of peace and a pact that neither of us will hurt the other all our lives.
Jegar-sahadutha: in Syriac, and its meaning is the heap of witness.
Galeed: in Hebrew, and its meaning is also the heap of witness.
Mizpah: its meaning is the watchtower.

Jacob agreed to Laban's word because he was a peaceable man, so he took a stone and set it up in the middle and asked the men who were with Laban to gather stones around this stone, and they made a heap, that is, a pile of stones, and then ate upon it to declare their love and reconciliation. They called it the heap of witness because it bears witness to the peace between them, and they also called it the watchtower because God watches over this covenant so that no one will violate it. The heap of witness is a type of the Cross, and the food that they ate is a type of the sacrament of Holy Communion.

Laban declared that this covenant meant keeping Jacob's wives, who were Laban's daughters, so that he would not marry other women and humiliate Leah and Rachel, and that neither party would move and pass beyond this heap to harm the other.

Laban swore by his gods and the God of Abraham, while Jacob called himself to witness by the fear and honor of his father Isaac, which he had received from God. This means that Laban was still worshiping idols and considered the God of Abraham one of the gods, while Isaac and Jacob worshiped God alone.
Jacob offered sacrifices to confirm the covenant and they ate together as proof of love, and then Laban and his men departed, returning to their country.

How beautiful is reconciliation between you and all people! Seek it however much others wrong you, that you may keep your peace and go on to your goal, which is the love of God, and be free for every positive work.
Jacob prepares to meet Esau

Jacob was thinking about meeting his brother Esau, and whether he would accept meeting him or refuse, or try to take revenge on him for what he had done to him 20 years before when he stole his blessing. Therefore God reassured him through his meeting with Laban, for God appeared and prevented Laban from harming him and a treaty of peace was made. And now He reassures him a second time after he set out toward his brother to meet him, for a company of angels appeared to him, as one appeared to him in the past when he fled from Esau in the dream of the ladder, to confirm to him that He had not forgotten His promise to keep him as long as he held fast to his faith.
Mahanaim: it lies east of the Jordan River at about its middle, between it and the Jabbok River, which branches off from about its middle toward the east and runs to the north.

When Jacob saw the angels he rejoiced greatly and said, This is God's host, and his heart was reassured, and he called the name of the place where they appeared to him Mahanaim, that is, two camps, meaning the camp or host of the angels in heaven and God's camp on earth, which is Jacob and his family. For the Church consists of a part in heaven and a part still striving on earth.

God cares for your feelings as long as you seek Him and want to live with Him, and He moves toward you and shows you His love in many forms to reassure you, so enjoy Him and thank Him, and move on your way in life leaning on His hand.
The land of Seir: Seir means hairy, and the land of Seir is a mountain range that extends from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Dead Sea.

Edom: the meaning is red, and what is meant by it is the offspring of Esau, which lives in the land of Seir, which had belonged to the Horites, and the offspring of Esau took possession of it from them.

Despite God's reassurance to Jacob, there was still within him a fear of Esau's revenge on him, so he sent messengers from his servants to Esau to learn his feelings toward him, and the messengers went south along the Jordan River and the Dead Sea until they reached the mountains of Seir. In this he depended on his human thinking and did not consult God.

If there is anxiety or fear within you, take refuge in God many times, and do not rush in your anxiety to take decisions that you think will protect you but that in truth increase your anxiety and may harm you. Seek God, for He is near you and will guide you to your good.

Jacob gave his messengers a message to Esau, full of humility and fear and also carrying meanings of love, and told him in it that he had lived abroad 20 years with his uncle Laban and God had blessed him with many servants and cattle, and he was returning to Canaan and hoped to find grace and acceptance in his eyes. His humility appears from his calling him my lord, although they were brothers, indeed Jacob had received from God authority over his brother as a blessing from Isaac.
The messengers informed Esau of this message, and they found him very rich, and when he heard it he went out with 400 men of his servants to meet Jacob. This means one of two things:
1- Either joy and welcome at meeting his brother.
2- Or preparation for revenge because of his being deprived of his father's blessing.

Esau had decided to take revenge on his brother, but after the death of their father ... so is he still insisting on revenge? ... And will he take revenge now or postpone it until after Isaac's death? ... Or has he calmed down and forgotten what happened after God blessed him with many offspring and servants? We cannot know, and perhaps feelings of longing for his brother were mixed with feelings of revenge and distress; in any case, the hope is in God's intervention to reconcile the two brothers.

When Jacob heard from his messengers the news of Esau's coming out with his many men to meet him, he was very afraid, remembering the decision of revenge that Esau had declared 20 years before ... Thus Jacob did not benefit from relying on his own thinking and sending messengers, but his fear increased, so he divided those who were with him into two companies and separated them, so that if Esau attacked one company the other would find an opportunity to flee.

After Jacob's human attempts failed, he took refuge in God. The text of his prayer is mentioned here, and it is the first prayer in the Holy Bible whose text is given, and it includes many meanings, the most important of which are:
1- His sense of sonship to God and his special relationship with Him, since he calls Him the God of his fathers, and this makes him speak with boldness and confidence.
2- He declares his submission to God's commands, who commanded him to return from Haran to Canaan, and by this he affirms his allegiance to God and his taking refuge in Him.
3- He declares in humility his unworthiness of the kindness and blessings of God that He had given him ... Thus boldness and confidence in God are mingled with deep humility.

4- He thanks God and declares that He is the source of all the favor and blessing upon him, because when he fled from Esau and crossed the Jordan River on his way to Haran he possessed nothing at all. And after his return from Haran to Canaan God blessed him, so he became two hosts, that is, two companies, including his wives, children, servants and possessions, so in himself he is nothing, but God's blessing made him very great.
The mother with the children: he means his wives and children.
5- He asked God to rescue him from the hand of his brother Esau, who was coming to take revenge on him, because if God did not intervene he would kill all who were with him, the great and the small.
6- He reminded God of His promises to him of blessing and many offspring. And God rejoices in His children who hold fast to His promises and remind Him of them, that is, ask Him to care for them.

Show your feelings to God in love and humility and ask of Him what you want, for He is your heavenly Father who loves you and rejoices in your words and supports you whatever your weakness, indeed your few words are very precious to Him.

Jacob rested part of the night and thought during it of sending gifts to his brother Esau, to soften his heart toward him and establish friendly relations with him that would make him forget feelings of distress and revenge.

Do not be troubled by feelings of evil if they surround you, and know that love is stronger than hatred, so pray for those who oppose you and offer them love in kind words or gifts or services, even if they do not welcome it at first, but they are gradually affected by it, so you remove the evil from their hearts and keep your peace and win the hearts of many. This is not weakness, but it is true strength, to change people's hearts from evil to good, and do not care about what they say about you at first, that you are weak or that they think of exploiting you, for you are the stronger by your love and you please God, who supports you and subdues them to you and blesses your life.
She-camel: the female of the camel.
He-goat: the male of the goat.
She-ass: the female of the donkey.
Ewe: the female of the sheep.
She-goat: the female of the goat.
Ram: the male of the sheep.
The details of the gift sent to Esau are mentioned, a group of herds of cattle numbering 580 head, which is a great gift and means two things:
1- Jacob's great wealth.
2- His great love and his fear of Esau and his attempt to appease him.
A space: a sufficient distance.

He divided the gift into a group of gifts, giving each drove to some of his servants, probably dividing it into five droves, and put a sufficient distance between each drove and the next so that it would clearly appear that they were five gifts, so they would gradually affect Esau's heart and absorb all the anger within him.

He charged his servants who led the droves that when each of them met Esau and he asked him who he was and what was with him, he should say to him, It is a present sent from your servant Jacob. And he said within himself, By this I will appease him and gain his favor before I meet him.
Jacob sent his gift ahead of him to Esau, while he himself lodged or rested part of the night in the place where he had pitched his tent.
Ford: a part of the river of little depth that can be crossed on foot, and the width of the river is small in this region.

Jabbok: one of the tributaries of the Jordan River, branching off from about its middle, as we mentioned, at a distance of 23 miles north of the Dead Sea, and the meaning of its name is the flowing, and it is now called the Zarqa.

The gift crossed with his servants to Esau, then the rest of his servants with all his possessions crossed the Jabbok River heading south toward the Dead Sea, and only his wives and children remained with Jacob, so he crossed with them the Jabbok River on foot, heading south as a caravan before him, while he himself remained alone for the rest of the night.
The hollow of his thigh: the place where the thigh joins the body.

After the caravan of his wives and children had gone some distance on their way to meet Esau, and this was during the night, Jacob remained alone and stood praying, asking God's help in his meeting with Esau, that He would turn away his anger and that he would not take revenge on him. While he was praying, God wished to reassure him, so He appeared to him in the form of an angel or sent him an angel in human form, and Jacob felt that he was a heavenly being, so he hastened to hold him and ask his help. The angel pretended that he wanted to depart from him, but Jacob clung to him asking his blessing because he felt that he was sent from God. Jacob continued to implore him, clinging to him, through the rest of the night until the dawn rose, and the angel pretended weakness before Jacob as if unable to free himself from his clinging, in order to encourage him as he continued to ask his blessing and help, and Jacob even says to him, "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me," for I am in great need before the power of Esau who is coming against me. In the end the angel not only blessed him but struck him, that is, touched him, on the hollow of his thigh, so the thigh was partly dislocated from the body, and Jacob suffered pain but continued to hold the angel, asking his help. This shows how much Jacob clung to God and his sense of his weakness and need.

Strive in your prayers with God and ask Him for all you want. Be persistent with Him, declaring your need with the boldness of sons, for He rejoices in your faith and your clinging to Him, and when He sees the extent of your striving He will surely give you many blessings. Do not doubt or despair, and hold fast to God.

The angel changed Jacob's name to Israel, which means he wrestles with God, in honor of Jacob because of his spiritual striving in prayer and his faith and reliance on Him, and on the other hand because of his bearing with others such as Laban until God blessed him and enriched him and sent him away from him in peace. By this he is an example for all his offspring in holding fast to God and in good dealing with others, because his offspring were called by this name, that is, the children of Israel.

Jacob asked the angel, or the spiritual person who appeared to him, about his name, and he did not answer him, because he had understood that he was a spiritual being from heaven, and he gave him what he needed, which was the blessing, and then ascended from him.
Peniel or Penuel: the meaning is the face of God.
Jacob rejoiced with an inexpressible joy because he had seen God and felt His presence through his meeting with the angel, so he called the name of the place Peniel.

In the morning, when the sun rose, Jacob was reassured and moved south to catch up with his wives and children, and he was suffering from the angel's blow, so he limped in his walking. God permitted him this pain throughout his life so that he would not be proud because of his vision and his wrestling with God, but would always feel his weakness and need, and so continue to enjoy God's work with him. And the offspring of Jacob magnified this great event in the life of their father, so they did not eat the sinew of the thigh, which is the nerve extending along the leg, in esteem and reverence for this great event, that is, Jacob's meeting with God, which resulted in the pain apparent in his walking.
The meeting with Esau and settling in Canaan

As Jacob was walking with his wives and children, he saw Esau coming from afar with his four hundred men. He feared their great number, despite God's appearing to him and blessing him. So he divided those with him into three groups: the two maidservants, Bilhah and Zilpah, with their children in front, followed by Leah and her children, then the third group, which was Rachel and her son Joseph. As for himself, he went ahead of them all and bowed himself to the ground seven times as he drew near to Esau. This shows Jacob's feelings, which were:

1- His love for Rachel, so he placed her at the end of the procession, so that if Esau attacked she would have a chance to escape, with Leah before her, to have a middle chance of escape, while the two maidservants were in front.
2- He went ahead of them all, sacrificing himself, so that if Esau attacked he would be the first to die. In this he is a type of Christ the Redeemer, who dies for His Church.

3- He bowed seven times, a complete number that signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in the believing person. This shows how humble Jacob was in abasing himself before Esau, and his respect and honor for him.

God worked in Esau's heart when he saw Jacob. Perhaps it reminded him of the days of their boyhood, their love, their play and their being together, and made him forget the cause of his anger, which was the stealing of his blessing. So his heart yearned toward his brother Jacob, and he ran quickly to meet him, embraced him and kissed him. Both were moved by this meeting of love after twenty years, and their tears flowed.

When Esau saw the women and children who were with Jacob, he asked him about them. Jacob told him that they were his wives and his children whom God had graciously given him. Then he presented each wife with her children, and they bowed before Esau. This shows the following:
1- Jacob's sense that God alone is the source of all his blessings.
2- That he took care to teach the members of his household humility in dealing with others, and respect for them.

Esau also asked his brother Jacob about the droves of flocks that had reached him before he saw him, and he called them an army because they were so many. Jacob answered that it was a small gift he presented to him so that he might be pleased with him. Esau said that he had many possessions, trying to return the gift to Jacob, who urged him to take it, and in the end he accepted.

After Esau had shown feelings of love in kissing and embracing his brother, and then in trying to return the gift to him, we find him offering his love again in proposing to accompany him to Canaan, where he lived, with Esau going ahead as his guide until he brought him to the place where he would settle. But Jacob excused himself, because he had small children with him, besides newly born animals; if he went quickly with all this company, they might not endure it and might faint on the way. So he asked leave for Esau to go ahead, and Jacob and those with him would come on slowly.

Esau's love appears for the fourth time in his offer to Jacob to leave with him some of his men to guide him on the way and guard him. But Jacob thanked him for this and declared his joy at the grace he had found in Esau's eyes, and assured him that he could go on by himself with those who were with him. So they bade each other farewell, and Esau went back to his place in Seir.

God is able to change the hearts of those who are hostile to you, so that they love you and are at peace with you, and even show concern for you. So be reassured, for you are not alone, and God is able to give you favor in the eyes of all. Seek Him and repeat His name, and you will feel His presence with you and rejoice in Him.

entries.section: (2) Jacob's settling in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Succoth: it means booths. There is a city of this name about a mile east of the Jordan, and another of the same name west of the Jordan, besides the one near Rameses in Egypt (Ex 12:37). Jacob went on his way southward and came to a place where he made booths for his cattle, so he called the name of the place Succoth, because he made booths there.

entries.section: (2) Jacob's settling in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Shechem: a city lying west of the Jordan River between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, and now called Nablus.
Jacob journeyed until he came near a city called Shechem in the land of Canaan.

entries.section: (2) Jacob's settling in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: Kesitah: a metal coin stamped with the figure of a lamb, and of great value.

Jacob bought a parcel of ground near the city of Shechem, paying its price, which was a hundred pieces of money (kesitah), and pitched his tents and booths there. In this parcel the children of Israel buried the bones of Joseph when they came out of Egypt (Josh 24:32), and afterward they moved them to the cave of Machpelah.

entries.section: (2) Jacob's settling in the land of Canaan

paragraphs.text: The most important thing Jacob did after settling in Canaan was that he built an altar and offered sacrifices to God in the midst of the idolaters who were spread around him.

Thank God after every work you complete or every place you reach, to declare to yourself that your leader and the ruler of your life is God. Do not be preoccupied with the conduct of those around you, in their distance from God and their preoccupation with the world, for your distinction and your strength lie in God's being with you, so you enjoy His blessings and rejoice in His presence within you.
Dinah and Shechem

After Jacob settled near the city of Shechem, his daughter Dinah went out to get to know the daughters of the pagan tribe living near them, out of curiosity to learn their customs and to mix with them, though she knew they were wicked and far from God.
Humbled her: raped her.

Shechem: the prince of the tribe in this city, son of Hamor, the chief of the tribe, which was one of the Hivite tribes. Shechem saw Dinah walking in the city and was taken with her beauty. He spoke with her and was able to lure her until he lay with her and raped her.

Control your curiosity to know the news of evil and the events of the world, which can make you stumble. Do not give yourself over to the media without restraint, lest you expose yourself to falling into sin, and Satan humbles you and robs you of your purity, trying to lead you away from God.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: Shechem continued in his love for Dinah, with whom he had committed fornication; indeed his heart clung to her and he wanted to marry her, so he asked his father to get her for him as a wife.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: Jacob learned what had happened to his daughter. Perhaps she remained with Shechem after he raped her, until Hamor came, on the same day or after it, to ask her father for her hand; or perhaps she kept going out to meet him for several days and then stayed with him, and then Hamor came to seek her for his son from her father. In any case, Jacob was greatly grieved, and from the horror of the calamity he kept silent and waited until his sons came from their work tending the flock, so that he might consult with them.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: Hamor decided to seek Dinah for his son Shechem, so he took him with him and visited Jacob and asked him for Dinah to be Shechem's wife.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: During the visit of Hamor and Shechem to Jacob to seek Dinah's hand, Jacob's sons arrived after finishing their work in the pasture, and they heard and learned the whole story. They were very angry at Shechem's rape of their sister Dinah, and at how such a vile thing had happened in the family of their father Israel, which was distinguished by purity, righteousness and a clean life with God. This matter was not merely unseemly but a great calamity that no one had expected.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: Hamor tried to resolve the problem and ease her brothers' anger by proposing that this marriage be the beginning of good relations between the family of Israel and their tribe, so that they would unite in one life, trade together, and have one land between them. For Israel was a stranger in the land, and he would regard this treaty and intermarriage as a kind of security for him.

entries.section: (2) Hamor asks for Dinah as a wife for Shechem

paragraphs.text: Shechem the son of Hamor made another offer showing his love for Dinah and his attachment to her. He asked Jacob and his sons to set the dowry, that is, what is paid to the bride, and the gift presented to her family, as they saw fit; indeed they should multiply it and ask for the greatest dowry and gift, and he and his father were ready to meet their demands.

Do not be hasty in your actions, lest you fall into sins that cannot be resolved and wrong others, so that they do not forgive you however much you try to settle it. Control your tongue and your actions, pray before you undertake anything, and always keep the fear of God before your eyes, so that you do not sin against Him or wrong anyone.

entries.section: (3) The deceitful speech of Jacob's sons

paragraphs.text: In their distress over what had happened, Jacob's sons thought of a deception in order to take revenge on the tribe of Shechem and not on Shechem alone.

entries.section: (3) The deceitful speech of Jacob's sons

paragraphs.text: Jacob's sons pretended to agree to Dinah's marriage to Shechem, but they told Hamor and his son that it was their custom that every male be circumcised, and that they could not intermarry with any foreign tribe unless all its males were circumcised. So if they wanted Dinah to marry Shechem, all the males of their tribe must be circumcised.

entries.section: (3) The deceitful speech of Jacob's sons

paragraphs.text: Then they said to Hamor and his son that if they would not consent to be circumcised, they would take Dinah and go to their tents. This shows that Dinah had remained with Shechem after he raped her, whether on the same day or some days later.

Here it appears that Jacob's sons, led by Simeon and Levi, used religion as a deception to reach their evil ends. This is a very wrong thing, that is, to pretend to be religious in order to accomplish evil.

Know that your spiritual practices are a private matter between you and God; indeed Christ commands you to keep them in secret. So do not try to display these practices before people, or to use them for any personal ends in your dealings with all those around you, or to hide some of your sins.

entries.section: (4) Hamor and Shechem's speech to the men of their city

paragraphs.text: Shechem and his father agreed to the condition Jacob's sons asked, which was the circumcision of every male, and they left their presence to carry out the matter. Shechem was like a prince in his tribe and held a great position, and therefore what he and his father said had an influence on the whole tribe.

entries.section: (4) Hamor and Shechem's speech to the men of their city

paragraphs.text: The gate of their city: the square where the people gather.

Hamor and his son Shechem stood at the entrance of their city and spoke to the crowds of the people. They told them that Jacob and his clan were peaceable people, and that they could ally themselves with them and intermarry with them and share life with them, but there was one condition: that all the males be circumcised, so that they might all live as one family. One of the benefits of this intermarriage between the two tribes was that the others' possessions would become theirs, that is, the possessions of the tribe of Shechem, since they would become one great people with many possessions. All this was to encourage them to accept the matter.

entries.section: (4) Hamor and Shechem's speech to the men of their city

paragraphs.text: All who went out of the gate of his city: all the working men of the city who go out to their work.

Because of the standing of Hamor and Shechem among the people, and because the offer was beneficial and convincing, the people of the city agreed to circumcision in order to intermarry with the family of Israel, and they were circumcised.

Present your words to others in a convincing way so that they accept them, and care for their feelings and opinions; for in proportion as you respect people's opinions they respect yours and understand you, and even love your company and companionship.

entries.section: (5) The killing of the men of Shechem's tribe

paragraphs.text: Unawares: no one resisted them.

Simeon and Levi led a band made up of their servants and attacked the city of Shechem and killed all its men, including Shechem and Hamor. No one resisted them because of the pain of their circumcision, for they attacked on the third day after being circumcised. And they took their sister Dinah, who was in Shechem's house.

entries.section: (5) The killing of the men of Shechem's tribe

paragraphs.text: The rest of Jacob's sons also attacked the city of Shechem after the men were killed, and joined the killers in plundering their spoil and taking captive their women and children to be servants and slaves for them. Thus they brought this tribe to an end.

entries.section: (5) The killing of the men of Shechem's tribe

paragraphs.text: Jacob was greatly distressed at what had happened, because it was an unjust revenge. Instead of refusing the marriage or punishing Shechem with some penalty, they killed innocent men, took captive their women and children, and plundered their spoil. This was a terrible injustice. On the other hand, he feared that the neighboring tribes, when they heard what had happened, would rise against him and kill him, especially since his clan was few in number compared with the large tribes around them.

entries.section: (5) The killing of the men of Shechem's tribe

paragraphs.text: Simeon and Levi justified their crime by saying that they could not keep silent over the rape of their sister Dinah and her being treated as a harlot.

Do not be rash in your anger and make unwise decisions, but wait, think and pray first, that God may guide you and you may do His will; then you will not regret it because of God's anger against you and the anger of people as well.
Jacob at Bethel

Jacob was troubled after his sons killed the tribe of Shechem, so God intervened to rescue him and restore his peace. He commanded him to move to Bethel, where God had appeared to him at the ladder when he was fleeing from Esau (ch. 28:10-22). This was the place where he vowed that God would have a house and he would worship Him. He had not gone there immediately after coming from Padan-aram, from his uncle Laban, and perhaps this was by divine arrangement so that he might dwell in different places in the land of Canaan, for God to prove to him that all the land of Canaan would be his and his offspring's.
Jacob prepared to depart for Bethel in obedience to God's commands, and told those with him to prepare in two ways:
