Jacob finally died at the age of 147 years, and although he died in a foreign land, his spirit was gathered to his people, that is, his believing fathers, who were awaiting in hope the redemption of Christ and His resurrection, that they might be raised up to Paradise.

Look to the end of your life, which is death, so that you do not accept sin or become careless with it. And your remembrance of death every morning lifts you to heavenly readiness, so that you walk in all that pleases God and give love to everyone you meet.
We observe that Jacob is a type of Christ in the following:
1- The Holy Bible testified of Jacob that he was a perfect man (ch. 25:27), and Christ was perfect and said, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:26).

2- Jacob lived as a stranger, dwelling in tents, and was a stranger with his uncle and then in Egypt, and he described his life as the days of his pilgrimage; and Christ lived detached from the world throughout His life.
3- Jacob received the birthright and the blessing, and Christ is the firstborn among many brethren and is the hypostasis of wisdom and blessing.
4- Jacob was exploited by his uncle Laban, but God rescued him from his hands; and the Jews wronged Christ, persecuted Him and crucified Him, but God raised Him, that is, He rose by His divinity.

5- Jacob was deceived by his sons in the killing of the tribe of Shechem and in the selling of Joseph; and Christ was wounded by His beloved ones, and all those close to Him abandoned Him at the cross.
Here we present a summary of the life of Jacob, which is:
1- Jacob the unborn child in his mother's womb (ch. 25).
2- Jacob buys the birthright from Esau (ch. 25).
3- Jacob seizes his father's blessing (ch. 27).
4- Jacob's dream and the ladder (ch. 28).
5- Jacob marries, begets sons and works for his uncle (chs. 29, 30).
6- God delivers Jacob from the pursuit of his uncle Laban (ch. 31).
7- Jacob's wrestling with the angel (ch. 32).
8- Jacob's meeting and reconciliation with Esau (ch. 33).
9- Shechem's assault on Dinah, Jacob's daughter, and her brothers' vengeance upon them (ch. 34).
10- Jacob's journey to Bethel (ch. 35).
11- Jacob and his beloved son Joseph (chs. 37-48).
12- Jacob's blessings to his sons and his death. (ch. 49) The burial of Jacob and the death of Joseph

Joseph grieved and was deeply moved by his father's death. He embraced him, kissed him and closed his eyes, so that God's promise to Jacob would be fulfilled, that Joseph would be beside him until his death, would care for his body and close his eyes (ch. 4:46).

Since Joseph was the ruler of Egypt, all the people were his servants, for they had sold themselves to Pharaoh in order that he might give them food. So Joseph commanded the physicians who specialized in embalming to embalm his father. Egypt was famous for its excellence in medicine and in embalming, so they embalmed him over 40 days according to the procedures and stages of embalming, and the mourning for him continued for 70 days, as was the custom of the great men in Egypt.

Because Joseph was wearing mourning garments and had let his beard grow, he could not meet Pharaoh, since meeting kings at that time required certain signs of joy. So he spoke to Pharaoh's counselors and those close to him to ask Pharaoh's permission to bury his father in the land of Canaan as he had commanded, and Pharaoh agreed. It is noticeable that Jacob was careful to charge Joseph and his other sons to bury him in Canaan, and that Joseph kept to this, for the following reasons:
1- His faith, like that of his fathers, in the resurrection of the body, so he was careful to be buried in a holy place in order to teach his children this faith.

2- He felt his estrangement from the world and his detachment from the good things of Egypt, and he wanted his descendants to know this so that they would return to Canaan, which God had promised and which is a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven. Therefore he was careful to be buried there and not in Egypt.
3- He charged that he be buried with his fathers to declare before his children his adherence to the faith of his fathers, and not to the idolatry that was spread throughout the whole world.

Take care to teach your children and everyone around you life with God and holding fast to the faith in a practical way, through your conduct and your words, so that they see living faith in you and it becomes easy for them to follow your example.

Joseph took the embalmed body of his father and went up with it from Egypt to Canaan, because the land of Canaan is geographically higher than Egypt and the Nile valley. His brothers and their grown children went out with him, but they left their little ones and their flocks behind. Joseph was also accompanied by the great men of Egypt, namely the royal court and the elders of Egypt. Chariots and horsemen went with them, as was the custom of great men when moving from place to place, so the number traveling was very large, like an army.
The threshingfloor of Atad: the threshing floor is the area in which grain is threshed, and it is called the granary. Beyond Jordan: the valley adjoining the Jordan River.

The procession reached Canaan at a place called the threshingfloor of Atad, beside the Jordan River, and there they made another mourning for seven days in honor of Jacob, as was the custom of that time.
Abelmizraim: a mourning of the Egyptians.

When the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, saw this great mourning, they said that it must be a mourning of the Egyptians, who were known for their care in burying their dead and weeping for them.
After that they moved on to the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to the tribe of the sons of Heth, and buried Jacob there as he had commanded.

Take care to obey the commandments of your parents, not only during their lifetime but also after their departure, for they are divine guidance on their lips, so that you walk well as a child of God and advance on the road to the Kingdom of Heaven.
After the burial of Jacob, Joseph returned to Egypt with the whole procession that was with him.
Joseph's brothers thought that he might have honored them for the sake of his father, but that he might take vengeance on them after his death for their evils toward him.
They sent a messenger unto Joseph: they sent him a message with one of those close to him.

Fearing Joseph's vengeance, they sent to him, pleading with him not to take vengeance on them, saying that their father, to whom they had spoken words like these, had commanded them to apologize to him again after his death in order to confirm his forgiveness of them. Here they use the name of their father and his command so that Joseph would have compassion on them and forgive them, because he loved his father. So he allowed them to meet him and they offered him this apology. Joseph was moved and wept before them, because he had forgiven them and loved them and could not take vengeance on them.
Let your forgiveness be complete: do not remember the sins and offenses of others, nor wrong them, even after a while, just as God forgives you completely and honors you, whatever your sins may be.

Joseph's brothers were moved by his great love and his weeping, so they drew near to him and bowed down before him, thanking him for his forgiveness and declaring their servitude to him. Thus the dreams of Joseph, which God had promised from his youth, were fulfilled.

Joseph reassured them that he was not the judge or the avenger, for that belongs to God; as for him, he was their brother who loved them, and what was required of them was to continue in their repentance before God and in carefulness, and not to anger Him by any sin.

He explained to them that God had turned their evil toward him into good: they sold him out of envy and vengeance, but God turned it into a means of saving them from the famine and preserving offspring for him.

Do not be troubled by people's offenses, for God turns them to your good, to your spiritual growth, to your drawing near to God and to your deliverance from many sins. This helps you to forgive them, because despite their evil they were the means of your exaltation and spiritual growth.
Joseph added not only that he had forgiven them, but he promised to honor them and to provide for them and their children in Egypt.

Joseph lived until he reached the age of 110 years; that is, he sat on the throne of Egypt and its rule for 80 years, because he assumed its rule at the age of thirty, and he saw his children's grandchildren. That is, he lived a long life and enjoyed seeing his righteous offspring.

Before Joseph died, he gathered his brothers and their children and charged them to take his bones with them when God brought them up out of the land of Egypt and they returned to Canaan as God had promised them. For Pharaoh would not allow his brothers to carry him to Canaan at his death, and he would then have to be buried in Egypt; therefore he charged them to take his bones. This declares his estrangement from the world, despite his great position, and the attachment of his heart to God's promises. The children of Israel did as Joseph had charged: they took his bones when they went out under Moses (Ex 13:19), and he was buried in Shechem by Joshua (Josh 24:32), and afterward he was moved to the cave of Machpelah.

Do not let the concerns of the world, its pleasures and its positions distract you from your one goal, which is the Kingdom of Heaven; rather, let no day pass over you without enjoying prayer and reading the Holy Bible, so that you live for your true goal.

After Joseph's death they embalmed him like the great men and placed him in a coffin, as was the custom of the Egyptians, who made it of wood or stone to preserve the body, since they too believed in the other life.
Here we summarize the life of Joseph in the following points:
1- Joseph the beloved son in his father's house (ch. 37).
2- His brothers sell him as a slave (ch. 37).
3- Joseph's rule over the house of Potiphar and the attempt of Potiphar's wife to make him fall into sin (ch. 39)
4- Joseph the prisoner (ch. 40).
5- Joseph interprets dreams and rises to the throne of Egypt (ch. 41).
6- Joseph's meeting with his brothers and their accusation of spying (ch. 42).
7- The second meeting with his brothers and their accusation of stealing the cup (chs. 43, 44).
8- Joseph reveals himself to his brothers (ch. 45).
9- Joseph receives his father in Egypt (ch. 46).
10- Joseph presents his father to Pharaoh (ch. 47).
11- Jacob blesses Joseph and his two sons (ch. 48).
12- Jacob's charges and blessings to Joseph and his brothers (ch. 49).
13- The death of Joseph and his burial (ch. 50).
Joseph was a type of Christ, as appears from the following:
1- Joseph was his father's beloved son, and Christ is the only and beloved Son of His Father (Mt 3:17).

2- Joseph obeyed his father in visiting his brothers and took food with him to satisfy them and to ask about their welfare; and Christ obeyed the Father in His incarnation and redemption to visit humanity (Phil 2:8), and He fed the multitudes and healed the sick...
3- Joseph loved his brothers but they hated him, and so the Jewish nation hated Christ: "He came unto his own, and his own received him not" (Jn 1:11).
4- Joseph's brothers cast their brother into the pit and then brought him up alive; and Christ was buried in the tomb and then rose alive.
5- Joseph's brothers stripped their brother of his coat and dipped it in blood; and they stripped Christ and clothed Him in a purple robe, and His blood flowed on the cross (ch. 37:31, Mt 27:27-35).
6- Joseph's brothers sold their brother as a slave, and Judas Iscariot, the disciple of Christ, also sold Him for the price of a slave (ch. 37:36, Mt 26:14, 15).
7- Joseph was tempted by Potiphar's wife and overcame lust, and Christ was tempted by the devil and overcame him (ch. 39, Mt 4).
8- Potiphar's wife accused Joseph falsely, and the Jews accused Christ with false and untrue charges (ch. 39, Mk 14:56-59, Lk 23-2).
9- Joseph was cast into prison unjustly, and Christ was crucified and laid in the tomb unjustly.

10- Joseph was imprisoned with two men, one of whom escaped death, the cupbearer, while the baker perished; and Christ was crucified with two robbers, one of whom escaped and entered Paradise, while the other perished.
11- Joseph came out of prison and rose to the throne of Egypt, and Christ rose from the dead and ascended to His throne in heaven by His ascension.
12- Joseph took the name Zaphnath-paaneah, meaning the sustenance of life, and Christ is the food of life by His most holy Body and Blood.
13- All the Egyptians bowed down before Joseph, and also his father and his brothers, and to Christ every knee bows (Phil 2:10).
14- Joseph by his wisdom governed Egypt and provided for it, and Christ is the hypostasis of wisdom who governs the life of the whole world.
15- Joseph was not ashamed of his father and his shepherd brothers, and Christ is not ashamed to call us, sinful human beings, His brethren (Heb 2:11).
16- Joseph forgave his brothers who had wronged him, and Christ forgives the sins of everyone who disobeys Him and then repents.
